options.title: appstream.enable
options.description:
Whether to install files to support the
[AppStream metadata specification](https://www.freedesktop.org/software/appstream/docs/index.html).

options.title: boot.bcache.enable
options.description: Whether to enable bcache mount support.

options.title: boot.bcachefs.package
options.description:
The bcachefs-tools package to use. This package should also provide a passthru 'kernelModule'
attribute to build the out-of-tree kernel module.

options.title: boot.binfmt.addEmulatedSystemsToNixSandbox
options.description:
Whether to add the {option}`boot.binfmt.emulatedSystems` to {option}`nix.settings.extra-platforms`.
Disable this to use remote builders for those platforms, while allowing testing binaries locally.

options.title: boot.binfmt.emulatedSystems
options.description:
List of systems to emulate. Will also configure Nix to
support your new systems.
Warning: the builder can execute all emulated systems within the same build, which introduces impurities in the case of cross compilation.

options.title: boot.binfmt.preferStaticEmulators
options.description:
Whether to use static emulators when available.

This enables the kernel to preload the emulator binaries when
the binfmt registrations are added, obviating the need to make
the emulator binaries available inside chroots and chroot-like
sandboxes.

options.title: boot.binfmt.registrations
options.description:
Extra binary formats to register with the kernel.
See <https://www.kernel.org/doc/html/latest/admin-guide/binfmt-misc.html> for more details.

options.title: boot.binfmt.registrations.<name>.fixBinary
options.description:
Whether to open the interpreter file as soon as the
registration is loaded, rather than waiting for a
relevant file to be invoked.

See the description of the 'F' flag in the kernel docs
for more details.

options.title: boot.binfmt.registrations.<name>.interpreter
options.description:
The interpreter to invoke to run the program.

Note that the actual registration will point to
/run/binfmt/${name}, so the kernel interpreter length
limit doesn't apply.

options.title: boot.binfmt.registrations.<name>.magicOrExtension
options.description: The magic number or extension to match on.

options.title: boot.binfmt.registrations.<name>.mask
options.description: A mask to be ANDed with the byte sequence of the file before matching

options.title: boot.binfmt.registrations.<name>.matchCredentials
options.description:
Whether to launch with the credentials and security
token of the binary, not the interpreter (e.g. setuid
bit).

See the description of the 'C' flag in the kernel docs
for more details.

Implies/requires openBinary = true.

options.title: boot.binfmt.registrations.<name>.offset
options.description: The byte offset of the magic number used for recognition.

options.title: boot.binfmt.registrations.<name>.openBinary
options.description:
Whether to pass the binary to the interpreter as an open
file descriptor, instead of a path.

options.title: boot.binfmt.registrations.<name>.preserveArgvZero
boot.binfmt.registrations.<name>.recognitionType
options.description: Whether to recognize executables by magic number or extension.

options.title: boot.binfmt.registrations.<name>.wrapInterpreterInShell
options.description:
Whether to wrap the interpreter in a shell script.

This allows a shell command to be set as the interpreter.

options.title: boot.blacklistedKernelModules
options.type: (attribute set of boolean) or (list of string) convertible to it
options.description:
Set of names of kernel modules that should not be loaded
automatically by the hardware probing code. This can either be
a list of modules or an attrset. In an attrset, names that are
set to `true` represent modules that will be blacklisted.

options.title: boot.bootspec.enableValidation
options.description:
Whether to enable the validation of bootspec documents for each build.
      This will introduce Go in the build-time closure as we are relying on [Cuelang](https://cuelang.org/) for schema validation.
      Enable this option if you want to ascertain that your documents are correct
.

options.title: boot.bootspec.extensions
options.description:
User-defined data that extends the bootspec document.

To reduce incompatibility and prevent names from clashing
between applications, it is **highly recommended** to use a
unique namespace for your extensions.

options.title: boot.bootspec.package
options.description: The bootspec package to use.

options.title: boot.consoleLogLevel
options.description:
The kernel console `loglevel`. All Kernel Messages with a log level smaller
than this setting will be printed to the console.

options.title: boot.crashDump.enable
options.description:
If enabled, NixOS will set up a kernel that will
boot on crash, and leave the user in systemd rescue
to be able to save the crashed kernel dump at
/proc/vmcore.
It also activates the NMI watchdog.

options.title: boot.crashDump.kernelParams
options.description: Parameters that will be passed to the kernel kexec-ed on crash.

options.title: boot.crashDump.reservedMemory
options.description:
The amount of memory reserved for the crashdump kernel.
If you choose a too high value, dmesg will mention
"crashkernel reservation failed".

options.title: boot.devShmSize
options.description:
Size limit for the /dev/shm tmpfs. Look at {manpage}`mount(8)`, tmpfs size option,
for the accepted syntax.

options.title: boot.devSize
options.description:
Size limit for the /dev tmpfs. Look at {manpage}`mount(8)`, tmpfs size option,
for the accepted syntax.

options.title: boot.enableContainers
options.description: Whether to enable support for NixOS containers.

options.title: boot.extraModprobeConfig
options.description:
Any additional configuration to be appended to the generated
{file}`modprobe.conf`.  This is typically used to
specify module options.  See
{manpage}`modprobe.d(5)` for details.

options.title: boot.extraModulePackages
options.description: A list of additional packages supplying kernel modules.

options.title: boot.extraSystemdUnitPaths
options.description:
Additional paths that get appended to the SYSTEMD_UNIT_PATH environment variable
that can contain mutable unit files.

options.title: boot.growPartition
options.description: Whether to enable growing the root partition on boot.

options.title: boot.hardwareScan
options.description:
Whether to try to load kernel modules for all detected hardware.
Usually this does a good job of providing you with the modules
you need, but sometimes it can crash the system or cause other
nasty effects.

options.title: boot.initrd.allowMissingModules
options.description:
Whether the initrd can be built even though modules listed in
{option}`boot.initrd.kernelModules` or
{option}`boot.initrd.availableKernelModules` are missing from
the kernel. This is useful when combining configurations that
include a lot of modules, such as
{option}`hardware.enableAllHardware`, with kernels that don't
provide as many modules as typical NixOS kernels.

Note that enabling this is discouraged. Instead, try disabling
individual modules by setting e.g.
`boot.initrd.availableKernelModules.foo = lib.mkForce false;`

options.title: boot.initrd.availableKernelModules
options.type: (attribute set of boolean) or (list of string) convertible to it
options.description:
The set of kernel modules in the initial ramdisk used during the
boot process.  This set must include all modules necessary for
mounting the root device.  That is, it should include modules
for the physical device (e.g., SCSI drivers) and for the file
system (e.g., ext3).  The set specified here is automatically
closed under the module dependency relation, i.e., all
dependencies of the modules list here are included
automatically.  The modules listed here are available in the
initrd, but are only loaded on demand (e.g., the ext3 module is
loaded automatically when an ext3 filesystem is mounted, and
modules for PCI devices are loaded when they match the PCI ID
of a device in your system).  To force a module to be loaded,
include it in {option}`boot.initrd.kernelModules`.

This can either be a list of modules, or an attrset. In an
attrset, names that are set to `true` represent modules that will
be included. Note that setting these names to `false` does not
prevent the module from being loaded. For that, use
{option}`boot.blacklistedKernelModules`.

options.title: boot.initrd.checkJournalingFS
options.description: Whether to run {command}`fsck` on journaling filesystems such as ext3.

options.title: boot.initrd.clevis.devices
options.description: Encrypted devices that need to be unlocked at boot using Clevis

options.title: boot.initrd.clevis.devices.<name>.secretFile
options.description: Clevis JWE file used to decrypt the device at boot, in concert with the chosen pin (one of TPM2, Tang server, or SSS).

options.title: boot.initrd.clevis.enable
options.description: Whether to enable Clevis in initrd.

options.title: boot.initrd.clevis.package
options.description: The clevis package to use.

options.title: boot.initrd.clevis.useTang
options.description: Whether the Clevis JWE file used to decrypt the devices uses a Tang server as a pin.

options.title: boot.initrd.compressor
options.type: string or function that evaluates to a(n) string
options.description:
The compressor to use on the initrd image. May be any of:

- The name of one of the predefined compressors, see {file}`pkgs/build-support/kernel/initrd-compressor-meta.nix` for the definitions.
- A function which, given the nixpkgs package set, returns the path to a compressor tool, e.g. `pkgs: "${pkgs.pigz}/bin/pigz"`
- (not recommended, because it does not work when cross-compiling) the full path to a compressor tool, e.g. `"${pkgs.pigz}/bin/pigz"`

The given program should read data from stdin and write it to stdout compressed.
options.default: `zstd` if the kernel supports it (5.9+), `gzip` if not

options.title: boot.initrd.compressorArgs
options.description: Arguments to pass to the compressor for the initrd image, or null to use the compressor's defaults.

options.title: boot.initrd.enable
options.description:
Whether to enable the NixOS initial RAM disk (initrd). This may be
needed to perform some initialisation tasks (like mounting
network/encrypted file systems) before continuing the boot process.

options.title: boot.initrd.extraFiles
options.description: Extra files to link and copy in to the initrd.

options.title: boot.initrd.extraFiles.<name>.source
options.description: The object to make available inside the initrd.

options.title: boot.initrd.extraFirmwarePaths
options.description: Other firmware files (relative to `"${config.hardware.firmware}/lib/firmware"`) to include in the final initrd we are building.

options.title: boot.initrd.includeDefaultModules
options.description:
This option, if set, adds a collection of default kernel modules
to {option}`boot.initrd.availableKernelModules` and
{option}`boot.initrd.kernelModules`.

options.title: boot.initrd.kernelModules
options.type: (attribute set of boolean) or (list of string) convertible to it
options.description:
Set of modules that are always loaded by the initrd.

This can either be a list of modules, or an attrset. In an
attrset, names that are set to `true` represent modules that will
be included. Note that setting these names to `false` does not
prevent the module from being loaded. For that, use
{option}`boot.blacklistedKernelModules`.

options.title: boot.initrd.luks.cryptoModules
options.description:
A list of cryptographic kernel modules needed to decrypt the root device(s).
The default includes all common modules.

options.title: boot.initrd.luks.devices
options.description:
The encrypted disk that should be opened before the root
filesystem is mounted. Both LVM-over-LUKS and LUKS-over-LVM
setups are supported. The unencrypted devices can be accessed as
{file}`/dev/mapper/«name»`.

options.title: boot.initrd.luks.devices.<name>.allowDiscards
options.description:
Whether to allow TRIM requests to the underlying device. This option
has security implications; please read the LUKS documentation before
activating it.
This option is incompatible with authenticated encryption (dm-crypt
stacked over dm-integrity).

options.title: boot.initrd.luks.devices.<name>.bypassWorkqueues
options.description:
Whether to bypass dm-crypt's internal read and write workqueues.
Enabling this should improve performance on SSDs; see
[here](https://wiki.archlinux.org/index.php/Dm-crypt/Specialties#Disable_workqueue_for_increased_solid_state_drive_(SSD)_performance)
for more information. Needs Linux 5.9 or later.

options.title: boot.initrd.luks.devices.<name>.device
options.description: Path of the underlying encrypted block device.

options.title: boot.initrd.luks.devices.<name>.fallbackToPassword
options.description:
Whether to fallback to interactive passphrase prompt if the keyfile
cannot be found. This will prevent unattended boot should the keyfile
go missing.

options.title: boot.initrd.luks.devices.<name>.fido2.credential
options.description: The FIDO2 credential ID.

options.title: boot.initrd.luks.devices.<name>.fido2.credentials
options.description:
List of FIDO2 credential IDs.

Use this if you have multiple FIDO2 keys you want to use for the same luks device.

options.title: boot.initrd.luks.devices.<name>.fido2.gracePeriod
options.description: Time in seconds to wait for the FIDO2 key.

options.title: boot.initrd.luks.devices.<name>.fido2.passwordLess
options.description:
Defines whatever to use an empty string as a default salt.

Enable only when your device is PIN protected, such as [Trezor](https://trezor.io/).

options.title: boot.initrd.luks.devices.<name>.gpgCard
options.description:
The option to use this LUKS device with a GPG encrypted luks password by the GPG Smartcard.
If null (the default), GPG-Smartcard will be disabled for this device.

options.title: boot.initrd.luks.devices.<name>.gpgCard.encryptedPass
options.description: Path to the GPG encrypted passphrase.

options.title: boot.initrd.luks.devices.<name>.gpgCard.gracePeriod
options.description: Time in seconds to wait for the GPG Smartcard.

options.title: boot.initrd.luks.devices.<name>.gpgCard.publicKey
options.description: Path to the Public Key.

options.title: boot.initrd.luks.devices.<name>.header
options.description:
The name of the file or block device that
should be used as header for the encrypted device.

options.title: boot.initrd.luks.devices.<name>.keyFile
options.description:
The name of the file (can be a raw device or a partition) that
should be used as the decryption key for the encrypted device. If
not specified, you will be prompted for a passphrase instead.

options.title: boot.initrd.luks.devices.<name>.keyFileOffset
options.description:
The offset of the key file. Use this in combination with
`keyFileSize` to use part of a file as key file
(often the case if a raw device or partition is used as a key file).
If not specified, the key begins at the first byte of
`keyFile`.

options.title: boot.initrd.luks.devices.<name>.keyFileSize
options.description:
The size of the key file. Use this if only the beginning of the
key file should be used as a key (often the case if a raw device
or partition is used as key file). If not specified, the whole
`keyFile` will be used decryption, instead of just
the first `keyFileSize` bytes.

options.title: boot.initrd.luks.devices.<name>.keyFileTimeout
options.description:
The amount of time in seconds for a keyFile to appear before
timing out and trying passwords.

options.title: boot.initrd.luks.devices.<name>.postOpenCommands
options.description: Commands that should be run right after we have mounted our LUKS device.

options.title: boot.initrd.luks.devices.<name>.preLVM
options.description: Whether the luksOpen will be attempted before LVM scan or after it.

options.title: boot.initrd.luks.devices.<name>.preOpenCommands
options.description:
Commands that should be run right before we try to mount our LUKS device.
This can be useful, if the keys needed to open the drive is on another partition.

options.title: boot.initrd.luks.devices.<name>.tryEmptyPassphrase
options.description:
If keyFile fails then try an empty passphrase first before
prompting for password.

options.title: boot.initrd.luks.devices.<name>.yubikey
options.description:
The options to use for this LUKS device in YubiKey-PBA.
If null (the default), YubiKey-PBA will be disabled for this device.

options.title: boot.initrd.luks.devices.<name>.yubikey.gracePeriod
options.description: Time in seconds to wait for the YubiKey.

options.title: boot.initrd.luks.devices.<name>.yubikey.iterationStep
options.description: How much the iteration count for PBKDF2 is increased at each successful authentication.

options.title: boot.initrd.luks.devices.<name>.yubikey.keyLength
options.description: Length of the LUKS slot key derived with PBKDF2 in byte.

options.title: boot.initrd.luks.devices.<name>.yubikey.saltLength
options.description: Length of the new salt in byte (64 is the effective maximum).

options.title: boot.initrd.luks.devices.<name>.yubikey.slot
options.description: Which slot on the YubiKey to challenge.

options.title: boot.initrd.luks.devices.<name>.yubikey.storage.device
options.description:
An unencrypted device that will temporarily be mounted in stage-1.
Must contain the current salt to create the challenge for this LUKS device.

options.title: boot.initrd.luks.devices.<name>.yubikey.storage.fsType
options.description: The filesystem of the unencrypted device.

options.title: boot.initrd.luks.devices.<name>.yubikey.storage.path
options.description:
Absolute path of the salt on the unencrypted device with
that device's root directory as "/".

options.title: boot.initrd.luks.devices.<name>.yubikey.twoFactor
options.description: Whether to use a passphrase and a YubiKey (true), or only a YubiKey (false).

options.title: boot.initrd.luks.fido2Support
options.description: Enables support for authenticating with FIDO2 devices.

options.title: boot.initrd.luks.gpgSupport
options.description: Enables support for authenticating with a GPG encrypted password.

options.title: boot.initrd.luks.mitigateDMAAttacks
options.description:
Unless enabled, encryption keys can be easily recovered by an attacker with physical
access to any machine with PCMCIA, ExpressCard, ThunderBolt or FireWire port.
More information is available at <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DMA_attack>.

This option blacklists FireWire drivers, but doesn't remove them. You can manually
load the drivers if you need to use a FireWire device, but don't forget to unload them!

options.title: boot.initrd.luks.reusePassphrases
options.description:
When opening a new LUKS device try reusing last successful
passphrase.

Useful for mounting a number of devices that use the same
passphrase without retyping it several times.

Such setup can be useful if you use {command}`cryptsetup luksSuspend`.
Different LUKS devices will still have
different master keys even when using the same passphrase.

options.title: boot.initrd.luks.yubikeySupport
options.description:
Enables support for authenticating with a YubiKey on LUKS devices.
See the NixOS wiki for information on how to properly setup a LUKS device
and a YubiKey to work with this feature.

options.title: boot.initrd.network.enable
options.description:
Add network connectivity support to initrd. The network may be
configured using the `ip` kernel parameter,
as described in [the kernel documentation](https://www.kernel.org/doc/Documentation/filesystems/nfs/nfsroot.txt).
Otherwise, if
{option}`networking.useDHCP` is enabled, an IP address
is acquired using DHCP.

You should add the module(s) required for your network card to
boot.initrd.availableKernelModules.
`lspci -v | grep -iA8 'network\|ethernet'`
will tell you which.

options.title: boot.initrd.network.flushBeforeStage2
options.description:
Whether to clear the configuration of the interfaces that were set up in
the initrd right before stage 2 takes over. Stage 2 will do the regular network
configuration based on the NixOS networking options.

The default is false when systemd is enabled in initrd,
because the systemd-networkd documentation suggests it.

options.title: boot.initrd.network.ifstate.allowIfstateToDrasticlyIncreaseInitrdSize
options.description: IfState in initrd drastically increases the size of initrd, your boot partition may be too small and/or you may have significantly fewer generations. By setting this option, you acknowledge this fact and keep it in mind when reporting issues.

options.title: boot.initrd.network.ifstate.cleanupSettings
options.description: Content of IfState's initrd cleanup configuration file. See <https://ifstate.net/2.0/schema/> for details. This configuration gets applied before systemd switches to stage two. The goal is to deconfigurate the whole network in order to prevent access to services, before the firewall is configured. The stage two IfState configuration will start after the firewall is configured.

options.title: boot.initrd.network.ifstate.enable
options.description: Whether to enable initrd networking using IfState.

options.title: boot.initrd.network.ifstate.package
options.description: The initrd IfState package to use.

options.title: boot.initrd.network.ifstate.settings
options.description: Content of IfState's initrd configuration file. See <https://ifstate.net/2.2/schema/> for details.

options.title: boot.initrd.network.openvpn.configuration
options.description:
The configuration file for OpenVPN.

::: {.warning}
Unless your bootloader supports initrd secrets, this configuration
is stored insecurely in the global Nix store.
:::

options.title: boot.initrd.network.openvpn.enable
options.description:
Starts an OpenVPN client during initrd boot. It can be used to e.g.
remotely accessing the SSH service controlled by
{option}`boot.initrd.network.ssh` or other network services
included. Service is killed when stage-1 boot is finished.

options.title: boot.initrd.network.postCommands
options.description:
Shell commands to be executed after stage 1 of the
boot has initialised the network.

options.title: boot.initrd.network.ssh.authorizedKeyFiles
options.description:
Authorized keys taken from files for the root user on initrd.
You can combine the `authorizedKeyFiles` and `authorizedKeys` options.

options.title: boot.initrd.network.ssh.authorizedKeys
options.description:
Authorized keys for the root user on initrd.
You can combine the `authorizedKeys` and `authorizedKeyFiles` options.

options.title: boot.initrd.network.ssh.enable
options.description:
Start SSH service during initrd boot. It can be used to debug failing
boot on a remote server, enter pasphrase for an encrypted partition etc.
Service is killed when stage-1 boot is finished.

The sshd configuration is largely inherited from
{option}`services.openssh`.

options.title: boot.initrd.network.ssh.extraConfig
options.description: Verbatim contents of {file}`sshd_config`.

options.title: boot.initrd.network.ssh.hostKeys
options.description:
Specify SSH host keys to import into the initrd.

To generate keys, use
{manpage}`ssh-keygen(1)`
as root:

```
ssh-keygen -t rsa -N "" -f /etc/secrets/initrd/ssh_host_rsa_key
ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -N "" -f /etc/secrets/initrd/ssh_host_ed25519_key
```

::: {.warning}
Unless your bootloader supports initrd secrets, these keys
are stored insecurely in the global Nix store. Do NOT use
your regular SSH host private keys for this purpose or
you'll expose them to regular users!

Additionally, even if your initrd supports secrets, if
you're using initrd SSH to unlock an encrypted disk then
using your regular host keys exposes the private keys on
your unencrypted boot partition.
:::

options.title: boot.initrd.network.ssh.ignoreEmptyHostKeys
options.description:
Allow leaving {option}`config.boot.initrd.network.ssh.hostKeys` empty,
to deploy ssh host keys out of band.

options.title: boot.initrd.network.ssh.port
options.type: 16 bit unsigned integer; between 0 and 65535 (both inclusive)
options.description: Port on which SSH initrd service should listen.

options.title: boot.initrd.network.ssh.shell
options.description: Login shell of the remote user. Can be used to limit actions user can do.

options.title: boot.initrd.network.udhcpc.enable
options.description:
Enables the udhcpc service during stage 1 of the boot process. This
defaults to {option}`networking.useDHCP`. Therefore, this useful if
useDHCP is off but the initramfs should do dhcp.

options.title: boot.initrd.network.udhcpc.extraArgs
options.description:
Additional command-line arguments passed verbatim to
udhcpc if {option}`boot.initrd.network.enable` and
{option}`boot.initrd.network.udhcpc.enable` are enabled.

options.title: boot.initrd.nix-store-veritysetup.enable
options.description: Whether to enable nix-store-veritysetup.

options.title: boot.initrd.postDeviceCommands
options.description:
Shell commands to be executed immediately after stage 1 of the
boot has loaded kernel modules and created device nodes in
{file}`/dev`.

options.title: boot.initrd.postMountCommands
options.description:
Shell commands to be executed immediately after the stage 1
filesystems have been mounted.

options.title: boot.initrd.postResumeCommands
options.description: Shell commands to be executed immediately after attempting to resume.

options.title: boot.initrd.preDeviceCommands
options.description:
Shell commands to be executed before udev is started to create
device nodes.

options.title: boot.initrd.preFailCommands
options.description: Shell commands to be executed before the failure prompt is shown.

options.title: boot.initrd.preLVMCommands
options.description: Shell commands to be executed immediately before LVM discovery.

options.title: boot.initrd.prepend
options.description: Other initrd files to prepend to the final initrd we are building.

options.title: boot.initrd.secrets
options.type: attribute set of (null or absolute path)
options.description:
Secrets to append to the initrd. The attribute name is the
path the secret should have inside the initrd, the value
is the path it should be copied from (or null for the same
path inside and out).

Note that `nixos-rebuild switch` will generate the initrd
also for past generations, so if secrets are moved or deleted
you will also have to garbage collect the generations that
use those secrets.

options.title: boot.initrd.services.bcache.enable
options.description:
*This will only be used when systemd is used in stage 1.*

Whether to enable bcache support in the initrd.

options.title: boot.initrd.services.lvm.enable
options.description:
*This will only be used when systemd is used in stage 1.*

Whether to enable booting from LVM2 in the initrd.

options.title: boot.initrd.services.resolved.enable
options.description:
Whether to enable resolved for stage 1 networking.
Uses the toplevel 'services.resolved' options for 'resolved.conf'

options.title: boot.initrd.services.udev.binPackages
options.description:
*This will only be used when systemd is used in stage 1.*

Packages to search for binaries that are referenced by the udev rules in stage 1.
This list always contains /bin of the initrd.

options.title: boot.initrd.services.udev.packages
options.description:
*This will only be used when systemd is used in stage 1.*

List of packages containing {command}`udev` rules that will be copied to stage 1.
All files found in
{file}`«pkg»/etc/udev/rules.d` and
{file}`«pkg»/lib/udev/rules.d`
will be included.

options.title: boot.initrd.services.udev.rules
options.description:
{command}`udev` rules to include in the initrd
*only*. They'll be written into file
{file}`99-local.rules`. Thus they are read and applied
after the essential initrd rules.
options.example:
''
  SUBSYSTEM=="net", ACTION=="add", DRIVERS=="?*", ATTR{address}=="00:1D:60:B9:6D:4F", KERNEL=="eth*", NAME="my_fast_network_card"
''

options.title: boot.initrd.supportedFilesystems
options.type: (attribute set of boolean) or (list of string) convertible to it
options.description:
Names of supported filesystem types, or an attribute set of file system types
and their state. The set form may be used together with `lib.mkForce` to
explicitly disable support for specific filesystems, e.g. to disable ZFS
with an unsupported kernel.

options.title: boot.initrd.systemd.additionalUpstreamUnits

options.title: boot.initrd.systemd.contents.<name>.enable

options.title: boot.initrd.systemd.dbus.enable

options.title: boot.initrd.systemd.dmVerity.enable
options.description:
Mount verity-protected block devices in the initrd.

Enabling this option allows to use `systemd-veritysetup` and
`systemd-veritysetup-generator` in the initrd.

options.title: boot.initrd.systemd.emergencyAccess
options.type: boolean or null or (string, not containing newlines or colons)

null for no emergency access.

Can also be set to a hashed super user password to allow

For emergency access after initrd, use `systemd.enableEmergencyMode` instead.

options.title: boot.initrd.systemd.enable

stage 2 counterparts such as {option}`systemd.services`,

options.title: boot.initrd.systemd.extraBin

options.title: boot.initrd.systemd.initrdBin

options.title: boot.initrd.systemd.managerEnvironment

Environment variables of PID 1. These variables are

options.title: boot.initrd.systemd.mounts

Definition of systemd mount units.

options.title: boot.initrd.systemd.network.config

options.title: boot.initrd.systemd.network.links

options.title: boot.initrd.systemd.network.netdevs

options.title: boot.initrd.systemd.network.networks

options.title: boot.initrd.systemd.network.wait-online.anyInterface
options.description:
Whether to consider the network online when any interface is online, as opposed to all of them.
This is useful on portable machines with a wired and a wireless interface, for example.

This is on by default if {option}`networking.useDHCP` is enabled.

options.title: boot.initrd.systemd.network.wait-online.enable
options.description:
Whether to enable the systemd-networkd-wait-online service.

systemd-networkd-wait-online can timeout and fail if there are no network interfaces
available for it to manage. When systemd-networkd is enabled but a different service is
responsible for managing the system's internet connection (for example, NetworkManager or
connman are used to manage WiFi connections), this service is unnecessary and can be

options.title: boot.initrd.systemd.network.wait-online.extraArgs
options.description:
Extra command-line arguments to pass to systemd-networkd-wait-online.
These also affect per-interface `systemd-network-wait-online@` services.

See {manpage}`systemd-networkd-wait-online.service(8)` for all available options.

options.title: boot.initrd.systemd.network.wait-online.ignoredInterfaces
options.description: Network interfaces to be ignored when deciding if the system is online.

options.title: boot.initrd.systemd.network.wait-online.timeout

options.description: Packages providing systemd units and hooks.

options.title: boot.initrd.systemd.paths
options.description: Definition of systemd path units.

options.title: boot.initrd.systemd.repart.device
options.description:
The device to operate on.

If `device == null`, systemd-repart will operate on the device
backing the root partition. So in order to dynamically *create* the
root partition in the initrd you need to set a device.

options.title: boot.initrd.systemd.repart.discard
options.description:
Controls whether to issue the BLKDISCARD I/O control command on the
space taken up by any added partitions or on the space in between them.
Usually, it's a good idea to issue this request since it tells the underlying
hardware that the covered blocks shall be considered empty, improving performance.

See {manpage}`systemd-repart(8)` for details.

options.title: boot.initrd.systemd.repart.empty
options.description:
Controls how to operate on empty devices that contain no partition table yet.
See {manpage}`systemd-repart(8)` for details.

options.title: boot.initrd.systemd.repart.enable
options.description:
Grow and add partitions to a partition table at boot time in the initrd.
systemd-repart only works with GPT partition tables.

To run systemd-repart after the initrd, see
`options.systemd.repart.enable`.

options.title: boot.initrd.systemd.repart.extraArgs
options.description:
Extra command-line arguments to pass to systemd-repart.

See {manpage}`systemd-repart(8)` for all available options.

options.title: boot.initrd.systemd.root

Controls how systemd will interpret the root FS in initrd. See
{manpage}`kernel-command-line(7)`. NixOS currently does not
allow specifying the root file system itself this

options.title: boot.initrd.systemd.tmpfiles.settings.<config-name>.<path>.<tmpfiles-type>.argument

options.title: boot.kernel.randstructSeed
options.description:
Provides a custom seed for the {var}`RANDSTRUCT` security
option of the Linux kernel. Note that {var}`RANDSTRUCT` is
only enabled in NixOS hardened kernels. Using a custom seed requires
building the kernel and dependent packages locally, since this
customization happens at build time.

options.title: boot.kernel.sysctl
options.type: open submodule of attribute set of (sysctl option value)
options.description:
Runtime parameters of the Linux kernel, as set by
{manpage}`sysctl(8)`.  Note that sysctl
parameters names must be enclosed in quotes
(e.g. `"vm.swappiness"` instead of
`vm.swappiness`).  The value of each
parameter may be a string, integer, boolean, or null
(signifying the option will not appear at all).

options.title: boot.kernel.sysctl."net.core.rmem_max"
options.description: The maximum receive socket buffer size in bytes. In case of conflicting values, the highest will be used.

options.title: boot.kernel.sysctl."net.core.wmem_max"
options.description: The maximum send socket buffer size in bytes. In case of conflicting values, the highest will be used.

options.title: boot.kernel.sysfs
options.type: open submodule of nested attribute set of null or sysfs attribute values
options.description:
sysfs attributes to be set as soon as they become available.

Attribute names represent path components in the sysfs filesystem and
cannot be `.` or `..` nor contain any slash character (`/`).

Names may contain shell‐style glob patterns (`*`, `?` and `[…]`)
matching a single path component, these should however be used with
caution, as they may produce unexpected results if attribute paths
overlap.

Values will be converted to strings, with list elements concatenated
with commata and booleans converted to numeric values (`0` or `1`).

`null` values are ignored, allowing removal of values defined in other
modules, as are empty attribute sets.

List values defined in different modules will _not_ be concatenated.

This option may only be used for attributes which can be set
idempotently, as the configured values might be written more than once.

options.title: boot.kernelModules
options.type: (attribute set of boolean) or (list of string) convertible to it
options.description:
The set of kernel modules to be loaded in the second stage of
the boot process.  Note that modules that are needed to
mount the root file system should be added to
{option}`boot.initrd.availableKernelModules` or
{option}`boot.initrd.kernelModules`.

This can either be a list of modules, or an attrset. In an
attrset, names that are set to `true` represent modules that will
be included. Note that setting these names to `false` does not
prevent the module from being loaded. For that, use
{option}`boot.blacklistedKernelModules`.

options.title: boot.kernelPackages
options.description:
This option allows you to override the Linux kernel used by
NixOS.  Since things like external kernel module packages are
tied to the kernel you're using, it also overrides those.
This option is a function that takes Nixpkgs as an argument
(as a convenience), and returns an attribute set containing at
the very least an attribute {var}`kernel`.
Additional attributes may be needed depending on your
configuration.  For instance, if you use the NVIDIA X driver,
then it also needs to contain an attribute
{var}`nvidia_x11`.

Please note that we strictly support kernel versions that are
maintained by the Linux developers only. More information on the
availability of kernel versions is documented
[in the Linux section of the manual](https://nixos.org/manual/nixos/unstable/index.html#sec-kernel-config).

options.title: boot.kernelParams
options.type: list of string, with spaces inside double quotes
options.description: Parameters added to the kernel command line.

options.title: boot.kernelPatches
options.description:
A list of additional patches to apply to the kernel.

Every item should be an attribute set with the following attributes:

```nix
{
  name = "foo";                 # descriptive name, required

  patch = ./foo.patch;          # path or derivation that contains the patch source
                                # (required, but can be null if only config changes
                                # are needed)

  structuredExtraConfig = {     # attrset of extra configuration parameters without the CONFIG_ prefix
    FOO = lib.kernel.yes;       # (optional)
  };                            # values should generally be lib.kernel.yes,
                                # lib.kernel.no or lib.kernel.module

  features = {                  # attrset of extra "features" the kernel is considered to have
    foo = true;                 # (may be checked by other NixOS modules, optional)
  };

  extraConfig = "FOO y";        # extra configuration options in string form without the CONFIG_ prefix
                                # (optional, multiple lines allowed to specify multiple options)
                                # (deprecated, use structuredExtraConfig instead)
}
```

There's a small set of existing kernel patches in Nixpkgs, available as `pkgs.kernelPatches`,
that follow this format and can be used directly.

options.title: boot.kexec.enable
options.description: Whether to enable kexec.

options.title: boot.loader.efi.canTouchEfiVariables
options.description: Whether the installation process is allowed to modify EFI boot variables.

options.title: boot.loader.efi.efiSysMountPoint
options.description: Where the EFI System Partition is mounted.

options.title: boot.loader.external.enable
options.description: Whether to enable using an external tool to install your bootloader.

options.title: boot.loader.external.installHook
options.description:
The full path to a program of your choosing which performs the bootloader installation process.

The program will be called with an argument pointing to the output of the system's toplevel.

options.title: boot.loader.generationsDir.copyKernels
options.description:
Whether to copy the necessary boot files into /boot, so
/nix/store is not needed by the boot loader.

options.title: boot.loader.generationsDir.enable
options.description:
Whether to create symlinks to the system generations under
`/boot`.  When enabled,
`/boot/default/kernel`,
`/boot/default/initrd`, etc., are updated to
point to the current generation's kernel image, initial RAM
disk, and other bootstrap files.

This optional is not necessary with boot loaders such as GNU GRUB
for which the menu is updated to point to the latest bootstrap
files.  However, it is needed for U-Boot on platforms where the
boot command line is stored in flash memory rather than in a
menu file.

options.title: boot.loader.generic-extlinux-compatible.configurationLimit
options.description: Maximum number of configurations in the boot menu.

options.title: boot.loader.generic-extlinux-compatible.enable
options.description:
Whether to generate an extlinux-compatible configuration file
under `/boot/extlinux.conf`.  For instance,
U-Boot's generic distro boot support uses this file format.

See [U-boot's documentation](https://u-boot.readthedocs.io/en/latest/develop/distro.html)
for more information.

options.title: boot.loader.generic-extlinux-compatible.mirroredBoots
options.description: Mirror the boot configuration to multiple paths.

options.title: boot.loader.generic-extlinux-compatible.mirroredBoots.*.path
options.description:
The path to the boot directory where the extlinux-compatible
configuration files will be written.

options.title: boot.loader.generic-extlinux-compatible.populateCmd
options.description:
Contains the builder command used to populate an image,
honoring all options except the `-c <path-to-default-configuration>`
argument.
Useful to have for sdImage.populateRootCommands

options.title: boot.loader.generic-extlinux-compatible.useGenerationDeviceTree
options.description:
Whether to generate Device Tree-related directives in the
extlinux configuration.

When enabled, the bootloader will attempt to load the device
tree binaries from the generation's kernel.

Note that this affects all generations, regardless of the
setting value used in their configurations.

options.title: boot.loader.grub.backgroundColor
options.description: Background color to be used for GRUB to fill the areas the image isn't filling.

options.title: boot.loader.grub.configurationLimit
options.description:
Maximum of configurations in boot menu. GRUB has problems when
there are too many entries.

options.title: boot.loader.grub.configurationName
options.description: GRUB entry name instead of default.

options.title: boot.loader.grub.copyKernels
options.description:
Whether the GRUB menu builder should copy kernels and initial
ramdisks to /boot.  This is done automatically if /boot is
on a different partition than /.

options.title: boot.loader.grub.default
options.description:
Index of the default menu item to be booted.
Can also be set to "saved", which will make GRUB select
the menu item that was used at the last boot.

options.title: boot.loader.grub.device
options.description:
The device on which the GRUB boot loader will be installed.
The special value `nodev` means that a GRUB
boot menu will be generated, but GRUB itself will not
actually be installed.  To install GRUB on multiple devices,
use `boot.loader.grub.devices`.

options.title: boot.loader.grub.devices
options.description:
The devices on which the boot loader, GRUB, will be
installed. Can be used instead of `device` to
install GRUB onto multiple devices.

options.title: boot.loader.grub.efiInstallAsRemovable
options.description:
Whether to invoke `grub-install` with
`--removable`.

Unless you turn this on, GRUB will install itself somewhere in
`boot.loader.efi.efiSysMountPoint` (exactly where
depends on other config variables). If you've set
`boot.loader.efi.canTouchEfiVariables` *AND* you
are currently booted in UEFI mode, then GRUB will use
`efibootmgr` to modify the boot order in the
EFI variables of your firmware to include this location. If you are
*not* booted in UEFI mode at the time GRUB is being installed, the
NVRAM will not be modified, and your system will not find GRUB at
boot time. However, GRUB will still return success so you may miss
the warning that gets printed ("`efibootmgr: EFI variables
are not supported on this system.`").

If you turn this feature on, GRUB will install itself in a
special location within `efiSysMountPoint` (namely
`EFI/boot/boot$arch.efi`) which the firmwares
are hardcoded to try first, regardless of NVRAM EFI variables.

To summarize, turn this on if:
- You are installing NixOS and want it to boot in UEFI mode,
  but you are currently booted in legacy mode
- You want to make a drive that will boot regardless of
  the NVRAM state of the computer (like a USB "removable" drive)
- You simply dislike the idea of depending on NVRAM
  state to make your drive bootable

options.title: boot.loader.grub.efiSupport
options.description: Whether GRUB should be built with EFI support.

options.title: boot.loader.grub.enable
options.description: Whether to enable the GNU GRUB boot loader.

options.title: boot.loader.grub.enableCryptodisk
options.description:
Enable support for encrypted partitions. GRUB should automatically
unlock the correct encrypted partition and look for filesystems.

options.title: boot.loader.grub.entryOptions
options.description: Options applied to the primary NixOS menu entry.

options.title: boot.loader.grub.extraConfig
options.description:
Additional GRUB commands inserted in the configuration file
just before the menu entries.

options.title: boot.loader.grub.extraEntries
options.description: Any additional entries you want added to the GRUB boot menu.

options.title: boot.loader.grub.extraEntriesBeforeNixOS
options.description: Whether extraEntries are included before the default option.

options.title: boot.loader.grub.extraFiles
options.description:
A set of files to be copied to {file}`/boot`.
Each attribute name denotes the destination file name in
{file}`/boot`, while the corresponding
attribute value specifies the source file.

options.title: boot.loader.grub.extraGrubInstallArgs
options.description:
Additional arguments passed to `grub-install`.

A use case for this is to build specific GRUB2 modules
directly into the GRUB2 kernel image, so that they are available
and activated even in the `grub rescue` shell.

They are also necessary when the BIOS/UEFI is bugged and cannot
correctly read large disks (e.g. above 2 TB), so GRUB2's own
`nativedisk` and related modules can be used
to use its own disk drivers. The example shows one such case.
This is also useful for booting from USB.
See the
[
GRUB source code
](https://git.savannah.gnu.org/cgit/grub.git/tree/grub-core/commands/nativedisk.c?h=grub-2.04#n326)
for which disk modules are available.

The list elements are passed directly as `argv`
arguments to the `grub-install` program, in order.

options.title: boot.loader.grub.extraInstallCommands
options.description:
Additional shell commands inserted in the bootloader installer
script after generating menu entries.
options.example:
''
  # the example below generates detached signatures that GRUB can verify
  # https://www.gnu.org/software/grub/manual/grub/grub.html#Using-digital-signatures
  ''${pkgs.findutils}/bin/find /boot -not -path "/boot/efi/*" -type f -name '*.sig' -delete
  old_gpg_home=$GNUPGHOME
  export GNUPGHOME="$(mktemp -d)"
  ''${pkgs.gnupg}/bin/gpg --import ''${priv_key} > /dev/null 2>&1
  ''${pkgs.findutils}/bin/find /boot -not -path "/boot/efi/*" -type f -exec ''${pkgs.gnupg}/bin/gpg --detach-sign "{}" \; > /dev/null 2>&1
  rm -rf $GNUPGHOME
  export GNUPGHOME=$old_gpg_home
''

options.title: boot.loader.grub.memtest86.params
options.description:
Parameters added to the Memtest86+ command line. As of memtest86+ 5.01
the following list of (apparently undocumented) parameters are
accepted:

- `console=...`, set up a serial console.
  Examples:
  `console=ttyS0`,
  `console=ttyS0,9600` or
  `console=ttyS0,115200n8`.

- `btrace`, enable boot trace.

- `maxcpus=N`, limit number of CPUs.

- `onepass`, run one pass and exit if there
  are no errors.

- `tstlist=...`, list of tests to run.
  Example: `0,1,2`.

- `cpumask=...`, set a CPU mask, to select CPUs
  to use for testing.

This list of command line options was obtained by reading the
Memtest86+ source code.

- `menu` shows the menu.

When using a theme, the default value (`menu`) is appropriate for the graphical countdown.

When attempting to do flicker-free boot, `hidden` should be used.

See the [GRUB documentation section about `timeout_style`](https://www.gnu.org/software/grub/manual/grub/html_node/timeout.html).

::: {.note}
If this option is set to ‘countdown’ or ‘hidden’ [...] and ESC or F4 are pressed, or SHIFT is held down during that time, it will display the menu and wait for input.

Each attribute name denotes the destination file name,
and the corresponding attribute value is the contents of the entry.

To control the ordering of the entry in the boot menu, use the sort-key

<https://uapi-group.org/specifications/specs/boot_loader_specification/#sorting>

options.description:

script after generating menu entries. It can be used to expand

information (such as the resulting `init=` kernel parameter).
options.example:
''
  default_cfg=$(cat /boot/loader/loader.conf | grep default | awk '{print $2}')
  init_value=$(cat /boot/loader/entries/$default_cfg | grep init= | awk '{print $2}')
  sed -i "s|@INIT@|$init_value|g" /boot/custom/config_with_placeholder.conf
''

Make `netboot.xyz` available from the

options.title: boot.loader.systemd-boot.netbootxyz.sortKey

`systemd-boot` orders the menu entries by their sort keys,

it should start with {file}`o` or onwards.

options.title: boot.loader.systemd-boot.rebootForBitlocker
options.description:
Enable *EXPERIMENTAL* BitLocker support.

Try to detect BitLocker encrypted drives along with an active
TPM. If both are found and Windows Boot Manager is selected in
the boot menu, set the "BootNext" EFI variable and restart the
system. The firmware will then start Windows Boot Manager
directly, leaving the TPM PCRs in expected states so that
Windows can unseal the encryption key.

options.title: boot.loader.systemd-boot.sortKey
options.description:
The sort key used for the NixOS bootloader entries.
This key determines sorting relative to non-NixOS entries.
See also <https://uapi-group.org/specifications/specs/boot_loader_specification/#sorting>

This option can also be used to control the sorting of NixOS specialisations.

By default, specialisations inherit the sort key of their parent generation
and will have the same value for both the sort-key and the version (i.e. the generation number),
systemd-boot will therefore sort them based on their file name, meaning that
in your boot menu you will have each main generation directly followed by
its specialisations sorted alphabetically by their names.

If you want a different ordering for a specialisation, you can override
its sort-key which will cause the specialisation to be uncoupled from its
parent generation. It will then be sorted by its new sort-key just like
any other boot entry.

The sort-key is stored in the generation's bootspec, which means that
generations keep their sort-keys even if the original definition of the
generation was removed from the NixOS configuration.
It also means that updating the sort-key will only affect new generations,
while old ones will keep the sort-key that they were originally built with.

options.title: boot.loader.systemd-boot.windows
options.description:
Make Windows bootable from systemd-boot. This option is not necessary when Windows and
NixOS use the same EFI System Partition (ESP). In that case, Windows will automatically be
detected by systemd-boot.

However, if Windows is installed on a separate drive or ESP, you can use this option to add
a menu entry for each installation manually.

The attribute name is used for the title of the menu entry and internal file names.

options.title: boot.loader.systemd-boot.windows.<name>.efiDeviceHandle
options.description:
The device handle of the EFI System Partition (ESP) where the Windows bootloader is
located. This is the device handle that the EDK2 UEFI Shell uses to load the
bootloader.

To find this handle, follow these steps:
1. Set {option}`boot.loader.systemd-boot.edk2-uefi-shell.enable` to `true`
2. Run `nixos-rebuild boot`
3. Reboot and select "EDK2 UEFI Shell" from the systemd-boot menu
4. Run `map -c` to list all consistent device handles
5. For each device handle (for example, `HD0c1`), run `ls HD0c1:\EFI`
6. If the output contains the directory `Microsoft`, you might have found the correct device handle
7. Run `HD0c1:\EFI\Microsoft\Boot\Bootmgfw.efi` to check if Windows boots correctly
8. If it does, this device handle is the one you need (in this example, `HD0c1`)

This option is required, there is no useful default.

options.title: boot.loader.systemd-boot.windows.<name>.sortKey
options.description:
`systemd-boot` orders the menu entries by their sort keys,
so if you want something to appear after all the NixOS entries,
it should start with {file}`o` or onwards.

See also {option}`boot.loader.systemd-boot.sortKey`..
options.default: "attribute name of this entry, prefixed with \"o_windows_\""

options.title: boot.loader.systemd-boot.windows.<name>.title
options.description: The title of the boot menu entry.
options.default: "attribute name of this entry, prefixed with \"Windows \""

options.title: boot.loader.systemd-boot.xbootldrMountPoint
options.description:
Where the XBOOTLDR partition is mounted.

If set, this partition will be used as $BOOT to store boot loader entries and extra files
instead of the EFI partition. As per the bootloader specification, it is recommended that
the EFI and XBOOTLDR partitions be mounted at `/efi` and `/boot`, respectively.

options.title: boot.loader.timeout
options.description: Timeout (in seconds) until loader boots the default menu item. Use null if the loader menu should be displayed indefinitely.

options.title: boot.modprobeConfig.enable

options.title: boot.modprobeConfig.useUbuntuModuleBlacklist

options.title: boot.nixStoreMountOpts
options.description:
Defines the mount options used on a bind mount for the {file}`/nix/store`.
This affects the whole system except the nix store daemon, which will undo the bind mount.

`ro` enforces immutability of the Nix store.
The store daemon should already not put device mappers or suid binaries in the store,
meaning `nosuid` and `nodev` enforce what should already be the case.
