options.title: security.agnos.settings.accounts.*.certificates.*.domains
options.description: Domains the certificate represents

options.title: security.agnos.settings.accounts.*.certificates.*.fullchain_output_file
options.description:
Output path for the full chain including the acquired certificate.
If a relative path is specified, the file will be created in `/var/lib/agnos`.

options.title: security.agnos.settings.accounts.*.certificates.*.key_output_file
options.description:
Output path for the certificate private key.
If a relative path is specified, the file will be created in `/var/lib/agnos`.

options.title: security.agnos.settings.accounts.*.email
options.description: Email associated with this account.

options.title: security.agnos.settings.accounts.*.private_key_path
options.description:
Path of the PEM-encoded private key for this account.
Currently, only RSA keys are supported.

If this path does not exist, then the behavior depends on `generateKeys.enable`.
When this option is `true`,
the key will be automatically generated and saved to this path.
When it is `false`, agnos will fail.

If a relative path is specified,
the key will be looked up (or generated and saved to) under `/var/lib/agnos`.

options.title: security.agnos.settings.dns_listen_addr
options.description:
Address for agnos to listen on.
Note that this needs to be reachable by the outside world,
and 53 is required in most situations
since `NS` records do not allow specifying the port.

options.title: security.agnos.startAt
options.description:
How often or when to run agnos.

The format is described in
{manpage}`systemd.time(7)`.

options.title: security.agnos.temporarilyOpenFirewall
options.description:
When `true`, will open the port specified in `settings.dns_listen_addr`
before running the agnos service, and close it when agnos finishes running.

options.title: security.agnos.user
options.description: User to run Agnos as. The acquired certificates will be owned by this user.

options.title: security.allowSimultaneousMultithreading
options.description:
Whether to allow SMT/hyperthreading.  Disabling SMT means that only
physical CPU cores will be usable at runtime, potentially at
significant performance cost.

The primary motivation for disabling SMT is to mitigate the risk of
leaking data between threads running on the same CPU core (due to
e.g., shared caches).  This attack vector is unproven.

Disabling SMT is a supplement to the L1 data cache flushing mitigation
(see [](#opt-security.virtualisation.flushL1DataCache))
versus malicious VM guests (SMT could "bring back" previously flushed
data).

options.title: security.allowUserNamespaces
options.description:
Whether to allow creation of user namespaces.

The motivation for disabling user namespaces is the potential
presence of code paths where the kernel's permission checking
logic fails to account for namespacing, instead permitting a
namespaced process to act outside the namespace with the same
privileges as it would have inside it.  This is particularly
damaging in the common case of running as root within the namespace.

When user namespace creation is disallowed, attempting to create a
user namespace fails with "no space left on device" (ENOSPC).
root may re-enable user namespace creation at runtime.

options.title: security.apparmor.enable
options.description:
Whether to enable the AppArmor Mandatory Access Control system.

If you're enabling this module on a running system,
note that a reboot will be required to activate AppArmor in the kernel.

Also, beware that enabling this module privileges stability over security
by not trying to kill unconfined but newly confinable running processes by default,
though it would be needed because AppArmor can only confine new
or already confined processes of an executable.
This killing would for instance be necessary when upgrading to a NixOS revision
introducing for the first time an AppArmor profile for the executable
of a running process.

Enable [](#opt-security.apparmor.killUnconfinedConfinables)
if you want this service to do such killing
by sending a `SIGTERM` to those running processes.

options.title: security.apparmor.enableCache
options.description:
Whether to enable caching of AppArmor policies
in `/var/cache/apparmor/`.

Beware that AppArmor policies almost always contain Nix store paths,
and thus produce at each change of these paths
a new cached version accumulating in the cache.

options.title: security.apparmor.includes
options.type: attribute set of strings concatenated with "\n"
options.description:
List of paths to be added to AppArmor's searched paths
when resolving `include` directives.

options.title: security.apparmor.killUnconfinedConfinables
options.description:
Whether to enable killing of processes which have an AppArmor profile enabled
(in [](#opt-security.apparmor.policies))
but are not confined (because AppArmor can only confine new processes).

This is only sending a gracious `SIGTERM` signal to the processes,
not a `SIGKILL`.

Beware that due to a current limitation of AppArmor,
only profiles with exact paths (and no name) can enable such kills.

options.title: security.apparmor.packages
options.description: List of packages to be added to AppArmor's include path

options.title: security.apparmor.policies
options.description: AppArmor policies.

options.title: security.apparmor.policies.<name>.path
options.description: A path of a profile file to include. Incompatible with profile.

options.title: security.apparmor.policies.<name>.profile
options.description: The profile file contents. Incompatible with path.

options.title: security.apparmor.policies.<name>.state
options.description: How strictly this policy should be enforced

options.title: security.audit.backlogLimit
options.description:
The maximum number of outstanding audit buffers allowed; exceeding this is
considered a failure and handled in a manner specified by failureMode.

options.title: security.audit.enable
options.description:
Whether to enable the Linux audit system. The special `lock` value can be used to
enable auditing and prevent disabling it until a restart. Be careful about locking
this, as it will prevent you from changing your audit configuration until you
restart. If possible, test your configuration using build-vm beforehand.

options.title: security.audit.failureMode
options.description: How to handle critical errors in the auditing system

options.title: security.audit.rateLimit
options.description:
The maximum messages per second permitted before triggering a failure as
specified by failureMode. Setting it to zero disables the limit.

options.title: security.audit.rules
options.description: The ordered audit rules, with each string appearing as one line of the audit.rules file.

options.title: security.auditd.enable
options.description: Whether to enable the Linux Audit daemon.

options.title: security.auditd.plugins
options.description: Plugin definitions to register with auditd

options.title: security.auditd.plugins.<name>.active
options.description: Whether to enable Whether to enable this plugin.

options.title: security.auditd.plugins.<name>.args
options.description:
This allows you to pass arguments to the child program.
Generally plugins do not take arguments and have their own
config file that instructs them how they should be configured.

options.title: security.auditd.plugins.<name>.direction
options.description:
The option is dictated by the plugin. In or out are the only choices.
You cannot make a plugin operate in a way it wasn't  designed just by
changing this option. This option is to give a clue to the event dispatcher
about which direction events flow.

::: {.note}
Inbound events are not supported yet.
:::

options.title: security.auditd.plugins.<name>.format
options.description:
Binary passes the data exactly as the audit event dispatcher gets it from
the audit daemon. The string option tells the dispatcher to completely change
the event into a string suitable for parsing with the audit parsing library.

options.title: security.auditd.plugins.<name>.path
options.description: This is the absolute path to the plugin executable.

options.title: security.auditd.plugins.<name>.settings
options.type: null or (open submodule of attribute set of (null or boolean or non-empty string or absolute path or signed integer))
options.description: Plugin-specific config file to link to /etc/audit/<plugin>.conf

options.title: security.auditd.plugins.<name>.type
options.description:
This tells the dispatcher how the plugin wants to be run. There is only
one valid option, `always`, which means the plugin is external and should
always be run. The default is `always` since there are no more builtin plugins.

options.title: security.auditd.settings
options.type: open submodule of attribute set of (null or boolean or non-empty string or absolute path or signed integer)
options.description: auditd configuration file contents. See {auditd.conf} for supported values.

options.title: security.auditd.settings.admin_space_left
options.type: signed integer or string matching the pattern [0-9]+%
options.description:
This is a numeric value in mebibytes (MiB) that tells the audit daemon when to perform a configurable action because the system is running
low on disk space. This should be considered the last chance to do something before running out of disk space. The numeric value for
this parameter should be lower than the number for {option}`space_left`. You may also append a percent sign (e.g. 1%) to the number to have
the audit daemon calculate the number based on the disk partition size.

options.title: security.auditd.settings.space_left
options.type: signed integer or string matching the pattern [0-9]+%
options.description:
If the free space in the filesystem containing log_file drops below this value, the audit daemon takes the action specified by
{option}`space_left_action`. If the value of {option}`space_left` is specified as a whole number, it is interpreted as an absolute size in mebibytes
(MiB). If the value is specified as a number between 1 and 99 followed by a percentage sign (e.g., 5%), the audit daemon calculates
the absolute size in megabytes based on the size of the filesystem containing {option}`log_file`. (E.g., if the filesystem containing
{option}`log_file` is 2 gibibytes in size, and {option}`space_left` is set to 25%, then the audit daemon sets {option}`space_left` to approximately 500 mebibytes.

::: {.note}
This calculation is performed when the audit daemon starts, so if you resize the filesystem containing {option}`log_file` while the
audit daemon is running, you should send the audit daemon SIGHUP to re-read the configuration file and recalculate the correct per‐
centage.
:::

options.title: security.chromiumSuidSandbox.enable
options.description:
Whether to install the Chromium SUID sandbox which is an executable that
Chromium may use in order to achieve sandboxing.

If you get the error "The SUID sandbox helper binary was found, but is not
configured correctly.", turning this on might help.

Also, if the URL chrome://sandbox tells you that "You are not adequately
sandboxed!", turning this on might resolve the issue.

options.title: security.dhparams.defaultBitSize
options.description:
This allows to override the default bit size for all of the
Diffie-Hellman parameters set in
{option}`security.dhparams.params`.

options.title: security.dhparams.enable
options.description: Whether to generate new DH params and clean up old DH params.

options.title: security.dhparams.params
options.type: attribute set of ((submodule) or signed integer convertible to it)
options.description:
Diffie-Hellman parameters to generate.

The value is the size (in bits) of the DH params to generate. The
generated DH params path can be found in
`config.security.dhparams.params.«name».path`.

::: {.note}
The name of the DH params is taken as being the name of
the service it serves and the params will be generated before the
said service is started.
:::

::: {.warning}
If you are removing all dhparams from this list, you
have to leave {option}`security.dhparams.enable` for at
least one activation in order to have them be cleaned up. This also
means if you rollback to a version without any dhparams the
existing ones won't be cleaned up. Of course this only applies if
{option}`security.dhparams.stateful` is
`true`.
:::

::: {.note}
**For module implementers:** It's recommended
to not set a specific bit size here, so that users can easily
override this by setting
{option}`security.dhparams.defaultBitSize`.
:::

options.title: security.dhparams.params.<name>.bits
options.description:
The bit size for the prime that is used during a Diffie-Hellman
key exchange.

options.title: security.dhparams.params.<name>.path
options.description:
The resulting path of the generated Diffie-Hellman parameters
file for other services to reference. This could be either a
store path or a file inside the directory specified by
{option}`security.dhparams.path`.

options.title: security.dhparams.path
options.description:
Path to the directory in which Diffie-Hellman parameters will be
stored. This only is relevant if
{option}`security.dhparams.stateful` is
`true`.

options.title: security.dhparams.stateful
options.description:
Whether generation of Diffie-Hellman parameters should be stateful or
not. If this is enabled, PEM-encoded files for Diffie-Hellman
parameters are placed in the directory specified by
{option}`security.dhparams.path`. Otherwise the files are
created within the Nix store.

::: {.note}
If this is `false` the resulting store
path will be non-deterministic and will be rebuilt every time the
`openssl` package changes.
:::

options.title: security.doas.enable
options.description:
Whether to enable the {command}`doas` command, which allows
non-root users to execute commands as root.

options.title: security.doas.extraConfig
options.description:
Extra configuration text appended to {file}`doas.conf`. Be aware that
this option cannot be used to override the behaviour allowing
passwordless operation for root.

options.title: security.doas.extraRules
options.description:
Define specific rules to be set in the
{file}`/etc/doas.conf` file. More specific rules should
come after more general ones in order to yield the expected behavior.
You can use `mkBefore` and/or `mkAfter` to ensure
this is the case when configuration options are merged. Be aware that
this option cannot be used to override the behaviour allowing
passwordless operation for root.

options.title: security.doas.extraRules.*.args
options.description:
Arguments that must be provided to the command. When set to
`[]`, the command must be run without any arguments.

options.title: security.doas.extraRules.*.cmd
options.description:
The command the user is allowed to run. When set to
`null` (the default), all commands are allowed.

NOTE: It is best practice to specify absolute paths. If a
relative path is specified, only a restricted PATH will be
searched.

options.title: security.doas.extraRules.*.groups
options.description: The groups / GIDs this rule should apply for.

options.title: security.doas.extraRules.*.keepEnv
options.description:
If `true`, environment variables other than those
listed in
{manpage}`doas(1)`
are kept when creating the environment for the new process.

options.title: security.doas.extraRules.*.noLog
options.description:
If `true`, successful executions will not be logged
to
{manpage}`syslogd(8)`.

options.title: security.doas.extraRules.*.noPass
options.description:
If `true`, the user is not required to enter a
password.

options.title: security.doas.extraRules.*.persist
options.description:
If `true`, do not ask for a password again for some
time after the user successfully authenticates.

options.title: security.doas.extraRules.*.runAs
options.description:
Which user or group the specified command is allowed to run as.
When set to `null` (the default), all users are
allowed.

A user can be specified using just the username:
`"foo"`. It is also possible to only allow running as
a specific group with `":bar"`.

options.title: security.doas.extraRules.*.setEnv
options.description:
Keep or set the specified variables. Variables may also be
removed with a leading '-' or set using
`variable=value`. If the first character of
`value` is a '$', the value to be set is taken from
the existing environment variable of the indicated name. This
option is processed after the default environment has been
created.

NOTE: All rules have `setenv { SSH_AUTH_SOCK }` by
default. To prevent `SSH_AUTH_SOCK` from being
inherited, add `"-SSH_AUTH_SOCK"` anywhere in this
list.

options.title: security.doas.extraRules.*.users
options.description: The usernames / UIDs this rule should apply for.

options.title: security.doas.package
options.description: The doas package to use.

options.title: security.doas.wheelNeedsPassword
options.description:
Whether users of the `wheel` group must provide a password to
run commands as super user via {command}`doas`.

options.title: security.duosec.acceptEnvFactor
options.description:
Look for factor selection or passcode in the
`$DUO_PASSCODE` environment variable before
prompting the user for input.

When $DUO_PASSCODE is non-empty, it will override
autopush. The SSH client will need SendEnv DUO_PASSCODE in
its configuration, and the SSH server will similarly need
AcceptEnv DUO_PASSCODE.

options.title: security.duosec.allowTcpForwarding
options.description:
By default, when SSH forwarding, enabling Duo Security will
disable TCP forwarding. By enabling this, you potentially
undermine some of the SSH based login security. Note this is
not needed if you use PAM.

options.title: security.duosec.autopush
options.description:
If `true`, Duo Unix will automatically send
a push login request to the user’s phone, falling back on a
phone call if push is unavailable. If
`false`, the user will be prompted to
choose an authentication method. When configured with
`autopush = yes`, we recommend setting
`prompts = 1`.

options.title: security.duosec.failmode
options.description:
On service or configuration errors that prevent Duo
authentication, fail "safe" (allow access) or "secure" (deny
access). The default is "safe".

options.title: security.duosec.fallbackLocalIP
options.description:
Duo Unix reports the IP address of the authorizing user, for
the purposes of authorization and whitelisting. If Duo Unix
cannot detect the IP address of the client, setting
`fallbackLocalIP = yes` will cause Duo Unix
to send the IP address of the server it is running on.

If you are using IP whitelisting, enabling this option could
cause unauthorized logins if the local IP is listed in the
whitelist.

options.title: security.duosec.groups
options.description:
If specified, Duo authentication is required only for users
whose primary group or supplementary group list matches one
of the space-separated pattern lists. Refer to
<https://duo.com/docs/duounix> for details.

options.title: security.duosec.host
options.description: Duo API hostname.

options.title: security.duosec.integrationKey
options.description: Integration key.

options.title: security.duosec.motd
options.description:
Print the contents of `/etc/motd` to screen
after a successful login.

options.title: security.duosec.pam.enable
options.description: If enabled, protect logins with Duo Security using PAM support.

options.title: security.duosec.prompts
options.description:
If a user fails to authenticate with a second factor, Duo
Unix will prompt the user to authenticate again. This option
sets the maximum number of prompts that Duo Unix will
display before denying access. Must be 1, 2, or 3. Default
is 3.

For example, when `prompts = 1`, the user
will have to successfully authenticate on the first prompt,
whereas if `prompts = 2`, if the user
enters incorrect information at the initial prompt, he/she
will be prompted to authenticate again.

When configured with `autopush = true`, we
recommend setting `prompts = 1`.

options.title: security.duosec.pushinfo
options.description:
Include information such as the command to be executed in
the Duo Push message.

options.title: security.duosec.secretKeyFile
options.description: A file containing your secret key. The security of your Duo application is tied to the security of your secret key.

options.title: security.duosec.ssh.enable
options.description: If enabled, protect SSH logins with Duo Security.

options.title: security.enableWrappers
options.description: Whether to enable SUID/SGID wrappers.

options.title: security.forcePageTableIsolation
options.description:
Whether to force-enable the Page Table Isolation (PTI) Linux kernel
feature even on CPU models that claim to be safe from Meltdown.

This hardening feature is most beneficial to systems that run untrusted
workloads that rely on address space isolation for security.

options.title: security.googleOsLogin.enable
options.description:
Whether to enable Google OS Login.

The OS Login package enables the following components:
AuthorizedKeysCommand to query valid SSH keys from the user's OS Login
profile during ssh authentication phase.
NSS Module to provide user and group information
PAM Module for the sshd service, providing authorization and
authentication support, allowing the system to use data stored in
Google Cloud IAM permissions to control both, the ability to log into
an instance, and to perform operations as root (sudo).

options.title: security.ipa.basedn
options.description: Base DN to use when performing LDAP operations.

options.title: security.ipa.cacheCredentials
options.description: Whether to cache credentials.

options.title: security.ipa.certificate
options.description:
IPA server CA certificate.

Use `nix-prefetch-url http://$server/ipa/config/ca.crt` to
obtain the file and the hash.

options.title: security.ipa.chromiumSupport
options.description: Whether to whitelist the FreeIPA domain in Chromium.

options.title: security.ipa.domain
options.description: Domain of the IPA server.

options.title: security.ipa.dyndns.enable
options.description: Whether to enable FreeIPA automatic hostname updates.

options.title: security.ipa.dyndns.interface
options.description: Network interface to perform hostname updates through.

options.title: security.ipa.enable
options.description: Whether to enable FreeIPA domain integration.

options.title: security.ipa.ifpAllowedUids
options.description: A list of users allowed to access the ifp dbus interface.

options.title: security.ipa.ipaHostname
options.description: Fully-qualified hostname used to identify this host in the IPA domain.
options.default:
if config.networking.domain != null then config.networking.fqdn
else "${networking.hostName}.${security.ipa.domain}"

options.title: security.ipa.offlinePasswords
options.description: Whether to store offline passwords when the server is down.

options.title: security.ipa.realm
options.description: Kerberos realm.

options.title: security.ipa.server
options.description: IPA Server hostname.

options.title: security.ipa.shells
options.description:
List of shells which binaries should be installed to /bin/<name>.

FreeIPA typicly configures somesthing like /bin/bash into the users shell attribute.

options.title: security.ipa.useAsTimeserver
options.description: Whether to add the IPA server to the timeserver.

options.title: security.isolate.boxRoot
options.description:
All sandboxes are created under this directory.
To avoid symlink attacks, this directory and all its ancestors
must be writeable only by root.

options.title: security.isolate.cgRoot
options.description:
Control group which subgroups are placed under.
Either an explicit path to a subdirectory in cgroupfs, or "auto:file" to read
the path from "file", where it is put by `isolate-cg-helper`.

options.title: security.isolate.enable
options.description:
Whether to enable Sandbox for securely executing untrusted programs
.

options.title: security.isolate.extraConfig
options.description: Extra configuration to append to the configuration file.

options.title: security.isolate.firstGid
options.type: integer or floating point number between 1000 and 65533 (both inclusive)
options.description: Start of block of GIDs reserved for sandboxes.

options.title: security.isolate.firstUid
options.type: integer or floating point number between 1000 and 65533 (both inclusive)
options.description: Start of block of UIDs reserved for sandboxes.

options.title: security.isolate.lockRoot
options.description: Directory where lock files are created.

options.title: security.isolate.numBoxes
options.type: integer or floating point number between 1000 and 65533 (both inclusive)
options.description:
Number of UIDs and GIDs to reserve, starting from
{option}`firstUid` and {option}`firstGid`.

options.title: security.isolate.package
options.description: The isolate-unwrapped package to use.

options.title: security.isolate.restrictedInit
options.description: If true, only root can create sandboxes.

options.title: security.krb5.enable
options.description: Enable and configure Kerberos utilities

options.title: security.krb5.package
options.description: The krb5 package to use.

options.title: security.krb5.settings
options.type: open submodule of attribute set of attribute set of ((list of attribute set of ((list of (signed integer or string or boolean)) or signed integer or string or boolean)) or attribute set of ((list of (signed integer or string or boolean)) or signed integer or string or boolean) or (list of (signed integer or string or boolean)) or signed integer or string or boolean)
options.description:
Structured contents of the {file}`krb5.conf` file. See
{manpage}`krb5.conf(5)` for details about configuration.

options.title: security.krb5.settings.include
options.type: (list of absolute path) or absolute path convertible to it
options.description: Files to include in the Kerberos configuration.

options.title: security.krb5.settings.includedir
options.type: (list of absolute path) or absolute path convertible to it
options.description: Directories containing files to include in the Kerberos configuration.

options.title: security.krb5.settings.module
options.type: (list of absolute path) or absolute path convertible to it
options.description: Modules to obtain Kerberos configuration from.

options.title: security.lockKernelModules
options.description:
Disable kernel module loading once the system is fully initialised.
Module loading is disabled until the next reboot. Problems caused
by delayed module loading can be fixed by adding the module(s) in
question to {option}`boot.kernelModules`.

options.title: security.loginDefs.chfnRestrict
options.description: Use chfn SUID to allow non-root users to change their account GECOS information.

options.title: security.loginDefs.package
options.description: The shadow package to use.

options.title: security.loginDefs.settings
options.type: open submodule of attribute set of (atom (null, bool, int, float or string))
options.description:
Config options for the /etc/login.defs file, that defines
the site-specific configuration for the shadow password suite.
See {manpage}`login.defs(5)` man page for available options.

options.title: security.loginDefs.settings.DEFAULT_HOME
options.description: Indicate if login is allowed if we can't cd to the home directory.

options.title: security.loginDefs.settings.ENCRYPT_METHOD
options.description: This defines the system default encryption algorithm for encrypting passwords.

options.title: security.loginDefs.settings.GID_MAX
options.type: 32 bit unsigned integer; between 0 and 4294967295 (both inclusive)
options.description: Range of group IDs used for the creation of regular groups by useradd, groupadd, or newusers.

options.title: security.loginDefs.settings.GID_MIN
options.type: 32 bit unsigned integer; between 0 and 4294967295 (both inclusive)
options.description: Range of group IDs used for the creation of regular groups by useradd, groupadd, or newusers.

options.title: security.loginDefs.settings.SYS_GID_MAX
options.type: 32 bit unsigned integer; between 0 and 4294967295 (both inclusive)
options.description: Range of group IDs used for the creation of system groups by useradd, groupadd, or newusers

options.title: security.loginDefs.settings.SYS_GID_MIN
options.type: 32 bit unsigned integer; between 0 and 4294967295 (both inclusive)
options.description: Range of group IDs used for the creation of system groups by useradd, groupadd, or newusers

options.title: security.loginDefs.settings.SYS_UID_MAX
options.type: 32 bit unsigned integer; between 0 and 4294967295 (both inclusive)
options.description: Range of user IDs used for the creation of system users by useradd or newusers.

options.title: security.loginDefs.settings.SYS_UID_MIN
options.type: 32 bit unsigned integer; between 0 and 4294967295 (both inclusive)
options.description: Range of user IDs used for the creation of system users by useradd or newusers.

options.title: security.loginDefs.settings.TTYGROUP
options.description:
The terminal permissions: the login tty will be owned by the TTYGROUP group,
and the permissions will be set to TTYPERM

options.title: security.loginDefs.settings.TTYPERM
options.description:
The terminal permissions: the login tty will be owned by the TTYGROUP group,
and the permissions will be set to TTYPERM

options.title: security.loginDefs.settings.UID_MAX
options.type: 32 bit unsigned integer; between 0 and 4294967295 (both inclusive)
options.description: Range of user IDs used for the creation of regular users by useradd or newusers.

options.title: security.loginDefs.settings.UID_MIN
options.type: 32 bit unsigned integer; between 0 and 4294967295 (both inclusive)
options.description: Range of user IDs used for the creation of regular users by useradd or newusers.

options.title: security.loginDefs.settings.UMASK
options.description: The file mode creation mask is initialized to this value.

options.title: security.lsm
options.description: A list of the LSMs to initialize in order.

options.title: security.pam.dp9ik.authserver
options.description:
This controls the hostname for the 9front authentication server
that users will be authenticated against.

options.title: security.pam.dp9ik.control
options.description: This option sets the pam "control" used for this module.

options.title: security.pam.dp9ik.enable
options.description:
Whether to enable the dp9ik pam module provided by tlsclient.

If set, users can be authenticated against the 9front
authentication server given in {option}`security.pam.dp9ik.authserver`
.

options.title: security.pam.enableEcryptfs
options.description: Whether to enable eCryptfs PAM module (mounting ecryptfs home directory on login).

options.title: security.pam.enableFscrypt
options.description:
Whether to enable fscrypt, to automatically unlock directories with the user's login password.

This also enables a service at security.pam.services.fscrypt which is used by
fscrypt to verify the user's password when setting up a new protector. If you
use something other than pam_unix to verify user passwords, please remember to
adjust this PAM service
.

options.title: security.pam.enableOTPW
options.description: Whether to enable the OTPW (one-time password) PAM module.

options.title: security.pam.enableUMask
options.description: Whether to enable umask PAM module.

options.title: security.pam.krb5.enable
options.description:
Enables Kerberos PAM modules (`pam-krb5`,
`pam-ccreds`).

If set, users can authenticate with their Kerberos password.
This requires a valid Kerberos configuration
(`security.krb5.enable` should be set to `true`).

Note that the Kerberos PAM modules are not necessary when using SSS
to handle Kerberos authentication.

options.title: security.pam.loginLimits
options.description:
Define resource limits that should apply to users or groups.
Each item in the list should be an attribute set with a
{var}`domain`, {var}`type`,
{var}`item`, and {var}`value`
attribute.  The syntax and semantics of these attributes
must be that described in {manpage}`limits.conf(5)`.

Note that these limits do not apply to systemd services,
whose limits can be changed via {option}`systemd.settings.Manager`
instead.

options.title: security.pam.loginLimits.*.domain
options.description: Username, groupname, or wildcard this limit applies to

options.title: security.pam.loginLimits.*.item
options.description: Item this limit applies to

options.title: security.pam.loginLimits.*.type
options.description: Type of this limit

options.title: security.pam.loginLimits.*.value
options.description: Value of this limit

options.title: security.pam.makeHomeDir.skelDirectory
options.description:
Path to skeleton directory whose contents are copied to home
directories newly created by `pam_mkhomedir`.

options.title: security.pam.makeHomeDir.umask
options.description:
The user file mode creation mask to use on home directories
newly created by `pam_mkhomedir`.

options.title: security.pam.mount.additionalSearchPaths
options.description:
Additional programs to include in the search path of pam_mount.
Useful for example if you want to use some FUSE filesystems like bindfs.

options.title: security.pam.mount.createMountPoints
options.description: Create mountpoints for volumes if they do not exist.

options.title: security.pam.mount.cryptMountOptions
options.description:
Global mount options that apply to every crypt volume.
You can define volume-specific options in the volume definitions.

options.title: security.pam.mount.debugLevel
options.description:
Sets the Debug-Level. 0 disables debugging, 1 enables pam_mount tracing,
and 2 additionally enables tracing in mount.crypt. The default is 0.
For more information, visit <https://pam-mount.sourceforge.net/pam_mount.conf.5.html>.

options.title: security.pam.mount.enable
options.description: Enable PAM mount system to mount filesystems on user login.

options.title: security.pam.mount.extraVolumes
options.description:
List of volume definitions for pam_mount.
For more information, visit <https://pam-mount.sourceforge.net/pam_mount.conf.5.html>.

options.title: security.pam.mount.fuseMountOptions
options.description:
Global mount options that apply to every FUSE volume.
You can define volume-specific options in the volume definitions.

options.title: security.pam.mount.logoutHup
options.description: Kill remaining processes after logout by sending a SIGHUP.

options.title: security.pam.mount.logoutKill
options.description: Kill remaining processes after logout by sending a SIGKILL.

options.title: security.pam.mount.logoutTerm
options.description: Kill remaining processes after logout by sending a SIGTERM.

options.title: security.pam.mount.logoutWait
options.description:
Amount of microseconds to wait until killing remaining processes after
final logout.
For more information, visit <https://pam-mount.sourceforge.net/pam_mount.conf.5.html>.

options.title: security.pam.mount.removeCreatedMountPoints
options.description:
Remove mountpoints created by pam_mount after logout. This
only affects mountpoints that have been created by pam_mount
in the same session.

options.title: security.pam.oath.digits
options.description:
Specify the lib.length of the one-time password in number of
digits.

options.title: security.pam.oath.enable
options.description: Enable the OATH (one-time password) PAM module.

options.title: security.pam.oath.usersFile
options.description:
Set the path to file where the user's credentials are
stored. This file must not be world readable!

options.title: security.pam.oath.window
options.description:
Specify the number of one-time passwords to check in order
to accommodate for situations where the system and the
client are slightly out of sync (iteration for HOTP or time
steps for TOTP).

options.title: security.pam.p11.control
options.description:
This option sets pam "control".
If you want to have multi factor authentication, use "required".
If you want to use the PKCS#11 device instead of the regular password,
use "sufficient".

Read
{manpage}`pam.conf(5)`
for better understanding of this option.

options.title: security.pam.p11.enable
options.description:
Enables P11 PAM (`pam_p11`) module.

If set, users can log in with SSH keys and PKCS#11 tokens.

More information can be found [here](https://github.com/OpenSC/pam_p11).

options.title: security.pam.package
options.description: The pam package to use.

options.title: security.pam.rssh.enable
options.description: Whether to enable authenticating using a signature performed by the ssh-agent.

options.title: security.pam.rssh.settings
options.type: open submodule of attribute set of (null or boolean or string or signed integer or path in the Nix store)
options.description:
Options to pass to the pam_rssh module. Refer to
<https://github.com/z4yx/pam_rssh/blob/main/README.md#optional-arguments>
for supported values.

Boolean values render just the key if true, and nothing if false.
Null values are ignored.
All other values are rendered as key-value pairs.

options.title: security.pam.rssh.settings.auth_key_file
options.description:
Path to file with trusted public keys in OpenSSH's `authorized_keys` format. The following
variables are expanded to the respective PAM items:

- `service`: `PAM_SERVICE`, the service name,
- `user`: `PAM_USER`, the username of the entity under whose identity service will be given,
- `tty`: `PAM_TTY`, the terminal name,
- `rhost`: `PAM_RHOST`, the requesting hostname, and
- `ruser`: `PAM_RUSER`, the requesting entity.

These PAM items are explained in {manpage}`pam_get_item(3)`.

Variables may be specified as `$var`, `${var}` or `${var:defaultValue}`.

::: {.note}
Specifying user-writeable files here results in an insecure configuration: a malicious process
can then edit such an `authorized_keys` file and bypass the ssh-agent-based authentication.

This option is ignored if {option}`security.pam.rssh.settings.authorized_keys_command` is set.

If both this option and {option}`security.pam.rssh.settings.authorized_keys_command` are unset,
the keys will be read from `${HOME}/.ssh/authorized_keys`, which should be considered
insecure.

options.title: security.pam.services
options.description:
This option defines the PAM services.  A service typically
corresponds to a program that uses PAM,
e.g. {command}`login` or {command}`passwd`.
Each attribute of this set defines a PAM service, with the attribute name
defining the name of the service.

options.title: security.pam.services.<name>.allowNullPassword
options.description:
Whether to allow logging into accounts that have no password
set (i.e., have an empty password field in
{file}`/etc/passwd` or
{file}`/etc/group`).  This does not enable
logging into disabled accounts (i.e., that have the password
field set to `!`).  Note that regardless of
what the pam_unix documentation says, accounts with hashed
empty passwords are always allowed to log in.

options.title: security.pam.services.<name>.duoSecurity.enable
options.description:
If set, use the Duo Security pam module
`pam_duo` for authentication.  Requires
configuration of {option}`security.duosec` options.

options.title: security.pam.services.<name>.enable
options.description: Whether to enable this PAM service.

options.title: security.pam.services.<name>.enableAppArmor
options.description:
Enable support for attaching AppArmor profiles at the
user/group level, e.g., as part of a role based access
control scheme.

options.title: security.pam.services.<name>.enableGnomeKeyring
options.description:
If enabled, pam_gnome_keyring will attempt to automatically unlock the
user's default Gnome keyring upon login. If the user login password does
not match their keyring password, Gnome Keyring will prompt separately
after login.

options.title: security.pam.services.<name>.enableUMask
options.description: If enabled, the pam_umask module will be loaded.

options.title: security.pam.services.<name>.failDelay.delay
options.description: The delay time (in microseconds) on failure.

options.title: security.pam.services.<name>.failDelay.enable
options.description:
If enabled, this will replace the `FAIL_DELAY` setting from `login.defs`.
Change the delay on failure per-application.

options.title: security.pam.services.<name>.forwardXAuth
options.description:
Whether X authentication keys should be passed from the
calling user to the target user (e.g. for
{command}`su`)

options.title: security.pam.services.<name>.fprintAuth
options.description:
If set, fingerprint reader will be used (if exists and
your fingerprints are enrolled).

options.title: security.pam.services.<name>.gnupg.enable
options.description:
If enabled, pam_gnupg will attempt to automatically unlock the
user's GPG keys with the login password via
{command}`gpg-agent`. The keygrips of all keys to be
unlocked should be written to {file}`~/.pam-gnupg`,
and can be queried with {command}`gpg -K --with-keygrip`.
Presetting passphrases must be enabled by adding
`allow-preset-passphrase` in
{file}`~/.gnupg/gpg-agent.conf`.

options.title: security.pam.services.<name>.gnupg.noAutostart
options.description:
Don't start {command}`gpg-agent` if it is not running.
Useful in conjunction with starting {command}`gpg-agent` as
a systemd user service.

options.title: security.pam.services.<name>.gnupg.storeOnly
options.description:
Don't send the password immediately after login, but store for PAM
`session`.

options.title: security.pam.services.<name>.googleAuthenticator.allowNullOTP
options.description:
Whether to allow login for accounts that have no OTP set
(i.e., accounts with no OTP configured or no existing
{file}`~/.google_authenticator`).

options.title: security.pam.services.<name>.googleAuthenticator.enable
options.description:
If set, users with enabled Google Authenticator (created
{file}`~/.google_authenticator`) will be required
to provide Google Authenticator token to log in.

options.title: security.pam.services.<name>.googleAuthenticator.forwardPass
options.description:
The authentication provides a single field requiring
the user's password followed by the one-time password (OTP).

options.title: security.pam.services.<name>.googleOsLoginAccountVerification
options.description:
If set, will use the Google OS Login PAM modules
(`pam_oslogin_login`,
`pam_oslogin_admin`) to verify possible OS Login
users and set sudoers configuration accordingly.
This only makes sense to enable for the `sshd` PAM
service.

options.title: security.pam.services.<name>.googleOsLoginAuthentication
options.description:
If set, will use the `pam_oslogin_login`'s user
authentication methods to authenticate users using 2FA.
This only makes sense to enable for the `sshd` PAM
service.

options.title: security.pam.services.<name>.kwallet.enable
options.description:
If enabled, pam_wallet will attempt to automatically unlock the
user's default KDE wallet upon login. If the user has no wallet named
"kdewallet", or the login password does not match their wallet
password, KDE will prompt separately after login.

options.title: security.pam.services.<name>.kwallet.forceRun
options.description:
The `force_run` option is used to tell the PAM module for KWallet
to forcefully run even if no graphical session (such as a GUI
display manager) is detected. This is useful for when you are
starting an X Session or a Wayland Session from a TTY. If you
intend to log-in from a TTY, it is recommended that you enable
this option **and** ensure that `plasma-kwallet-pam.service` is
started by `graphical-session.target`.

options.title: security.pam.services.<name>.kwallet.package
options.description: The kwallet-pam package to use.

options.title: security.pam.services.<name>.limits
options.description:
Attribute set describing resource limits.  Defaults to the
value of {option}`security.pam.loginLimits`.
The meaning of the values is explained in {manpage}`limits.conf(5)`.

options.title: security.pam.services.<name>.limits.*.domain
options.description: Username, groupname, or wildcard this limit applies to

options.title: security.pam.services.<name>.limits.*.item
options.description: Item this limit applies to

options.title: security.pam.services.<name>.limits.*.type
options.description: Type of this limit

options.title: security.pam.services.<name>.limits.*.value
options.description: Value of this limit

options.title: security.pam.services.<name>.logFailures
options.description: Whether to log authentication failures in {file}`/var/log/faillog`.

options.title: security.pam.services.<name>.makeHomeDir
options.description:
Whether to try to create home directories for users
with `$HOME`s pointing to nonexistent
locations on session login.

options.title: security.pam.services.<name>.mysqlAuth
options.description:
If set, the `pam_mysql` module will be used to
authenticate users against a MySQL/MariaDB database.

options.title: security.pam.services.<name>.name
options.description: Name of the PAM service.

options.title: security.pam.services.<name>.nodelay
options.description: Whether the delay after typing a wrong password should be disabled.

options.title: security.pam.services.<name>.oathAuth
options.description: If set, the OATH Toolkit will be used.

options.title: security.pam.services.<name>.otpwAuth
options.description:
If set, the OTPW system will be used (if
{file}`~/.otpw` exists).

options.title: security.pam.services.<name>.p11Auth
options.description:
If set, keys listed in
{file}`~/.ssh/authorized_keys` and
{file}`~/.eid/authorized_certificates`
can be used to log in with the associated PKCS#11 tokens.

options.title: security.pam.services.<name>.pamMount
options.description: Enable PAM mount (pam_mount) system to mount filesystems on user login.

options.title: security.pam.services.<name>.requireWheel
options.description: Whether to permit root access only to members of group wheel.

options.title: security.pam.services.<name>.rootOK
options.description:
If set, root doesn't need to authenticate (e.g. for the
{command}`useradd` service).

options.title: security.pam.services.<name>.rssh
options.description:
If set, the calling user's SSH agent is used to authenticate
against the configured keys. This module works in a manner
similar to pam_ssh_agent_auth, but supports a wider range
of SSH key types, including those protected by security
keys (FIDO2).

options.title: security.pam.services.<name>.setEnvironment
options.description:
Whether the service should set the environment variables
listed in {option}`environment.sessionVariables`
using `pam_env.so`.

options.title: security.pam.services.<name>.setLoginUid
options.description:
Set the login uid of the process
({file}`/proc/self/loginuid`) for auditing
purposes.  The login uid is only set by ‘entry points’ like
{command}`login` and {command}`sshd`, not by
commands like {command}`sudo`.

options.title: security.pam.services.<name>.showMotd
options.description: Whether to show the message of the day.

options.title: security.pam.services.<name>.sshAgentAuth
options.description:
If set, the calling user's SSH agent is used to authenticate
against the keys in the calling user's
{file}`~/.ssh/authorized_keys`.  This is useful
for {command}`sudo` on password-less remote systems.

options.title: security.pam.services.<name>.sssdStrictAccess
options.description: enforce sssd access control

options.title: security.pam.services.<name>.startSession
options.description:
If set, the service will register a new session with
systemd's login manager.  For local sessions, this will give
the user access to audio devices, CD-ROM drives.  In the
default PolicyKit configuration, it also allows the user to
reboot the system.

options.title: security.pam.services.<name>.text
options.description: Contents of the PAM service file.

options.title: security.pam.services.<name>.ttyAudit.disablePattern
options.description:
For each user matching one of comma-separated
glob patterns, disable TTY auditing

options.title: security.pam.services.<name>.ttyAudit.enable
options.description: Enable or disable TTY auditing for specified users

options.title: security.pam.services.<name>.ttyAudit.enablePattern
options.description:
For each user matching one of comma-separated
glob patterns, enable TTY auditing

options.title: security.pam.services.<name>.ttyAudit.openOnly
options.description:
Set the TTY audit flag when opening the session,
but do not restore it when closing the session.
Using this option is necessary for some services
that don't fork() to run the authenticated session,
such as sudo.

options.title: security.pam.services.<name>.u2fAuth
options.description:
If set, users listed in
{file}`$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/Yubico/u2f_keys` (or
{file}`$HOME/.config/Yubico/u2f_keys` if XDG variable is
not set) are able to log in with the associated U2F key. Path can be
changed using {option}`security.pam.u2f.authFile` option.

options.title: security.pam.services.<name>.unixAuth
options.description:
Whether users can log in with passwords defined in
{file}`/etc/shadow`.

options.title: security.pam.services.<name>.updateWtmp
options.description: Whether to update {file}`/var/log/wtmp`.

options.title: security.pam.services.<name>.usshAuth
options.description:
If set, users with an SSH certificate containing an authorized principal
in their SSH agent are able to log in. Specific options are controlled
using the {option}`security.pam.ussh` options.

Note that the  {option}`security.pam.ussh.enable` must also be
set for this option to take effect.

options.title: security.pam.services.<name>.yubicoAuth
options.description:
If set, users listed in
{file}`~/.yubico/authorized_yubikeys`
are able to log in with the associated Yubikey tokens.

options.title: security.pam.services.<name>.zfs
options.description: Enable unlocking and mounting of encrypted ZFS home dataset at login.

options.title: security.pam.sshAgentAuth.authorizedKeysFiles
options.description:
A list of paths to files in OpenSSH's `authorized_keys` format, containing
the keys that will be trusted by the `pam_ssh_agent_auth` module.

The following patterns are expanded when interpreting the path:
- `%f` and `%H` respectively expand to the fully-qualified and short hostname ;
- `%u` expands to the username ;
- `~` or `%h` expands to the user's home directory.

::: {.note}
Specifying user-writeable files here result in an insecure configuration:  a malicious process
can then edit such an authorized_keys file and bypass the ssh-agent-based authentication.

See [issue #31611](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/issues/31611)
:::

options.title: security.pam.sshAgentAuth.enable
options.description:
Whether to enable authenticating using a signature performed by the ssh-agent.
This allows using SSH keys exclusively, instead of passwords, for instance on remote machines
.

options.title: security.pam.u2f.control
options.description:
This option sets pam "control".
If you want to have multi factor authentication, use "required".
If you want to use U2F device instead of regular password, use "sufficient".

Read
{manpage}`pam.conf(5)`
for better understanding of this option.

options.title: security.pam.u2f.enable
options.description:
Enables U2F PAM (`pam-u2f`) module.

If set, users listed in
{file}`$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/Yubico/u2f_keys` (or
{file}`$HOME/.config/Yubico/u2f_keys` if XDG variable is
not set) are able to log in with the associated U2F key. The path can
be changed using {option}`security.pam.u2f.authFile` option.

File format is:
```
<username1>:<KeyHandle1>,<UserKey1>,<CoseType1>,<Options1>:<KeyHandle2>,<UserKey2>,<CoseType2>,<Options2>:...
<username2>:<KeyHandle1>,<UserKey1>,<CoseType1>,<Options1>:<KeyHandle2>,<UserKey2>,<CoseType2>,<Options2>:...
```
This file can be generated using {command}`pamu2fcfg` command.

More information can be found [here](https://developers.yubico.com/pam-u2f/).

options.title: security.pam.u2f.settings
options.type: open submodule of attribute set of (null or boolean or string or signed integer or path in the Nix store)
options.description:
Options to pass to the PAM module.

Boolean values render just the key if true, and nothing if false.
Null values are ignored.
All other values are rendered as key-value pairs.

options.title: security.pam.u2f.settings.appid
options.description:
By default `pam-u2f` module sets the application
ID to `pam://$HOSTNAME`.

When using {command}`pamu2fcfg`, you can specify your
application ID with the `-i` flag.

More information can be found [here](https://developers.yubico.com/pam-u2f/Manuals/pam_u2f.8.html)

options.title: security.pam.u2f.settings.authfile
options.description:
By default `pam-u2f` module reads the keys from
{file}`$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/Yubico/u2f_keys` (or
{file}`$HOME/.config/Yubico/u2f_keys` if XDG variable is
not set).

If you want to change auth file locations or centralize database (for
example use {file}`/etc/u2f-mappings`) you can set this
option.

File format is:
`username:first_keyHandle,first_public_key: second_keyHandle,second_public_key`
This file can be generated using {command}`pamu2fcfg` command.

More information can be found [here](https://developers.yubico.com/pam-u2f/).

options.title: security.pam.u2f.settings.cue
options.description:
By default `pam-u2f` module does not inform user
that he needs to use the u2f device, it just waits without a prompt.

If you set this option to `true`,
`cue` option is added to `pam-u2f`
module and reminder message will be displayed.

options.title: security.pam.u2f.settings.debug
options.description: Debug output to stderr.

options.title: security.pam.u2f.settings.interactive
options.description:
Set to prompt a message and wait before testing the presence of a U2F device.
Recommended if your device doesn’t have a tactile trigger.

options.title: security.pam.u2f.settings.origin
options.description:
By default `pam-u2f` module sets the origin
to `pam://$HOSTNAME`.
Setting origin to an host independent value will allow you to
reuse credentials across machines

When using {command}`pamu2fcfg`, you can specify your
application ID with the `-o` flag.

More information can be found [here](https://developers.yubico.com/pam-u2f/Manuals/pam_u2f.8.html)

options.title: security.pam.ussh.authorizedPrincipals
options.description:
Comma-separated list of authorized principals to permit; if the user
presents a certificate with one of these principals, then they will be
authorized.

Note that `pam-ussh` also requires that the certificate
contain a principal matching the user's username. The principals from
this list are in addition to those principals.

Mutually exclusive with `authorizedPrincipalsFile`.

options.title: security.pam.ussh.authorizedPrincipalsFile
options.description:
Path to a list of principals; if the user presents a certificate with
one of these principals, then they will be authorized.

Note that `pam-ussh` also requires that the certificate
contain a principal matching the user's username. The principals from
this file are in addition to those principals.

Mutually exclusive with `authorizedPrincipals`.

options.title: security.pam.ussh.caFile
options.description:
By default `pam-ussh` reads the trusted user CA keys
from {file}`/etc/ssh/trusted_user_ca`.

This should be set the same as your `TrustedUserCAKeys`
option for sshd.

options.title: security.pam.ussh.control
options.description:
This option sets pam "control".
If you want to have multi factor authentication, use "required".
If you want to use the SSH certificate instead of the regular password,
use "sufficient".

Read
{manpage}`pam.conf(5)`
for better understanding of this option.

options.title: security.pam.ussh.enable
options.description:
Enables Uber's USSH PAM (`pam-ussh`) module.

This is similar to `pam-ssh-agent`, except that
the presence of a CA-signed SSH key with a valid principal is checked
instead.

Note that this module must both be enabled using this option and on a
per-PAM-service level as well (using `usshAuth`).

More information can be found [here](https://github.com/uber/pam-ussh).

options.title: security.pam.ussh.group
options.description:
If set, then the authenticating user must be a member of this group
to use this module.

options.title: security.pam.yubico.challengeResponsePath
options.description:
If not null, set the path used by yubico pam module where the challenge expected response is stored.

More information can be found [here](https://developers.yubico.com/yubico-pam/Authentication_Using_Challenge-Response.html).

options.title: security.pam.yubico.control
options.description:
This option sets pam "control".
If you want to have multi factor authentication, use "required".
If you want to use Yubikey instead of regular password, use "sufficient".

Read
{manpage}`pam.conf(5)`
for better understanding of this option.

options.title: security.pam.yubico.debug
options.description: Debug output to stderr.

options.title: security.pam.yubico.enable
options.description:
Enables Yubico PAM (`yubico-pam`) module.

If set, users listed in
{file}`~/.yubico/authorized_yubikeys`
are able to log in with the associated Yubikey tokens.

The file must have only one line:
`username:yubikey_token_id1:yubikey_token_id2`
More information can be found [here](https://developers.yubico.com/yubico-pam/).

options.title: security.pam.yubico.id
options.description: client id

options.title: security.pam.yubico.mode
options.description:
Mode of operation.

Use "client" for online validation with a YubiKey validation service such as
the YubiCloud.

Use "challenge-response" for offline validation using YubiKeys with HMAC-SHA-1
Challenge-Response configurations. See the man-page {manpage}`ykpamcfg(1)` for further
details on how to configure offline Challenge-Response validation.

More information can be found [here](https://developers.yubico.com/yubico-pam/Authentication_Using_Challenge-Response.html).

options.title: security.pam.zfs.enable
options.description: Enable unlocking and mounting of encrypted ZFS home dataset at login.

options.title: security.pam.zfs.homes

Prefix of home datasets. This value will be concatenated with
`"/" + <username>` in order to determine the home dataset to unlock.

options.title: security.pam.zfs.mountRecursively

options.title: security.pam.zfs.noUnmount

options.title: security.pki.caBundle

A list of blacklisted CA certificate names that won't be imported from
the Mozilla Trust Store into
{file}`/etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt`. Use the
names from that file.
options.example:
[
  "WoSign"
  "WoSign China"
  "CA WoSign ECC Root"
  "Certification Authority of WoSign G2"
]

options.title: security.pki.certificateFiles
options.description:
A list of files containing trusted root certificates in PEM
format. These are concatenated to form
{file}`/etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt`, which is
used by many programs that use OpenSSL, such as
{command}`curl` and {command}`git`.

options.title: security.pki.certificates

options.title: security.pki.useCompatibleBundle
options.description:
Whether to enable usage of a compatibility bundle.

Such a bundle consists exclusively of `BEGIN CERTIFICATE` and no `BEGIN TRUSTED CERTIFICATE`,
which is an OpenSSL specific PEM format.

It is known to be incompatible with certain software stacks.

Nevertheless, enabling this will strip all additional trust rules provided by the
certificates themselves. This can have security consequences depending on your usecases
.

Enable the shadow authentication suite, which provides critical programs such as su, login, passwd.

options.title: security.tpm2.fapi.ekCertLess
options.description:
A switch to disable Endorsement Key (EK) certificate verification.

A value of null indicates that the generated fapi config file does not
contain a ek_cert_less key. The effect of not having that key at all is
the same as setting its value to false.

A value of false means that the tss2 cli will not work if there is no
EK Cert installed, or if the installed EK Cert can't be validated.

A value of true means that the tss2 cli will work even if there's no EK
cert installed.

options.title: security.tpm2.fapi.ekFingerprint
options.description:
The fingerprint of the endorsement key.

A value of null means that you have chosen not to specify the expected
fingerprint of the EK. You can still have an endorsement key, it just
won't get checked to see if it's fingerprint matches a particular value
before being used.

If not specified in the FAPI config it can be specified by environment

Configuration part of the device TCTI, e.g. the path to the TPM device.

The format is specified in the

options.title: security.unprivilegedUsernsClone
options.description:
When disabled, unprivileged users will not be able to create new namespaces.
By default unprivileged user namespaces are disabled.
This option only works in a hardened profile.

options.title: security.virtualisation.flushL1DataCache
options.description:
Whether the hypervisor should flush the L1 data cache before
entering guests.
See also [](#opt-security.allowSimultaneousMultithreading).

- `null`: uses the kernel default
- `"never"`: disables L1 data cache flushing entirely.
  May be appropriate if all guests are trusted.
- `"cond"`: flushes L1 data cache only for pre-determined
  code paths.  May leak information about the host address space
  layout.
- `"always"`: flushes L1 data cache every time the hypervisor
  enters the guest.  May incur significant performance cost.

options.title: security.wrapperDirSize
options.description:
Size limit for the /run/wrappers tmpfs. Look at {manpage}`mount(8)`, tmpfs size option,
for the accepted syntax. WARNING: don't set to less than 64MB.

options.title: security.wrappers
options.description:
This option effectively allows adding setuid/setgid bits, capabilities,
changing file ownership and permissions of a program without directly
modifying it. This works by creating a wrapper program in a directory
(not configurable), which is then added to the shell `PATH`.

options.title: security.wrappers.<name>.capabilities
options.description:
A comma-separated list of capability clauses to be given to the
wrapper program. The format for capability clauses is described in the
“TEXTUAL REPRESENTATION” section of the {manpage}`cap_from_text(3)`
manual page. For a list of capabilities supported by the system, check
the {manpage}`capabilities(7)` manual page.

::: {.note}
`cap_setpcap`, which is required for the wrapper
program to be able to raise caps into the Ambient set is NOT raised
to the Ambient set so that the real program cannot modify its own
capabilities!! This may be too restrictive for cases in which the
real program needs cap_setpcap but it at least leans on the side
security paranoid vs. too relaxed.
:::

options.description:
Service type. The following values are valid:

- `"proxy"`: HTTP/HTTPS proxy (default port 3128).
- `"socks"`: SOCKS 4/4.5/5 proxy (default port 1080).
- `"pop3p"`: POP3 proxy (default port 110).
- `"ftppr"`: FTP proxy (default port 21).
- `"admin"`: Web interface (default port 80).
- `"dnspr"`: Caching DNS proxy (default port 53).
- `"tcppm"`: TCP portmapper.
- `"udppm"`: UDP portmapper.

options.title: services._3proxy.usersFile
options.description:
Load users and passwords from this file.

Example users file with plain-text passwords:

```
  test1:CL:password1
  test2:CL:password2
```

Example users file with md5-crypted passwords:

```
  test1:CR:$1$tFkisVd2$1GA8JXkRmTXdLDytM/i3a1
  test2:CR:$1$rkpibm5J$Aq1.9VtYAn0JrqZ8M.1ME.
```

You can generate md5-crypted passwords via <https://unix4lyfe.org/crypt/>
Note that htpasswd tool generates incompatible md5-crypted passwords.
Consult [documentation](https://github.com/z3APA3A/3proxy/wiki/How-To-%28incomplete%29#USERS) for more information.

IP address / port.
If there is one server block configured to enable http2, then it is
enabled for all server blocks on this IP.
See <https://stackoverflow.com/a/39466948/263061>.

options.description:

This requires activating the QUIC transport protocol
`services.nginx.virtualHosts.<name>.quic = true;`.
Note that HTTP/3 support is experimental and *not* yet recommended for production.
Read more at <https://quic.nginx.org/>
HTTP/3 availability must be manually advertised, preferably in each location block.

options.title: services.agorakit.nginx.http3_hq
options.description:

This requires activating the QUIC transport protocol
`services.nginx.virtualHosts.<name>.quic = true;`.
Note that special application protocol support is experimental and *not* yet recommended for production.
Read more at <https://quic.nginx.org/>

options.title: services.agorakit.nginx.kTLS

database role and database if they do not already exist, and (re)set the role password

[{option}`config.services.akkoma.config.":pleroma"."Pleroma.Repo"`](#opt-services.akkoma.config.__pleroma_._Pleroma.Repo_).

options.title: services.alloy.configPath
options.description:
Alloy configuration file/directory path.

We default to `/etc/alloy` here, and expect the user to configure a
configuration file via `environment.etc."alloy/config.alloy"`.

This allows config reload, contrary to specifying a store path.

All `.alloy` files in the same directory (ignoring subdirs) are also
honored and are added to `systemd.services.alloy.reloadTriggers` to
enable config reload during nixos-rebuild switch.

This can also point to another directory containing `*.alloy` files, or
a single Alloy file in the Nix store (at the cost of reload).

Component names must be unique across all Alloy configuration files, and
configuration blocks must not be repeated.

Alloy will continue to run if subsequent reloads of the configuration
file fail, potentially marking components as unhealthy depending on
the nature of the failure. When this happens, Alloy will continue
functioning in the last valid state.

Anubis policy configuration in Nix syntax. Set to `null` to use the baked-in policy which should be
sufficient for most use-cases.

This option has no effect if `settings.POLICY_FNAME` is set to a different value, which is useful for
importing an existing configuration.

See [the documentation](https://anubis.techaro.lol/docs/admin/policies) for details.

options.title: services.anubis.instances.<name>.settings.BIND
options.description:
The address that Anubis listens to. See Go's [`net.Listen`](https://pkg.go.dev/net#Listen) for syntax.
Use the prefix "/run/anubis/anubis-<name>/". The prefix "/run/anubis" is deprecated.

Defaults to Unix domain sockets. To use TCP sockets, set this to a TCP address and `BIND_NETWORK` to `"tcp"`.

options.title: services.anubis.instances.<name>.settings.BIND_NETWORK
options.description:
The network family that Anubis should bind to.

Accepts anything supported by Go's [`net.Listen`](https://pkg.go.dev/net#Listen).

Common values are `tcp` and `unix`.

options.title: services.anubis.instances.<name>.settings.DIFFICULTY
options.description:
The difficulty required for clients to solve the challenge.

Currently, this means the amount of leading zeros in a successful response.

options.title: services.anubis.instances.<name>.settings.METRICS_BIND
options.description:
The address Anubis' metrics server listens to. See Go's [`net.Listen`](https://pkg.go.dev/net#Listen) for
syntax.
Use the prefix "/run/anubis/anubis-<name>/". The prefix "/run/anubis" is deprecated.

The metrics server is enabled by default and may be disabled. However, due to implementation details, this is
only possible by setting a command line flag. See {option}`services.anubis.defaultOptions.extraFlags` for an
example.

Defaults to Unix domain sockets. To use TCP sockets, set this to a TCP address and `METRICS_BIND_NETWORK` to
`"tcp"`.

options.title: services.anubis.instances.<name>.settings.METRICS_BIND_NETWORK
options.description:
The network family that the metrics server should bind to.

Accepts anything supported by Go's [`net.Listen`](https://pkg.go.dev/net#Listen).

Common values are `tcp` and `unix`.

options.title: services.anubis.instances.<name>.settings.OG_PASSTHROUGH

options.title: services.anuko-time-tracker.nginx.acmeFallbackHost
options.description:
Host which to proxy requests to if ACME challenge is not found. Useful
if you want multiple hosts to be able to verify the same domain name.

With this option, you could request certificates for the present domain
with an ACME client that is running on another host, which you would
specify here.

options.title: services.anuko-time-tracker.nginx.acmeRoot
options.description:
Directory for the ACME challenge, which is **public**. Don't put certs or keys in here.
Set to null to inherit from config.security.acme.

options.title: services.anuko-time-tracker.nginx.addSSL
options.description:
Whether to enable HTTPS in addition to plain HTTP. This will set defaults for
`listen` to listen on all interfaces on the respective default
ports (80, 443).

options.title: services.anuko-time-tracker.nginx.basicAuth
options.description:
Basic Auth protection for a vhost.

WARNING: This is implemented to store the password in plain text in the
Nix store.

options.title: services.anuko-time-tracker.nginx.basicAuthFile
options.description:
Basic Auth password file for a vhost.
Can be created by running {command}`nix-shell --packages apacheHttpd --run 'htpasswd -B -c FILENAME USERNAME'`.

options.title: services.anuko-time-tracker.nginx.default
options.description: Makes this vhost the default.

options.title: services.anuko-time-tracker.nginx.enableACME
options.description:
Whether to ask Let's Encrypt to sign a certificate for this vhost.
Alternately, you can use an existing certificate through {option}`useACMEHost`.

options.title: services.anuko-time-tracker.nginx.extraConfig
options.description: These lines go to the end of the vhost verbatim.

options.title: services.anuko-time-tracker.nginx.forceSSL
options.description:
Whether to add a separate nginx server block that redirects (defaults
to 301, configurable with `redirectCode`) all plain HTTP traffic to
HTTPS. This will set defaults for `listen` to listen on all interfaces
on the respective default ports (80, 443), where the non-SSL listens
are used for the redirect vhosts.

options.title: services.anuko-time-tracker.nginx.globalRedirect
options.description:
If set, all requests for this host are redirected (defaults to 301,
configurable with `redirectCode`) to the given hostname.

options.title: services.anuko-time-tracker.nginx.http2
options.description:
Whether to enable the HTTP/2 protocol.
Note that (as of writing) due to nginx's implementation, to disable
HTTP/2 you have to disable it on all vhosts that use a given
IP address / port.
If there is one server block configured to enable http2, then it is
enabled for all server blocks on this IP.
See <https://stackoverflow.com/a/39466948/263061>.

options.title: services.anuko-time-tracker.nginx.http3
options.description:
Whether to enable the HTTP/3 protocol.
This requires activating the QUIC transport protocol
`services.nginx.virtualHosts.<name>.quic = true;`.
Note that HTTP/3 support is experimental and *not* yet recommended for production.
Read more at <https://quic.nginx.org/>
HTTP/3 availability must be manually advertised, preferably in each location block.

options.title: services.anuko-time-tracker.nginx.http3_hq
options.description:
Whether to enable the HTTP/0.9 protocol negotiation used in QUIC interoperability tests.
This requires activating the QUIC transport protocol
`services.nginx.virtualHosts.<name>.quic = true;`.
Note that special application protocol support is experimental and *not* yet recommended for production.
Read more at <https://quic.nginx.org/>

options.title: services.anuko-time-tracker.nginx.kTLS
options.description:
Whether to enable kTLS support.
Implementing TLS in the kernel (kTLS) improves performance by significantly
reducing the need for copying operations between user space and the kernel.
Required Nginx version 1.21.4 or later.

options.title: services.anuko-time-tracker.nginx.listen
options.description:
Listen addresses and ports for this virtual host.
IPv6 addresses must be enclosed in square brackets.
Note: this option overrides `addSSL`
and `onlySSL`.

If you only want to set the addresses manually and not
the ports, take a look at `listenAddresses`.

options.title: services.apcupsd.configText
options.description:
Contents of the runtime configuration file, apcupsd.conf. The default
settings makes apcupsd autodetect USB UPSes, limit network access to
localhost and shutdown the system when the battery level is below 50
percent, or when the UPS has calculated that it has 5 minutes or less
of remaining power-on time. See man apcupsd.conf for details.

options.title: services.apcupsd.enable
options.description:
Whether to enable the APC UPS daemon. apcupsd monitors your UPS and
permits orderly shutdown of your computer in the event of a power
failure. User manual: http://www.apcupsd.com/manual/manual.html.
Note that apcupsd runs as root (to allow shutdown of computer).
You can check the status of your UPS with the "apcaccess" command.

options.title: services.apcupsd.hooks
options.type: attribute set of strings concatenated with "\n"
options.description:
Each attribute in this option names an apcupsd event and the string
value it contains will be executed in a shell, in response to that
event (prior to the default action). See "man apccontrol" for the
list of events and what they represent.

A hook script can stop apccontrol from doing its default action by
exiting with value 99. Do not do this unless you know what you're
doing.

options.title: services.asterisk.confFiles
options.description:
Sets the content of config files (typically ending with
`.conf`) in the Asterisk configuration directory.

Note that if you want to change `asterisk.conf`, it
is preferable to use the {option}`services.asterisk.extraConfig`
option over this option. If `"asterisk.conf"` is
specified with the {option}`confFiles` option (not recommended),
you must be prepared to set your own `astetcdir`
path.

See
<https://www.asterisk.org/community/documentation/>
for more examples of what is possible here.
options.example:
{
  "extensions.conf" = ''
    [tests]
    ; Dial 100 for "hello, world"
    exten => 100,1,Answer()
    same  =>     n,Wait(1)
    same  =>     n,Playback(hello-world)
    same  =>     n,Hangup()

    [softphones]
    include => tests

    [unauthorized]
  '';
  "sip.conf" = ''
    [general]
    allowguest=no              ; Require authentication
    context=unauthorized       ; Send unauthorized users to /dev/null
    srvlookup=no               ; Don't do DNS lookup
    udpbindaddr=0.0.0.0        ; Listen on all interfaces
    nat=force_rport,comedia    ; Assume device is behind NAT

    [softphone](!)
    type=friend                ; Match on username first, IP second
    context=softphones         ; Send to softphones context in
                               ; extensions.conf file
    host=dynamic               ; Device will register with asterisk
    disallow=all               ; Manually specify codecs to allow
    allow=g722
    allow=ulaw
    allow=alaw

    [myphone](softphone)
    secret=GhoshevFew          ; Change this password!
  '';
  "logger.conf" = ''
    [general]

    [logfiles]
    ; Add debug output to log
    syslog.local0 => notice,warning,error,debug
  '';
}

options.title: services.athens.downloadMode
options.type: one of "sync", "async", "redirect", "async_redirect", "none" or string matching the pattern ^file:.*$|^custom:.*$
options.description:
Defines how Athens behaves when a module@version
is not found in storage. There are 7 options:
1. "sync": download the module synchronously and
return the results to the client.
2. "async": return 404, but asynchronously store the module
in the storage backend.
3. "redirect": return a 301 redirect status to the client
with the base URL as the DownloadRedirectURL from below.
4. "async_redirect": same as option number 3 but it will
asynchronously store the module to the backend.
5. "none": return 404 if a module is not found and do nothing.
6. "file:<path>": will point to an HCL file that specifies
any of the 5 options above based on different import paths.
7. "custom:<base64-encoded-hcl>" is the same as option 6
but the file is fully encoded in the option. This is
useful for using an environment variable in serverless
deployments.

options.title: services.athens.networkMode
options.description:
Configures how Athens will return the results
of the /list endpoint as it can be assembled from both its own
storage and the upstream VCS.

Note, that for better error messaging, this would also affect how other
endpoints behave.

Modes:
1. strict: merge VCS versions with storage versions, but fail if either of them fails.
2. offline: only get storage versions, never reach out to VCS.
3. fallback: only return storage versions, if VCS fails. Note this means that you may
see inconsistent results since fallback mode does a best effort of giving you what's
available at the time of requesting versions.

options.type: 16 bit unsigned integer; between 0 and 65535 (both inclusive)
options.description:
Specify the port (a positive integer) on which the Director daemon
will listen for Bacula Console connections. This same port number
must be specified in the Director resource of the Console

need not be specified. This directive should not be used if you
