Alternately, you can use an existing certificate through {option}`useACMEHost`.

options.title: services.fedimintd.<name>.nginx.config.extraConfig
options.description: These lines go to the end of the vhost verbatim.

options.title: services.fedimintd.<name>.nginx.config.forceSSL
options.description:
Whether to add a separate nginx server block that redirects (defaults
to 301, configurable with `redirectCode`) all plain HTTP traffic to
HTTPS. This will set defaults for `listen` to listen on all interfaces
on the respective default ports (80, 443), where the non-SSL listens
are used for the redirect vhosts.

options.title: services.fedimintd.<name>.nginx.config.globalRedirect
options.description:
If set, all requests for this host are redirected (defaults to 301,
configurable with `redirectCode`) to the given hostname.

options.title: services.fedimintd.<name>.nginx.config.http2
options.description:
Whether to enable the HTTP/2 protocol.
Note that (as of writing) due to nginx's implementation, to disable
HTTP/2 you have to disable it on all vhosts that use a given
IP address / port.
If there is one server block configured to enable http2, then it is
enabled for all server blocks on this IP.
See <https://stackoverflow.com/a/39466948/263061>.

options.title: services.fedimintd.<name>.nginx.config.http3
options.description:
Whether to enable the HTTP/3 protocol.
This requires activating the QUIC transport protocol
`services.nginx.virtualHosts.<name>.quic = true;`.
Note that HTTP/3 support is experimental and *not* yet recommended for production.
Read more at <https://quic.nginx.org/>
HTTP/3 availability must be manually advertised, preferably in each location block.

options.title: services.fedimintd.<name>.nginx.config.http3_hq
options.description:
Whether to enable the HTTP/0.9 protocol negotiation used in QUIC interoperability tests.
This requires activating the QUIC transport protocol
`services.nginx.virtualHosts.<name>.quic = true;`.
Note that special application protocol support is experimental and *not* yet recommended for production.
Read more at <https://quic.nginx.org/>

options.title: services.fedimintd.<name>.nginx.config.kTLS
options.description:
Whether to enable kTLS support.
Implementing TLS in the kernel (kTLS) improves performance by significantly
reducing the need for copying operations between user space and the kernel.
Required Nginx version 1.21.4 or later.

the ports, take a look at `listenAddresses`.

options.title: services.firewalld.settings.IPv6_rpfilter
options.description:
Performs reverse path filtering (RPF) on IPv6 packets as per RFC 3704.

Possible values:

`"strict"`
: Performs "strict" filtering as per RFC 3704.
  This check verifies that the in ingress interface is the same interface that would be used to send a packet reply to the source.
  That is, `ingress == egress`.

`"loose"`
: Performs "loose" filtering as per RFC 3704.
  This check only verifies that there is a route back to the source through any interface; even if it's not the same one on which the packet arrived.

`"strict-forward"`
: This is almost identical to "strict", but does not perform RPF for packets targeted to the host (INPUT).

`"loose-forward"`
: This is almost identical to "loose", but does not perform RPF for packets targeted to the host (INPUT).

`"no"`
: RPF is completely disabled.

The rp_filter for IPv4 is controlled using sysctl.

options.title: services.firewalld.settings.IndividualCalls

The use of individual calls increases the time that is needed to apply changes and to start the daemon, but is good for debugging as error messages are more specific.

options.description:

If you intend to modify firewalld's rules, set this to `false`.

options.description:

Firewalld will be strict and not allow published container ports until they're explicitly allowed via firewalld.
If set to `false`, then docker (and podman) integrates seamlessly with firewalld.
Published container ports are implicitly allowed.

options.title: services.firezone.server.settings
options.type: open submodule of attribute set of (boolean or floating point number or signed integer or string or absolute path or package)
options.description:
Environment variables for the Firezone server. For a list of available
variables, please refer to the [upstream definitions](https://github.com/firezone/firezone/blob/main/elixir/apps/domain/lib/domain/config/definitions.ex).
Some variables like `OUTBOUND_EMAIL_ADAPTER_OPTS` require json values
for which you can use `VAR = builtins.toJSON { /* ... */ }`.

Each component has an additional `settings` option which allows you to
override specific variables passed to that component.

options.title: services.firezone.server.settingsSecret
options.type: open submodule of attribute set of absolute path
options.description:
This is a convenience option which allows you to set secret values for
environment variables by specifying a file which will contain the value
at runtime. Before starting the server, the content of each file will
be loaded into the respective environment variable.

Otherwise, this option is equivalent to
{option}`services.firezone.server.settings`. Refer to the settings
option for more information regarding the actual variables and how
filtering rules are applied for each component.

options.title: services.firezone.server.settingsSecret.COOKIE_ENCRYPTION_SALT
options.description:
A file containing a unique base64 encoded secret for the
`COOKIE_ENCRYPTION_SALT`. All Firezone components in your cluster must
use the same value.

If this is `null`, a shared value will automatically be generated
on startup and used for all components on this machine. You do
not need to set this except when you spread your cluster over
multiple hosts.

options.title: services.firezone.server.smtp.configureManually
options.description:
Outbound email configuration is mandatory for Firezone and supports
many different delivery adapters. Yet, most users will only need an
SMTP relay to send emails, so this configuration enforced by default.

If you want to utilize an alternative way to send emails (e.g. via a
supportd API-based service), enable this option and define
`OUTBOUND_EMAIL_FROM`, `OUTBOUND_EMAIL_ADAPTER` and
`OUTBOUND_EMAIL_ADAPTER_OPTS` manually via
{option}`services.firezone.server.settings` and/or
{option}`services.firezone.server.settingsSecret`.

The Firezone documentation holds [a list of supported Swoosh adapters](https://github.com/firezone/firezone/blob/main/website/src/app/docs/reference/env-vars/readme.mdx#outbound-emails).

options.title: services.fluidd.nginx.forceSSL
options.description:
Whether to add a separate nginx server block that redirects (defaults
to 301, configurable with `redirectCode`) all plain HTTP traffic to
HTTPS. This will set defaults for `listen` to listen on all interfaces
on the respective default ports (80, 443), where the non-SSL listens
are used for the redirect vhosts.

options.title: services.fluidd.nginx.globalRedirect
options.description:

options.title: services.fluidd.nginx.http2
options.description:
Whether to enable the HTTP/2 protocol.
Note that (as of writing) due to nginx's implementation, to disable
HTTP/2 you have to disable it on all vhosts that use a given
IP address / port.
If there is one server block configured to enable http2, then it is
enabled for all server blocks on this IP.
See <https://stackoverflow.com/a/39466948/263061>.

options.title: services.fluidd.nginx.http3
options.description:
Whether to enable the HTTP/3 protocol.
This requires activating the QUIC transport protocol
`services.nginx.virtualHosts.<name>.quic = true;`.
Note that HTTP/3 support is experimental and *not* yet recommended for production.
Read more at <https://quic.nginx.org/>
HTTP/3 availability must be manually advertised, preferably in each location block.

options.title: services.fluidd.nginx.http3_hq
options.description:
Whether to enable the HTTP/0.9 protocol negotiation used in QUIC interoperability tests.
This requires activating the QUIC transport protocol
`services.nginx.virtualHosts.<name>.quic = true;`.
Note that special application protocol support is experimental and *not* yet recommended for production.
Read more at <https://quic.nginx.org/>

options.title: services.fluidd.nginx.kTLS
options.description:
Whether to enable kTLS support.
Implementing TLS in the kernel (kTLS) improves performance by significantly
reducing the need for copying operations between user space and the kernel.

`MiB` is assumed. This parameter does not
change the memory allocation of the program. Rather, it sets
a hard limit beyond which the process will kill itself and
be restarted. The default value of `8GiB`
is double the intended memory usage in the default
configuration (providing an emergency buffer to deal with
memory leaks or similar problems). It is not recommended to
decrease the value of this parameter below its default
value. It may be increased if you wish to allocate a very
large amount of storage engine memory or cache. In
particular, when the `storageMemory`
parameter is increased, the `memory`
parameter should be increased by an equal amount.

options.title: services.gancio.nginx.acmeFallbackHost
options.description:
Host which to proxy requests to if ACME challenge is not found. Useful
if you want multiple hosts to be able to verify the same domain name.

With this option, you could request certificates for the present domain
with an ACME client that is running on another host, which you would
specify here.

options.title: services.gancio.nginx.acmeRoot
options.description:
Directory for the ACME challenge, which is **public**. Don't put certs or keys in here.
Set to null to inherit from config.security.acme.

options.title: services.gancio.nginx.addSSL
options.description:
Whether to enable HTTPS in addition to plain HTTP. This will set defaults for
`listen` to listen on all interfaces on the respective default
ports (80, 443).

options.title: services.gancio.nginx.basicAuth
options.description:
Basic Auth protection for a vhost.

WARNING: This is implemented to store the password in plain text in the
Nix store.

options.title: services.gancio.nginx.basicAuthFile
options.description:
Basic Auth password file for a vhost.
Can be created by running {command}`nix-shell --packages apacheHttpd --run 'htpasswd -B -c FILENAME USERNAME'`.

options.title: services.gancio.nginx.default
options.description: Makes this vhost the default.

options.title: services.gancio.nginx.enableACME
options.description:
Whether to ask Let's Encrypt to sign a certificate for this vhost.
Alternately, you can use an existing certificate through {option}`useACMEHost`.

options.title: services.gancio.nginx.extraConfig
options.description: These lines go to the end of the vhost verbatim.

options.title: services.gancio.nginx.forceSSL
options.description:
Whether to add a separate nginx server block that redirects (defaults
to 301, configurable with `redirectCode`) all plain HTTP traffic to
HTTPS. This will set defaults for `listen` to listen on all interfaces
on the respective default ports (80, 443), where the non-SSL listens
are used for the redirect vhosts.

options.title: services.gancio.nginx.globalRedirect
options.description:
If set, all requests for this host are redirected (defaults to 301,
configurable with `redirectCode`) to the given hostname.

options.title: services.gancio.nginx.http2
options.description:
Whether to enable the HTTP/2 protocol.
Note that (as of writing) due to nginx's implementation, to disable
HTTP/2 you have to disable it on all vhosts that use a given
IP address / port.
If there is one server block configured to enable http2, then it is
enabled for all server blocks on this IP.
See <https://stackoverflow.com/a/39466948/263061>.

options.title: services.gancio.nginx.http3
options.description:
Whether to enable the HTTP/3 protocol.
This requires activating the QUIC transport protocol
`services.nginx.virtualHosts.<name>.quic = true;`.
Note that HTTP/3 support is experimental and *not* yet recommended for production.
Read more at <https://quic.nginx.org/>
HTTP/3 availability must be manually advertised, preferably in each location block.

options.title: services.gancio.nginx.http3_hq
options.description:
Whether to enable the HTTP/0.9 protocol negotiation used in QUIC interoperability tests.
This requires activating the QUIC transport protocol
`services.nginx.virtualHosts.<name>.quic = true;`.
Note that special application protocol support is experimental and *not* yet recommended for production.
Read more at <https://quic.nginx.org/>

options.title: services.gancio.nginx.kTLS
options.description:
Whether to enable kTLS support.
Implementing TLS in the kernel (kTLS) improves performance by significantly
reducing the need for copying operations between user space and the kernel.
Required Nginx version 1.21.4 or later.

options.title: services.gancio.nginx.listen
options.description:
Listen addresses and ports for this virtual host.
IPv6 addresses must be enclosed in square brackets.
Note: this option overrides `addSSL`
and `onlySSL`.

If you only want to set the addresses manually and not
the ports, take a look at `listenAddresses`.

options.description:

options.title: services.github-runners.<name>.ephemeral
options.description:
If enabled, causes the following behavior:

- Passes the `--ephemeral` flag to the runner configuration script
- De-registers and stops the runner with GitHub after it has processed one job
- On stop, systemd wipes the runtime directory (this always happens, even without using the ephemeral option)
- Restarts the service after its successful exit
- On start, wipes the state directory and configures a new runner

You should only enable this option if `tokenFile` points to a file which contains a
personal access token (PAT). If you're using the option with a registration token, restarting the
service will fail as soon as the registration token expired.

Changing this option triggers a new runner registration.

options.title: services.github-runners.<name>.group
options.description:
Group under which to run the service.

The effect of this option depends on the value of the `user` option:

- `group == null` and `user == null`:
  The service runs with a dynamically allocated user and group.
- `group == null` and `user != null`:
  The service runs as the given user and its default group.
- `group != null` and `user == null`:
  This configuration is invalid. In this case, the service would use the given group
  but run as root implicitly. If this is really what you want, set `user = "root"` explicitly.

options.title: services.github-runners.<name>.tokenFile
options.description:
The full path to a file which contains either

* a fine-grained personal access token (PAT),
* a classic PAT
* or a runner registration token

Changing this option or the `tokenFile`’s content triggers a new runner registration.

We suggest using the fine-grained PATs. A runner registration token is valid
only for 1 hour after creation, so the next time the runner configuration changes
this will give you hard-to-debug HTTP 404 errors in the configure step.

The file should contain exactly one line with the token without any newline.
(Use `echo -n '…token…' > …token file…` to make sure no newlines sneak in.)

If the file contains a PAT, the service creates a new registration token
on startup as needed.
If a registration token is given, it can be used to re-register a runner of the same
name but is time-limited as noted above.

For fine-grained PATs:

Give it "Read and Write access to organization/repository self hosted runners",
depending on whether it is organization wide or per-repository. You might have to
experiment a little, fine-grained PATs are a `beta` Github feature and still subject
to change; nonetheless they are the best option at the moment.

For classic PATs:

Make sure the PAT has a scope of `admin:org` for organization-wide registrations
or a scope of `repo` for a single repository.

For runner registration tokens:

Nothing special needs to be done, but updating will break after one hour,
so these are not recommended.

options.title: services.github-runners.<name>.url
options.description:
Repository to add the runner to.

Changing this option triggers a new runner registration.

IMPORTANT: If your token is org-wide (not per repository), you need to
provide a github org link, not a single repository, so do it like this
`https://github.com/nixos`, not like this
`https://github.com/nixos/nixpkgs`.
Otherwise, you are going to get a `404 NotFound`
from `POST https://api.github.com/actions/runner-registration`
in the configure script.

options.title: services.gitlab-runner.services.<name>.authenticationTokenConfigFile
options.description:
Absolute path to a file containing environment variables used for
gitlab-runner registrations with *runner authentication tokens*.
They replace the deprecated *runner registration tokens*, as
outlined in the [GitLab documentation].

A list of all supported environment variables can be found with
`gitlab-runner register --help`.

The ones you probably want to set are:
- `CI_SERVER_URL=<CI server URL>`
- `CI_SERVER_TOKEN=<runner authentication token secret>`

::: {.warning}
Make sure to use a quoted absolute path,
or it is going to be copied to Nix Store.
:::

[GitLab documentation]: https://docs.gitlab.com/17.0/ee/ci/runners/new_creation_workflow.html#estimated-time-frame-for-planned-changes

options.title: services.gitlab-runner.services.<name>.registrationConfigFile
options.description:
Absolute path to a file with environment variables
used for gitlab-runner registration with *runner registration
tokens*.

A list of all supported environment variables can be found in
`gitlab-runner register --help`.

The ones you probably want to set are:
- `CI_SERVER_URL=<CI server URL>`
- `REGISTRATION_TOKEN=<registration secret>`

Support for *runner registration tokens* is deprecated since
GitLab 16.0, has been disabled by default in GitLab 17.0 and
will be removed in GitLab 18.0, as outlined in the
[GitLab documentation]. Please consider migrating to
[runner authentication tokens] and check the documentation on
{option}`services.gitlab-runner.services.<name>.authenticationTokenConfigFile`.

::: {.warning}
Make sure to use a quoted absolute path,
or it is going to be copied to Nix Store.
:::

[GitLab documentation]: https://docs.gitlab.com/17.0/ee/ci/runners/new_creation_workflow.html#estimated-time-frame-for-planned-changes
[runner authentication tokens]: https://docs.gitlab.com/17.0/ee/ci/runners/new_creation_workflow.html#the-new-runner-registration-workflow

options.title: services.gitlab.secrets.activeRecordDeterministicKeyFile

in the DB. This should not be the same as `services.gitlab.secrets.activeRecordPrimaryKeyFile`!

Make sure the secret is at ideally 32 characters and all random,
no regular words or you'll be exposed to dictionary attacks.

This should be a string, not a nix path, since nix paths are
copied into the world-readable nix store.

This should be a string, not a nix path, since nix paths are

options.title: services.gitlab.secrets.otpFile

Make sure the secret is at least 32 characters and all random,
no regular words or you'll be exposed to dictionary attacks.

This should be a string, not a nix path, since nix paths are
copied into the world-readable nix store.

options.title: services.gitlab.secrets.secretFile

This should be Perl code that modifies the `%RC`

content is generated by invoking `gitolite print-default-rc`,
and extra configuration from this option is appended to it. The result
is placed to Nix store, and the `~/.gitolite.rc` file
becomes a symlink to it.

If you already have a customized (or otherwise changed)
`~/.gitolite.rc` file, NixOS will refuse to replace
it with a symlink, and the `gitolite-init` initialization service
will fail. In this situation, in order to use this option, you
will need to take any customizations you may have in
`~/.gitolite.rc`, convert them to appropriate Perl
statements, add them to this option, and remove the file.

options.title: services.grafana.provision.alerting.templates.settings.deleteTemplates.*.orgId

options.title: services.grafana.provision.alerting.templates.settings.templates
options.description: List of templates to import or update.

options.title: services.grafana.provision.alerting.templates.settings.templates.*.template
options.description: Alerting with a custom text template

options.title: services.grafana.provision.dashboards
options.description: Declaratively provision Grafana's dashboards.

options.description:
Path to YAML dashboard configuration. Can't be used with
[](#opt-services.grafana.provision.dashboards.settings) simultaneously.
Can be either a directory or a single YAML file. Will end up in the store.

options.title: services.grafana.provision.dashboards.settings
options.description:
Grafana dashboard configuration in Nix. Can't be used with
[](#opt-services.grafana.provision.dashboards.path) simultaneously. See
<https://grafana.com/docs/grafana/latest/administration/provisioning/#dashboards>
for supported options.

options.title: services.grafana.provision.dashboards.settings.apiVersion
options.description: Config file version.

options.title: services.grafana.provision.dashboards.settings.providers
options.description: List of dashboards to insert/update.

options.title: services.grafana.provision.dashboards.settings.providers.*.name
options.description: A unique provider name.

options.title: services.grafana.provision.dashboards.settings.providers.*.options.path
options.description: Path grafana will watch for dashboards. Required when using the 'file' type.

options.title: services.grafana.provision.dashboards.settings.providers.*.type
options.description: Dashboard provider type.

options.title: services.grafana.provision.datasources
options.description: Declaratively provision Grafana's datasources.

options.title: services.grafana.provision.datasources.path
options.description:
Path to YAML datasource configuration. Can't be used with
[](#opt-services.grafana.provision.datasources.settings) simultaneously.
Can be either a directory or a single YAML file. Will end up in the store.

options.title: services.grafana.provision.datasources.settings
options.description:
Grafana datasource configuration in Nix. Can't be used with
[](#opt-services.grafana.provision.datasources.path) simultaneously. See
<https://grafana.com/docs/grafana/latest/administration/provisioning/#data-sources>
for supported options.

options.title: services.grafana.provision.datasources.settings.apiVersion
options.description: Config file version.

options.title: services.grafana.provision.datasources.settings.datasources
options.description: List of datasources to insert/update.

options.title: services.grafana.provision.datasources.settings.datasources.*.access
options.description: Access mode. proxy or direct (Server or Browser in the UI). Required.

options.title: services.grafana.provision.datasources.settings.datasources.*.editable
options.description: Allow users to edit datasources from the UI.

options.title: services.grafana.provision.datasources.settings.datasources.*.jsonData
options.description: Extra data for datasource plugins.

options.title: services.grafana.provision.datasources.settings.datasources.*.name
options.description: Name of the datasource. Required.

options.title: services.grafana.provision.datasources.settings.datasources.*.secureJsonData
options.description:
Datasource specific secure configuration. Please note that the contents of this option
will end up in a world-readable Nix store. Use the file provider
pointing at a reasonably secured file in the local filesystem
to work around that. Look at the documentation for details:
<https://grafana.com/docs/grafana/latest/setup-grafana/configure-grafana/#file-provider>

options.title: services.grafana.provision.datasources.settings.datasources.*.type
options.description: Datasource type. Required.

options.title: services.grafana.provision.datasources.settings.datasources.*.uid
options.description: Custom UID which can be used to reference this datasource in other parts of the configuration, if not specified will be generated automatically.

options.title: services.grafana.provision.datasources.settings.datasources.*.url
options.description: Url of the datasource.

options.title: services.grafana.provision.datasources.settings.deleteDatasources
options.description: List of datasources that should be deleted from the database.

options.title: services.grafana.provision.datasources.settings.deleteDatasources.*.name
options.description: Name of the datasource to delete.

options.title: services.grafana.provision.datasources.settings.deleteDatasources.*.orgId
options.description: Organization ID of the datasource to delete.

options.title: services.grafana.provision.datasources.settings.prune
options.description:
When `true`, provisioned datasources from this file will be deleted
automatically when removed from
{option}`services.grafana.provision.datasources.settings.datasources`.

options.title: services.grafana.provision.enable
options.description: Whether to enable provision.

options.title: services.grafana.settings
options.type: open submodule of attribute set of section of an INI file (attrs of INI atom (null, bool, int, float or string) or a non-empty list of them)
options.description:
Grafana settings. See <https://grafana.com/docs/grafana/latest/setup-grafana/configure-grafana/>
for available options. INI format is used.

options.title: services.grafana.settings.analytics.check_for_plugin_updates
options.description:
When set to `false`, disables checking for new versions of installed plugins from https://grafana.com.
When enabled, the check for a new plugin runs every 10 minutes.
It will notify, via the UI, when a new plugin update exists.
The check itself will not prompt any auto-updates of the plugin, nor will it send any sensitive information.

options.title: services.grafana.settings.analytics.check_for_updates
options.description:
When set to `false`, disables checking for new versions of Grafana from Grafana's GitHub repository.
When enabled, the check for a new version runs every 10 minutes.
It will notify, via the UI, when a new version is available.
The check itself will not prompt any auto-updates of the Grafana software, nor will it send any sensitive information.

options.title: services.grafana.settings.analytics.feedback_links_enabled
options.description: Set to `false` to remove all feedback links from the UI.

options.title: services.grafana.settings.analytics.reporting_enabled
options.description:
When enabled Grafana will send anonymous usage statistics to `stats.grafana.org`.
No IP addresses are being tracked, only simple counters to track running instances, versions, dashboard and error counts.
Counters are sent every 24 hours.

options.title: services.grafana.settings.database.ca_cert_path
options.description: The path to the CA certificate to use.

options.title: services.grafana.settings.database.cache_mode
options.description:
For `sqlite3` only.
[Shared cache](https://www.sqlite.org/sharedcache.html) setting used for connecting to the database.

options.title: services.grafana.settings.database.client_cert_path
options.description: The path to the client cert. Only if server requires client authentication.

options.title: services.grafana.settings.database.client_key_path
options.description: The path to the client key. Only if server requires client authentication.

options.title: services.grafana.settings.database.conn_max_lifetime
options.description:
Sets the maximum amount of time a connection may be reused.
The default is 14400 (which means 14400 seconds or 4 hours).
For MySQL, this setting should be shorter than the `wait_timeout` variable.

options.title: services.grafana.settings.database.host
options.description:
Only applicable to MySQL or Postgres.
Includes IP or hostname and port or in case of Unix sockets the path to it.
For example, for MySQL running on the same host as Grafana: `host = "127.0.0.1:3306"`
or with Unix sockets: `host = "/var/run/mysqld/mysqld.sock"`

options.title: services.grafana.settings.database.isolation_level
options.description:
Only the MySQL driver supports isolation levels in Grafana.
In case the value is empty, the driver's default isolation level is applied.

options.title: services.grafana.settings.database.locking_attempt_timeout_sec
options.description:
For `mysql`, if the `migrationLocking` feature toggle is set,
specify the time (in seconds) to wait before failing to lock the database for the migrations.

options.title: services.grafana.settings.database.log_queries
options.description: Set to `true` to log the sql calls and execution times

options.title: services.grafana.settings.database.max_idle_conn
options.description: The maximum number of connections in the idle connection pool.

options.title: services.grafana.settings.database.max_open_conn
options.description: The maximum number of open connections to the database.

options.title: services.grafana.settings.database.name
options.description: The name of the Grafana database.

options.title: services.grafana.settings.database.password
options.description:
The database user's password (not applicable for `sqlite3`).

Please note that the contents of this option
will end up in a world-readable Nix store. Use the file provider
pointing at a reasonably secured file in the local filesystem
to work around that. Look at the documentation for details:
<https://grafana.com/docs/grafana/latest/setup-grafana/configure-grafana/#file-provider>

options.title: services.grafana.settings.database.path
options.description: Only applicable to `sqlite3` database. The file path where the database will be stored.

options.title: services.grafana.settings.database.query_retries
options.description: This setting applies to `sqlite3` only and controls the number of times the system retries a query when the database is locked.

options.title: services.grafana.settings.database.server_cert_name
options.description:
The common name field of the certificate used by the `mysql` or `postgres` server.
Not necessary if `ssl_mode` is set to `skip-verify`.

options.title: services.grafana.settings.database.ssl_mode
options.description:
For Postgres, use either `disable`, `require` or `verify-full`.
For MySQL, use either `true`, `false`, or `skip-verify`.

options.title: services.grafana.settings.database.transaction_retries
options.description: This setting applies to `sqlite3` only and controls the number of times the system retries a transaction when the database is locked.

options.title: services.grafana.settings.database.type
options.description: Database type.

options.title: services.grafana.settings.database.user
options.description: The database user (not applicable for `sqlite3`).

options.title: services.grafana.settings.database.wal
options.description:
For `sqlite3` only.
Setting to enable/disable [Write-Ahead Logging](https://sqlite.org/wal.html).

options.title: services.grafana.settings.paths.plugins
options.description: Directory where grafana will automatically scan and look for plugins

options.title: services.grafana.settings.paths.provisioning
options.description:
Folder that contains provisioning config files that grafana will apply on startup and while running.
Don't change the value of this option if you are planning to use `services.grafana.provision` options.
options.default: "directory with links to files generated from services.grafana.provision"

options.title: services.grafana.settings.security.admin_email
options.description: The email of the default Grafana Admin, created on startup.

options.title: services.grafana.settings.security.admin_password
options.description:
Default admin password. Please note that the contents of this option
will end up in a world-readable Nix store. Use the file provider
pointing at a reasonably secured file in the local filesystem
to work around that. Look at the documentation for details:
<https://grafana.com/docs/grafana/latest/setup-grafana/configure-grafana/#file-provider>

options.title: services.grafana.settings.security.admin_user
options.description: Default admin username.

options.title: services.grafana.settings.security.allow_embedding
options.description:
When `false`, the HTTP header `X-Frame-Options: deny` will be set in Grafana HTTP responses
which will instruct browsers to not allow rendering Grafana in a `<frame>`, `<iframe>`, `<embed>` or `<object>`.
The main goal is to mitigate the risk of [Clickjacking](https://owasp.org/www-community/attacks/Clickjacking).

options.title: services.grafana.settings.security.content_security_policy
options.description:
Set to `true` to add the `Content-Security-Policy` header to your requests.
CSP allows to control resources that the user agent can load and helps prevent XSS attacks.

options.title: services.grafana.settings.security.content_security_policy_report_only
options.description:
Set to `true` to add the `Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only` header to your requests.
CSP in Report Only mode enables you to experiment with policies by monitoring their effects without enforcing them.
You can enable both policies simultaneously.

options.title: services.grafana.settings.security.cookie_samesite
options.description:
Sets the `SameSite` cookie attribute and prevents the browser from sending this cookie along with cross-site requests.
The main goal is to mitigate the risk of cross-origin information leakage.
This setting also provides some protection against cross-site request forgery attacks (CSRF),
[read more about SameSite here](https://owasp.org/www-community/SameSite).
Using value `disabled` does not add any `SameSite` attribute to cookies.

options.title: services.grafana.settings.security.cookie_secure
options.description: Set to `true` if you host Grafana behind HTTPS.

options.title: services.grafana.settings.security.csrf_additional_headers
options.description:
List of allowed headers to be set by the user.
Suggested to use for if authentication lives behind reverse proxies.

options.title: services.grafana.settings.security.csrf_trusted_origins
options.description:
List of additional allowed URLs to pass by the CSRF check.
Suggested when authentication comes from an IdP.

options.title: services.grafana.settings.security.data_source_proxy_whitelist
options.description:
Define a whitelist of allowed IP addresses or domains, with ports,
to be used in data source URLs with the Grafana data source proxy.
Format: `ip_or_domain:port` separated by spaces.
PostgreSQL, MySQL, and MSSQL data sources do not use the proxy and are therefore unaffected by this setting.

options.title: services.grafana.settings.security.disable_brute_force_login_protection
options.description: Set to `true` to disable [brute force login protection](https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Authentication_Cheat_Sheet.html#account-lockout).

options.title: services.grafana.settings.security.disable_gravatar
options.description: Set to `true` to disable the use of Gravatar for user profile images.

options.title: services.grafana.settings.security.disable_initial_admin_creation
options.description: Disable creation of admin user on first start of Grafana.

options.title: services.grafana.settings.security.secret_key
options.description:
Secret key used for signing. Please note that the contents of this option
will end up in a world-readable Nix store. Use the file provider
pointing at a reasonably secured file in the local filesystem
to work around that. Look at the documentation for details:
<https://grafana.com/docs/grafana/latest/setup-grafana/configure-grafana/#file-provider>

options.title: services.grafana.settings.security.strict_transport_security
options.description:
Set to `true` if you want to enable HTTP `Strict-Transport-Security` (HSTS) response header.
Only use this when HTTPS is enabled in your configuration,
or when there is another upstream system that ensures your application does HTTPS (like a frontend load balancer).
HSTS tells browsers that the site should only be accessed using HTTPS.

options.title: services.grafana.settings.security.strict_transport_security_max_age_seconds
options.description:
Sets how long a browser should cache HSTS in seconds.
Only applied if `strict_transport_security` is enabled.

options.title: services.grafana.settings.security.strict_transport_security_preload
options.description:
Set to `true` to enable HSTS `preloading` option.
Only applied if `strict_transport_security` is enabled.

options.title: services.grafana.settings.security.strict_transport_security_subdomains
options.description:
Set to `true` to enable HSTS `includeSubDomains` option.
Only applied if `strict_transport_security` is enabled.

options.title: services.grafana.settings.security.x_content_type_options
options.description:
Set to `false` to disable the `X-Content-Type-Options` response header.
The `X-Content-Type-Options` response HTTP header is a marker used by the server
to indicate that the MIME types advertised in the `Content-Type` headers should not be changed and be followed.

options.title: services.grafana.settings.security.x_xss_protection
options.description:
Set to `true` to enable the `X-XSS-Protection` header,
which tells browsers to stop pages from loading when they detect reflected cross-site scripting (XSS) attacks.

__Note:__ this is the default in Grafana, it's turned off here
since it's [recommended to not use this header anymore](https://owasp.org/www-project-secure-headers/#x-xss-protection).

options.title: services.grafana.settings.server.cdn_url
options.description:
Specify a full HTTP URL address to the root of your Grafana CDN assets.
Grafana will add edition and version paths.

For example, given a cdn url like `https://cdn.myserver.com`
grafana will try to load a javascript file from `http://cdn.myserver.com/grafana-oss/7.4.0/public/build/app.<hash>.js`.

options.title: services.grafana.settings.server.cert_file
options.description: Path to the certificate file (if `protocol` is set to `https` or `h2`).

options.title: services.grafana.settings.server.cert_key
options.description: Path to the certificate key file (if `protocol` is set to `https` or `h2`).

options.title: services.grafana.settings.server.domain
options.description:
The public facing domain name used to access grafana from a browser.

This setting is only used in the default value of the `root_url` setting.
If you set the latter manually, this option does not have to be specified.

options.title: services.grafana.settings.server.enable_gzip
options.description:
Set this option to `true` to enable HTTP compression, this can improve transfer speed and bandwidth utilization.
It is recommended that most users set it to `true`. By default it is set to `false` for compatibility reasons.

options.title: services.grafana.settings.server.enforce_domain
options.description:
Redirect to correct domain if the host header does not match the domain.
Prevents DNS rebinding attacks.

options.title: services.grafana.settings.server.http_addr
options.description:
Listening address.

::: {.note}
This setting intentionally varies from upstream's default to be a bit more secure by default.
:::

options.title: services.grafana.settings.server.http_port
options.type: 16 bit unsigned integer; between 0 and 65535 (both inclusive)
options.description: Listening port.

options.title: services.grafana.settings.server.protocol
options.description: Which protocol to listen.

options.title: services.grafana.settings.server.read_timeout
options.description:
Sets the maximum time using a duration format (5s/5m/5ms)
before timing out read of an incoming request and closing idle connections.
0 means there is no timeout for reading the request.

options.title: services.grafana.settings.server.root_url
options.description:
This is the full URL used to access Grafana from a web browser.
This is important if you use Google or GitHub OAuth authentication (for the callback URL to be correct).

This setting is also important if you have a reverse proxy in front of Grafana that exposes it through a subpath.
In that case add the subpath to the end of this URL setting.

options.title: services.grafana.settings.server.router_logging
options.description:
Set to `true` for Grafana to log all HTTP requests (not just errors).
These are logged as Info level events to the Grafana log.

options.title: services.grafana.settings.server.serve_from_sub_path
options.description:
Serve Grafana from subpath specified in the `root_url` setting.
By default it is set to `false` for compatibility reasons.

By enabling this setting and using a subpath in `root_url` above,
e.g. `root_url = "http://localhost:3000/grafana"`,
Grafana is accessible on `http://localhost:3000/grafana`.
If accessed without subpath, Grafana will redirect to an URL with the subpath.

options.title: services.grafana.settings.server.socket
options.description:
Path where the socket should be created when `protocol=socket`.
Make sure that Grafana has appropriate permissions before you change this setting.

options.title: services.grafana.settings.server.socket_gid
options.description:
GID where the socket should be set when `protocol=socket`.
Make sure that the target group is in the group of Grafana process and that Grafana process is the file owner before you change this setting.
It is recommended to set the gid as http server user gid.
Not set when the value is -1.

options.title: services.grafana.settings.server.socket_mode
options.description:
Mode where the socket should be set when `protocol=socket`.
Make sure that Grafana process is the file owner before you change this setting.

options.title: services.grafana.settings.server.static_root_path
options.description: Root path for static assets.

options.title: services.grafana.settings.smtp.cert_file
options.description: File path to a cert file.

options.title: services.grafana.settings.smtp.ehlo_identity
options.description: Name to be used as client identity for EHLO in SMTP dialog.

options.title: services.grafana.settings.smtp.enabled
options.description: Whether to enable SMTP.

options.title: services.grafana.settings.smtp.from_address
options.description: Address used when sending out emails.

options.title: services.grafana.settings.smtp.from_name
options.description: Name to be used as client identity for EHLO in SMTP dialog.

options.title: services.grafana.settings.smtp.host
options.description: Host to connect to.

options.title: services.grafana.settings.smtp.key_file
options.description: File path to a key file.

options.title: services.grafana.settings.smtp.password
options.description:
Password used for authentication. Please note that the contents of this option
will end up in a world-readable Nix store. Use the file provider
pointing at a reasonably secured file in the local filesystem
to work around that. Look at the documentation for details:
<https://grafana.com/docs/grafana/latest/setup-grafana/configure-grafana/#file-provider>

options.title: services.grafana.settings.smtp.skip_verify
options.description: Verify SSL for SMTP server.

options.title: services.grafana.settings.smtp.startTLS_policy
options.description: StartTLS policy when connecting to server.

options.title: services.grafana.settings.smtp.user
options.description: User used for authentication.

options.title: services.grafana.settings.users.allow_org_create
options.description: Set to `false` to prohibit users from creating new organizations.

options.title: services.grafana.settings.users.allow_sign_up
options.description:
Set to false to prohibit users from being able to sign up / create user accounts.
The admin user can still create users.

options.title: services.grafana.settings.users.auto_assign_org
options.description:
Set to `true` to automatically add new users to the main organization (id 1).
When set to `false,` new users automatically cause a new organization to be created for that new user.
The organization will be created even if the `allow_org_create` setting is set to `false`.

options.title: services.grafana.settings.users.auto_assign_org_id
options.description:
Set this value to automatically add new users to the provided org.
This requires `auto_assign_org` to be set to `true`.
Please make sure that this organization already exists.

options.title: services.grafana.settings.users.auto_assign_org_role
options.description: The role new users will be assigned for the main organization (if the `auto_assign_org` setting is set to `true`).

options.title: services.grafana.settings.users.default_language
options.description: This setting configures the default UI language, which must be a supported IETF language tag, such as `en-US`.

options.title: services.grafana.settings.users.default_theme
options.description: Sets the default UI theme. `system` matches the user's system theme.

options.title: services.grafana.settings.users.hidden_users
options.description:
This is a comma-separated list of usernames.
Users specified here are hidden in the Grafana UI.
They are still visible to Grafana administrators and to themselves.

options.title: services.grafana.settings.users.home_page
options.description:
Path to a custom home page.
Users are only redirected to this if the default home dashboard is used.
It should match a frontend route and contain a leading slash.

options.title: services.grafana.settings.users.login_hint
options.description: Text used as placeholder text on login page for login/username input.

options.title: services.grafana.settings.users.password_hint
options.description: Text used as placeholder text on login page for password input.

options.title: services.grafana.settings.users.user_invite_max_lifetime_duration
options.description:
The duration in time a user invitation remains valid before expiring.
This setting should be expressed as a duration.
Examples: `6h` (hours), `2d` (days), `1w` (week).
The minimum supported duration is `15m` (15 minutes).

options.title: services.grafana.settings.users.verify_email_enabled
options.description: Require email validation before sign up completes.

options.title: services.grafana.settings.users.viewers_can_edit
options.description:
Viewers can access and use Explore and perform temporary edits on panels in dashboards they have access to.
They cannot save their changes.

options.title: services.grafana_reporter.addr
options.description: Listening address.

options.title: services.grafana_reporter.enable
options.description: Whether to enable grafana_reporter.

options.title: services.grafana_reporter.grafana.addr
options.description: Grafana address.

options.title: services.grafana_reporter.grafana.port
options.type: 16 bit unsigned integer; between 0 and 65535 (both inclusive)
options.description: Grafana port.

options.title: services.grafana_reporter.grafana.protocol
options.description: Grafana protocol.

options.title: services.grafana_reporter.port
options.type: 16 bit unsigned integer; between 0 and 65535 (both inclusive)
options.description: Listening port.

options.title: services.grafana_reporter.templateDir
options.description: Optional template directory to use custom tex templates

options.title: services.graphite.carbon.aggregationRules
options.description: Defines if and how received metrics will be aggregated.

options.title: services.graphite.carbon.blacklist
options.description: Any metrics received which match one of the expressions will be dropped.

options.title: services.graphite.carbon.config
options.description: Content of carbon configuration file.
options.default:
''
  [cache]
  # Listen on localhost by default for security reasons
  UDP_RECEIVER_INTERFACE = 127.0.0.1
  PICKLE_RECEIVER_INTERFACE = 127.0.0.1
  LINE_RECEIVER_INTERFACE = 127.0.0.1
  CACHE_QUERY_INTERFACE = 127.0.0.1
  # Do not log every update
  LOG_UPDATES = False
  LOG_CACHE_HITS = False
''

options.title: services.graphite.carbon.enableAggregator
options.description: Whether to enable carbon aggregator, the carbon buffering service.

options.title: services.graphite.carbon.enableCache
options.description: Whether to enable carbon cache, the graphite storage daemon.

options.title: services.graphite.carbon.enableRelay
options.description: Whether to enable carbon relay, the carbon replication and sharding service.

options.title: services.graphite.carbon.relayRules
options.description: Relay rules are used to send certain metrics to a certain backend.

options.title: services.graphite.carbon.rewriteRules
options.description:
Regular expression patterns that can be used to rewrite metric names

options.title: services.h2o.defaultTLSRecommendations
options.description:
By default, H2O, without prejudice, will use as many TLS versions &
cipher suites as it & the TLS library (OpenSSL) can support. The user is
expected to hone settings for the security of their server. Setting some
constraints is recommended, & if unsure about what TLS settings to use,
this option gives curated TLS settings recommendations from Mozilla’s
‘SSL Configuration Generator’ project (see
<https://ssl-config.mozilla.org>) or read more at Mozilla’s Wiki (see
<https://wiki.mozilla.org/Security/Server_Side_TLS>).

modern
: Services with clients that support TLS 1.3 & don’t need backward
  compatibility

intermediate
: General-purpose servers with a variety of clients, recommended for
  almost all systems

old
: Compatible with a number of very old clients, & should be used only as
  a last resort

The default for all virtual hosts can be set with
services.h2o.defaultTLSRecommendations, but this value can be overridden
on a per-host basis using services.h2o.hosts.<name>.tls.recommmendations.
The settings will also be overidden by manual values set with
services.settings.h2o.hosts.<name>.tls.extraSettings.

NOTE: older/weaker ciphers might require overriding the OpenSSL version
of H2O (such as `openssl_legacy`). This can be done with
sevices.settings.h2o.package.

options.title: services.hercules-ci-agent.settings.concurrentTasks
options.type: positive integer, meaning >0, or value "auto" (singular enum)
options.description:
Number of tasks to perform simultaneously.

A task is a single derivation build, an evaluation or an effect run.
At minimum, you need 2 concurrent tasks for `x86_64-linux`
in your cluster, to allow for import from derivation.

`concurrentTasks` can be around the CPU core count or lower if memory is
the bottleneck.

The optimal value depends on the resource consumption characteristics of your workload,
including memory usage and in-task parallelism. This is typically determined empirically.

When scaling, it is generally better to have a double-size machine than two machines,
because each split of resources causes inefficiencies; particularly with regards
to build latency because of extra downloads.

options.title: services.hostapd.enable
options.description:
Whether to enable hostapd, a user space daemon for access point and
authentication servers. It implements IEEE 802.11 access point management,
IEEE 802.1X/WPA/WPA2/EAP Authenticators, RADIUS client, EAP server, and RADIUS
authentication server
.

options.title: services.hostapd.package
options.description: The hostapd package to use.

options.title: services.hostapd.radios
options.description:
This option allows you to define APs for one or multiple physical radios.
At least one radio must be specified.

For each radio, hostapd requires a separate logical interface (like wlp3s0, wlp3s1, ...).
A default interface is usually be created automatically by your system, but to use
multiple radios of a single device, it may be required to create additional logical interfaces
for example by using {option}`networking.wlanInterfaces`.

Each physical radio can only support a single hardware-mode that is configured via
({option}`services.hostapd.radios.<radio>.band`). To create a dual-band
or tri-band AP, you will have to use a device that has multiple physical radios
and supports configuring multiple APs (Refer to valid interface combinations in
{command}`iw list`).

options.title: services.hostapd.radios.<name>.band
options.description:
Specifies the frequency band to use, possible values are 2g for 2.4 GHz,
5g for 5 GHz, 6g for 6 GHz and 60g for 60 GHz.

options.title: services.hostapd.radios.<name>.channel
options.description:
The channel to operate on. Use 0 to enable ACS (Automatic Channel Selection).
Beware that not every device supports ACS in which case {command}`hostapd`
will fail to start.

options.title: services.hostapd.radios.<name>.countryCode
options.description:
Country code (ISO/IEC 3166-1). Used to set regulatory domain.
Set as needed to indicate country in which device is operating.
This can limit available channels and transmit power.
These two octets are used as the first two octets of the Country String
(dot11CountryString).

Setting this will force you to also enable IEEE 802.11d and IEEE 802.11h.

IEEE 802.11d: This advertises the countryCode and the set of allowed channels
and transmit power levels based on the regulatory limits.

IEEE802.11h: This enables radar detection and DFS (Dynamic Frequency Selection)
support if available. DFS support is required on outdoor 5 GHz channels in most
countries of the world.

options.title: services.hostapd.radios.<name>.driver
options.description:
The driver {command}`hostapd` will use.
{var}`nl80211` is used with all Linux mac80211 drivers.
{var}`none` is used if building a standalone RADIUS server that does
not control any wireless/wired driver.
Most applications will probably use the default.

options.title: services.hostapd.radios.<name>.dynamicConfigScripts
options.description:
All of these scripts will be executed in lexicographical order before hostapd
is started, right after the global segment was generated and may dynamically
append global options the generated configuration file.

The first argument will point to the configuration file that you may append to.

options.title: services.hostapd.radios.<name>.networks
options.description:
This defines a BSS, colloquially known as a WiFi network.
You have to specify at least one.

options.title: services.hostapd.radios.<name>.networks.<name>.apIsolate
options.description:
Isolate traffic between stations (clients) and prevent them from
communicating with each other.

options.title: services.hostapd.radios.<name>.networks.<name>.authentication.enableRecommendedPairwiseCiphers
options.description:
Additionally enable the recommended set of pairwise ciphers.
This enables newer secure ciphers, additionally to those defined in {option}`pairwiseCiphers`.
You will have to test whether your hardware supports these by trial-and-error, because
even if `iw list` indicates hardware support, your driver might not expose it.

Beware {command}`hostapd` will most likely not return a useful error message in case
this is enabled despite the driver or hardware not supporting the newer ciphers.
Look out for messages like `Failed to set beacon parameters`.

options.title: services.hostapd.radios.<name>.networks.<name>.authentication.mode
options.description:
Selects the authentication mode for this AP.

- {var}`"none"`: Don't configure any authentication. This will disable wpa alltogether
  and create an open AP. Use {option}`settings` together with this option if you
  want to configure the authentication manually. Any password options will still be
  effective, if set.
- {var}`"wpa2-sha1"`: Not recommended. WPA2-Personal using HMAC-SHA1. Passwords are set
  using {option}`wpaPassword` or preferably by {option}`wpaPasswordFile` or {option}`wpaPskFile`.
- {var}`"wpa2-sha256"`: WPA2-Personal using HMAC-SHA256 (IEEE 802.11i/RSN). Passwords are set
  using {option}`wpaPassword` or preferably by {option}`wpaPasswordFile` or {option}`wpaPskFile`.
- {var}`"wpa3-sae-transition"`: Use WPA3-Personal (SAE) if possible, otherwise fallback
  to WPA2-SHA256. Only use if necessary and switch to the newer WPA3-SAE when possible.
  You will have to specify both {option}`wpaPassword` and {option}`saePasswords` (or one of their alternatives).
- {var}`"wpa3-sae"`: Use WPA3-Personal (SAE). This is currently the recommended way to
  setup a secured WiFi AP (as of March 2023) and therefore the default. Passwords are set
  using either {option}`saePasswords` or {option}`saePasswordsFile`.

options.title: services.hostapd.radios.<name>.networks.<name>.authentication.pairwiseCiphers
options.description:
Set of accepted cipher suites (encryption algorithms) for pairwise keys (unicast packets).
By default this allows just CCMP, which is the only commonly supported secure option.
Use {option}`enableRecommendedPairwiseCiphers` to also enable newer recommended ciphers.

Please refer to the hostapd documentation for allowed values. Generally, only
CCMP or GCMP modes should be considered safe options. Most devices support CCMP while
GCMP and GCMP-256 is often only available with devices supporting WiFi 5 (IEEE 802.11ac) or higher.
CCMP-256 support is rare.

options.title: services.hostapd.radios.<name>.networks.<name>.authentication.saeAddToMacAllow
options.description:
If set, all sae password entries that have a non-wildcard MAC associated to
them will additionally be used to populate the MAC allow list. This is
additional to any entries set via {option}`macAllow` or {option}`macAllowFile`.

options.title: services.hostapd.radios.<name>.networks.<name>.authentication.saePasswords
options.description:
Sets allowed passwords for WPA3-SAE.

The last matching (based on peer MAC address and identifier) entry is used to
select which password to use. An empty string has the special meaning of
removing all previously added entries.

Warning: These entries will get put into a world-readable file in
the Nix store! Using {option}`saePasswordFile` instead is recommended.

Not used when {option}`mode` is {var}`"wpa2-sha1"` or {var}`"wpa2-sha256"`.

options.title: services.hostapd.radios.<name>.networks.<name>.authentication.saePasswords.*.id
options.description:
If this attribute is given with non-zero length, it will set the password identifier
for this entry. It can then only be used with that identifier.

options.title: services.hostapd.radios.<name>.networks.<name>.authentication.saePasswords.*.mac
options.description:
If this attribute is not included, or if is set to the wildcard address (`ff:ff:ff:ff:ff:ff`),
the entry is available for any station (client) to use. If a specific peer MAC address is included,
only a station with that MAC address is allowed to use the entry.

options.title: services.hostapd.radios.<name>.networks.<name>.authentication.saePasswords.*.password
options.description:
The password for this entry. SAE technically imposes no restrictions on
password length or character set. But due to limitations of {command}`hostapd`'s
config file format, a true newline character cannot be parsed.

Warning: This password will get put into a world-readable file in
the Nix store! Prefer using the sibling option {option}`passwordFile` or directly set {option}`saePasswordsFile`.

options.title: services.hostapd.radios.<name>.networks.<name>.authentication.saePasswords.*.passwordFile
options.description:
The password for this entry, read from the given file when starting hostapd.
SAE technically imposes no restrictions on password length or character set.
But due to limitations of {command}`hostapd`'s config file format, a true newline
character cannot be parsed.

options.title: services.hostapd.radios.<name>.networks.<name>.authentication.saePasswords.*.pk
options.description:
If this attribute is given, SAE-PK will be enabled for this connection.
This prevents evil-twin attacks, but a public key is required additionally to connect.
(Essentially adds pubkey authentication such that the client can verify identity of the AP)

options.title: services.hostapd.radios.<name>.networks.<name>.authentication.saePasswords.*.vlanid
options.description: If this attribute is given, all clients using this entry will get tagged with the given VLAN ID.

options.title: services.hostapd.radios.<name>.networks.<name>.authentication.saePasswordsFile
options.description:
Sets the password for WPA3-SAE. Follows the same rules as {option}`saePasswords`,
but reads the entries from the given file to prevent them from being
put into the Nix store.

One entry per line, empty lines and lines beginning with # will be ignored.
Each line must match the following format, although the order of optional
parameters doesn't matter:
`<password>[|mac=<peer mac>][|vlanid=<VLAN ID>][|pk=<m:ECPrivateKey-base64>][|id=<identifier>]`

Not used when {option}`mode` is {var}`"wpa2-sha1"` or {var}`"wpa2-sha256"`.

options.title: services.hostapd.radios.<name>.networks.<name>.authentication.wpaPassword
options.description:
Sets the password for WPA-PSK that will be converted to the pre-shared key.
The password length must be in the range [8, 63] characters. While some devices
may allow arbitrary characters (such as UTF-8) to be used, but the standard specifies
that each character in the passphrase must be an ASCII character in the range [0x20, 0x7e]
(IEEE Std. 802.11i-2004, Annex H.4.1). Use emojis at your own risk.

Not used when {option}`mode` is {var}`"wpa3-sae"`.

Warning: This password will get put into a world-readable file in the Nix store!
Using {option}`wpaPasswordFile` or {option}`wpaPskFile` instead is recommended.

options.title: services.hostapd.radios.<name>.networks.<name>.authentication.wpaPasswordFile
options.description:
Sets the password for WPA-PSK. Follows the same rules as {option}`wpaPassword`,
but reads the password from the given file to prevent the password from being
put into the Nix store.

Not used when {option}`mode` is {var}`"wpa3-sae"`.

options.title: services.hostapd.radios.<name>.networks.<name>.authentication.wpaPskFile
options.description:
Sets the password(s) for WPA-PSK. Similar to {option}`wpaPasswordFile`,
but additionally allows specifying multiple passwords, and some other options.

Each line, except for empty lines and lines starting with #, must contain a
MAC address and either a 64-hex-digit PSK or a password separated with a space.
The password must follow the same rules as outlined in {option}`wpaPassword`.
The special MAC address `00:00:00:00:00:00` can be used to configure PSKs
that any client can use.

An optional key identifier can be added by prefixing the line with `keyid=<keyid_string>`
An optional VLAN ID can be specified by prefixing the line with `vlanid=<VLAN ID>`.
An optional WPS tag can be added by prefixing the line with `wps=<0/1>` (default: 0).
Any matching entry with that tag will be used when generating a PSK for a WPS Enrollee
instead of generating a new random per-Enrollee PSK.

Not used when {option}`mode` is {var}`"wpa3-sae"`.

options.title: services.hostapd.radios.<name>.networks.<name>.bssid
options.description:
Specifies the BSSID for this BSS. Usually determined automatically,
but for now you have to manually specify them when using multiple BSS.
Try assigning related addresses from the locally administered MAC address ranges,
by reusing the hardware address but replacing the second nibble with 2, 6, A or E.
(e.g. if real address is `XX:XX:XX:XX:XX`, try `X2:XX:XX:XX:XX:XX`, `X6:XX:XX:XX:XX:XX`, ...
for the second, third, ... BSS)

options.title: services.hostapd.radios.<name>.networks.<name>.dynamicConfigScripts
options.description:
All of these scripts will be executed in lexicographical order before hostapd
is started, right after the bss segment was generated and may dynamically
append bss options to the generated configuration file.

The first argument will point to the configuration file that you may append to.
The second and third argument will point to this BSS's MAC allow and MAC deny file respectively.
options.example:
{
  exampleDynamicConfig = pkgs.writeShellScript "dynamic-config" ''
    HOSTAPD_CONFIG=$1
    # These always exist, but may or may not be used depending on the actual configuration
    MAC_ALLOW_FILE=$2
    MAC_DENY_FILE=$3

    cat >> "$HOSTAPD_CONFIG" << EOF
    # Add some dynamically generated statements here
    EOF
  '';
}

options.title: services.hostapd.radios.<name>.networks.<name>.group
options.description: Members of this group can access the control socket for this interface.

options.title: services.hostapd.radios.<name>.networks.<name>.ignoreBroadcastSsid
options.description:
Send empty SSID in beacons and ignore probe request frames that do not
specify full SSID, i.e., require stations to know SSID. Note that this does
not increase security, since your clients will then broadcast the SSID instead,
which can increase congestion.

- {var}`"disabled"`: Advertise ssid normally.
- {var}`"empty"`: send empty (length=0) SSID in beacon and ignore probe request for broadcast SSID
- {var}`"clear"`: clear SSID (ASCII 0), but keep the original length (this may be required with some
  legacy clients that do not support empty SSID) and ignore probe requests for broadcast SSID. Only
  use this if empty does not work with your clients.

options.title: services.hostapd.radios.<name>.networks.<name>.logLevel
options.description:
Levels (minimum value for logged events):
0 = verbose debugging
1 = debugging
2 = informational messages
3 = notification
4 = warning

options.title: services.hostapd.radios.<name>.networks.<name>.macAcl
options.description:
Station MAC address -based authentication. The following modes are available:

- {var}`"deny"`: Allow unless listed in {option}`macDeny` (default)
- {var}`"allow"`: Deny unless listed in {option}`macAllow`
- {var}`"radius"`: Use external radius server, but check both {option}`macAllow` and {option}`macDeny` first

Please note that this kind of access control requires a driver that uses
hostapd to take care of management frame processing and as such, this can be
used with driver=hostap or driver=nl80211, but not with driver=atheros.

options.title: services.hostapd.radios.<name>.networks.<name>.macAllow
options.description:
Specifies the MAC addresses to allow if {option}`macAcl` is set to {var}`"allow"` or {var}`"radius"`.
These values will be world-readable in the Nix store. Values will automatically be merged with
{option}`macAllowFile` if necessary.

options.title: services.hostapd.radios.<name>.networks.<name>.macAllowFile
options.description:
Specifies a file containing the MAC addresses to allow if {option}`macAcl` is set to {var}`"allow"` or {var}`"radius"`.
The file should contain exactly one MAC address per line. Comments and empty lines are ignored,
only lines starting with a valid MAC address will be considered (e.g. `11:22:33:44:55:66`) and
any content after the MAC address is ignored.

options.title: services.hostapd.radios.<name>.networks.<name>.macDeny
options.description:
Specifies the MAC addresses to deny if {option}`macAcl` is set to {var}`"deny"` or {var}`"radius"`.
These values will be world-readable in the Nix store. Values will automatically be merged with
{option}`macDenyFile` if necessary.

options.title: services.hostapd.radios.<name>.networks.<name>.macDenyFile
options.description:
Specifies a file containing the MAC addresses to deny if {option}`macAcl` is set to {var}`"deny"` or {var}`"radius"`.
The file should contain exactly one MAC address per line. Comments and empty lines are ignored,
only lines starting with a valid MAC address will be considered (e.g. `11:22:33:44:55:66`) and
any content after the MAC address is ignored.

options.title: services.hostapd.radios.<name>.networks.<name>.settings
options.type: open submodule of attribute set of (atom (bool, int or string) or a list of them for duplicate keys)
options.description:
Extra configuration options to put at the end of this BSS's defintion in the
hostapd.conf for the associated interface. To find out which options are global
and which are per-bss you have to read hostapd's source code, which is non-trivial
and not documented otherwise.

Lists will be converted to multiple definitions of the same key, and booleans to 0/1.
Otherwise, the inputs are not modified or checked for correctness.

options.title: services.hostapd.radios.<name>.networks.<name>.ssid
options.description: SSID to be used in IEEE 802.11 management frames.

options.title: services.hostapd.radios.<name>.networks.<name>.utf8Ssid
options.description: Whether the SSID is to be interpreted using UTF-8 encoding.

options.title: services.hostapd.radios.<name>.noScan
options.description:
Disables scan for overlapping BSSs in HT40+/- mode.
Caution: turning this on will likely violate regulatory requirements!

options.title: services.hostapd.radios.<name>.settings
options.type: open submodule of attribute set of (atom (bool, int or string) or a list of them for duplicate keys)
options.description:
Extra configuration options to put at the end of global initialization, before defining BSSs.
To find out which options are global and which are per-bss you have to read hostapd's source code,
which is non-trivial and not documented otherwise.

Lists will be converted to multiple definitions of the same key, and booleans to 0/1.
Otherwise, the inputs are not modified or checked for correctness.

Directory for the acme challenge which is PUBLIC, don't put certs or keys in here.

options.title: services.httpd.virtualHosts.<name>.addSSL
options.description:
Whether to enable HTTPS in addition to plain HTTP. This will set defaults for

options.title: services.httpd.virtualHosts.<name>.enableUserDir

Whether to enable serving {file}`~/public_html` as

options.title: services.httpd.virtualHosts.<name>.extraConfig

options.title: services.httpd.virtualHosts.<name>.forceSSL

Whether to add a separate nginx server block that permanently redirects (301)

options.title: services.httpd.virtualHosts.<name>.globalRedirect

`documents`, `notificationRules`, `notificationEndpoints`, `checks`, `dbrp`,
`annotations`, `sources`, `scrapers`, `notebooks`, `remotes`, `replications`.

Refer to `influx auth create --help` for a full list with descriptions.

`buckets` grants read access to all associated buckets. Use `readBuckets` to define
more granular access permissions.

to 301, configurable with `redirectCode`) all plain HTTP traffic to
HTTPS. This will set defaults for `listen` to listen on all interfaces
on the respective default ports (80, 443), where the non-SSL listens
are used for the redirect vhosts.

options.title: services.jirafeau.nginxConfig.globalRedirect
options.description:
If set, all requests for this host are redirected (defaults to 301,
configurable with `redirectCode`) to the given hostname.

options.title: services.jirafeau.nginxConfig.http2
options.description:
Whether to enable the HTTP/2 protocol.
Note that (as of writing) due to nginx's implementation, to disable
HTTP/2 you have to disable it on all vhosts that use a given
IP address / port.
If there is one server block configured to enable http2, then it is
enabled for all server blocks on this IP.
See <https://stackoverflow.com/a/39466948/263061>.

options.title: services.jirafeau.nginxConfig.http3
options.description:
Whether to enable the HTTP/3 protocol.
This requires activating the QUIC transport protocol
`services.nginx.virtualHosts.<name>.quic = true;`.
Note that HTTP/3 support is experimental and *not* yet recommended for production.
Read more at <https://quic.nginx.org/>
HTTP/3 availability must be manually advertised, preferably in each location block.

options.title: services.jirafeau.nginxConfig.http3_hq
options.description:
Whether to enable the HTTP/0.9 protocol negotiation used in QUIC interoperability tests.
This requires activating the QUIC transport protocol
`services.nginx.virtualHosts.<name>.quic = true;`.
Note that special application protocol support is experimental and *not* yet recommended for production.
Read more at <https://quic.nginx.org/>

options.title: services.jirafeau.nginxConfig.kTLS
options.description:
Whether to enable kTLS support.
Implementing TLS in the kernel (kTLS) improves performance by significantly
reducing the need for copying operations between user space and the kernel.
Required Nginx version 1.21.4 or later.

options.title: services.jirafeau.nginxConfig.listen
options.description:
Listen addresses and ports for this virtual host.

Note: this option overrides `addSSL`
and `onlySSL`.

If you only want to set the addresses manually and not
the ports, take a look at `listenAddresses`.

options.title: services.jirafeau.nginxConfig.locations.<name>.proxyPass

options.title: services.jirafeau.nginxConfig.locations.<name>.proxyWebsockets

options.title: services.jirafeau.nginxConfig.locations.<name>.root

options.title: services.jirafeau.nginxConfig.locations.<name>.tryFiles

options.title: services.jirafeau.nginxConfig.locations.<name>.uwsgiPass

Adds uwsgi_pass directive and sets recommended proxy headers if
recommendedUwsgiSettings is enabled.

options.title: services.jirafeau.nginxConfig.onlySSL
options.description:
Whether to enable HTTPS and reject plain HTTP connections. This will set
defaults for `listen` to listen on all interfaces on port 443.

options.title: services.jirafeau.nginxConfig.quic
options.description:
Whether to enable the QUIC transport protocol.
Note that QUIC support is experimental and
*not* yet recommended for production.
Read more at <https://quic.nginx.org/>

options.title: services.jirafeau.nginxConfig.redirectCode
options.description:
HTTP status used by `globalRedirect` and `forceSSL`. Possible usecases
include temporary (302, 307) redirects, keeping the request method and
body (307, 308), or explicitly resetting the method to GET (303).
See <https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Redirections>.

options.title: services.jirafeau.nginxConfig.rejectSSL
options.description:
Whether to listen for and reject all HTTPS connections to this vhost. Useful in
[default](#opt-services.nginx.virtualHosts._name_.default)
server blocks to avoid serving the certificate for another vhost. Uses the
`ssl_reject_handshake` directive available in nginx versions
1.19.4 and above.

options.title: services.jirafeau.nginxConfig.reuseport
options.description:
Create an individual listening socket .
It is required to specify only once on one of the hosts.

options.title: services.jirafeau.nginxConfig.root
options.description: The path of the web root directory.

options.title: services.jirafeau.nginxConfig.serverAliases
options.description: Additional names of virtual hosts served by this virtual host configuration.

options.title: services.jirafeau.nginxConfig.serverName
options.description: Name of this virtual host. Defaults to attribute name in virtualHosts.

options.title: services.jirafeau.nginxConfig.sslCertificate

options.title: services.jirafeau.nginxConfig.sslCertificateKey

options.title: services.jirafeau.nginxConfig.sslTrustedCertificate

options.title: services.jirafeau.nginxConfig.useACMEHost
options.description:
A host of an existing Let's Encrypt certificate to use.
This is useful if you have many subdomains and want to avoid hitting the
[rate limit](https://letsencrypt.org/docs/rate-limits).
Alternately, you can generate a certificate through {option}`enableACME`.
*Note that this option does not create any certificates, nor it does add subdomains to existing ones – you will need to create them manually using [](#opt-security.acme.certs).*

options.title: services.jirafeau.package
options.description: The jirafeau package to use.

options.title: services.jirafeau.poolConfig

details on configuration directives.

options.title: services.jitsi-meet.extraConfig

Text to append to {file}`config.js` web application config file.

options.title: services.jitsi-meet.interfaceConfig

options.title: services.jitsi-meet.jibri.enable

Additional configuration is possible with {option}`services.jibri`, and
{option}`services.jibri.finalizeScript` is especially useful.

options.title: services.jitsi-meet.jicofo.enable
options.description:
Whether to enable JiCoFo instance and configure it to connect to Prosody.

Additional configuration is possible with {option}`services.jicofo`.

options.title: services.jitsi-meet.jigasi.enable
options.description:
Whether to enable jigasi instance and configure it to connect to Prosody.

Additional configuration is possible with <option>services.jigasi</option>.

options.title: services.jitsi-meet.nginx.enable
options.description:
Whether to enable nginx virtual host that will serve the javascript application and act as
a proxy for the XMPP server. Further nginx configuration can be done by adapting
{option}`services.nginx.virtualHosts.<hostName>`.
When this is enabled, ACME will be used to retrieve a TLS certificate by default. To disable
this, set the {option}`services.nginx.virtualHosts.<hostName>.enableACME` to
`false` and if appropriate do the same for
{option}`services.nginx.virtualHosts.<hostName>.forceSSL`.

options.title: services.jitsi-meet.prosody.allowners_muc
options.description:
Add module allowners, any user in chat is able to
kick other. Usefull in jitsi-meet to kick ghosts.

options.title: services.jitsi-meet.prosody.enable
options.description:
Whether to configure Prosody to relay XMPP messages between Jitsi Meet components. Turn this
off if you want to configure it manually.

options.title: services.jitsi-meet.prosody.lockdown
options.description:
Whether to disable Prosody features not needed by Jitsi Meet.

The default Prosody configuration assumes that it will be used as a
general-purpose XMPP server rather than as a companion service for
Jitsi Meet. This option reconfigures Prosody to only listen on
localhost without support for TLS termination, XMPP federation or
the file transfer proxy.

options.title: services.jitsi-meet.secureDomain.authentication
options.description: The authentication type to be used by jitsi

options.title: services.jitsi-meet.videobridge.enable
options.description:
Jitsi Videobridge instance and configure it to connect to Prosody.

options.title: services.jitsi-meet.videobridge.passwordFile
options.description:
File containing password to the Prosody account for videobridge.

If `null`, a file with password will be generated automatically. Setting
this option is useful if you plan to connect additional videobridges to the XMPP server.

options.description:
XMPP servers to connect to.

options.title: services.jitsi-videobridge.xmppConfigs.<name>.disableCertificateVerification
options.description: Whether to skip validation of the server's certificate.

options.title: services.jitsi-videobridge.xmppConfigs.<name>.hostName

options.title: services.jitsi-videobridge.xmppConfigs.<name>.mucJids

options.description: Whether to enable jitterentropy-rngd service configuration.

options.title: services.jmusicbot.stateDir

The directory where config.txt and serversettings.json is saved.

Directory below `/var/lib/` to store journalbeat's
