using systemd's StateDirectory mechanism.

options.title: services.journalbeat.tags
options.description: Tags to place on the shipped log messages

options.title: services.journald.audit
options.description:
If enabled systemd-journald will turn on auditing on start-up.
If disabled it will turn it off. If unset it will neither enable nor disable it, leaving the previous state unchanged.

NixOS defaults to leaving this unset as enabling audit without auditd running leads to spamming /dev/kmesg with random messages
and if you enable auditd then auditd is responsible for turning auditing on.

If you want to have audit logs in journald and do not mind audit logs also ending up in /dev/kmesg you can set this option to true.

If you want to for some ununderstandable reason disable auditing if auditd enabled it then you can set this option to false.
It is of NixOS' opinion that setting this to false is definitely the wrong thing to do - but it's an option.

options.title: services.journald.console
options.description: If non-empty, write log messages to the specified TTY device.

options.title: services.journald.extraConfig
options.description:
Extra config options for systemd-journald. See {manpage}`journald.conf(5)`
for available options.

options.title: services.journald.forwardToSyslog
options.description: Whether to forward log messages to syslog.

options.title: services.journald.gateway.cert
options.description:
The path to a file or `AF_UNIX` stream socket to read the server

The certificate must be in PEM format. This option switches
`systemd-journal-gatewayd` into HTTPS mode and must be used together
with {option}`services.journald.gateway.key`.

options.title: services.journald.gateway.enable
options.description: Whether to enable the HTTP gateway to the journal.

options.title: services.journald.gateway.key

The key must be in PEM format.

This key should not be world-readable, and must be readably by the
`systemd-journal-gateway` user.

options.title: services.journald.gateway.merge
options.description:
Serve entries interleaved from all available journals, including other
machines.

This has the same meaning as `--merge` option for
{manpage}`journalctl(1)`.

options.title: services.journald.gateway.port
options.type: 16 bit unsigned integer; between 0 and 65535 (both inclusive)
options.description: The port to listen to.

options.title: services.journald.gateway.system
options.description:
Serve entries from system services and the kernel.

This has the same meaning as `--system` for {manpage}`journalctl(1)`.

options.title: services.journald.gateway.trust
options.description:
Specify the path to a file or `AF_UNIX` stream socket to read a CA
certificate from.

The certificate must be in PEM format.

Setting this option enforces client certificate checking.

options.title: services.journald.gateway.user
options.description:
Serve entries from services for the current user.

This has the same meaning as `--user` for {manpage}`journalctl(1)`.

options.title: services.journald.rateLimitBurst
options.description:
Configures the rate limiting burst limit (number of messages per
interval) that is applied to all messages generated on the system.
This rate limiting is applied per-service, so that two services
which log do not interfere with each other's limit.

Note that the effective rate limit is multiplied by a factor derived
from the available free disk space for the journal as described on
{manpage}`journald.conf(5)`.

Note that the total amount of logs stored is limited by journald settings
such as `SystemMaxUse`, which defaults to 10% the file system size
(capped at max 4GB), and `SystemKeepFree`, which defaults to 15% of the
file system size.

It is thus recommended to compute what period of time that you will be
able to store logs for when an application logs at full burst rate.
With default settings for log lines that are 100 Bytes long, this can
amount to just a few hours.

options.title: services.journald.rateLimitInterval
options.description:
Configures the rate limiting interval that is applied to all
messages generated on the system. This rate limiting is applied
per-service, so that two services which log do not interfere with
each other's limit. The value may be specified in the following
units: s, min, h, ms, us. To turn off any kind of rate limiting,
set either value to 0.

See {option}`services.journald.rateLimitBurst` for important
considerations when setting this value.

options.title: services.journald.remote.enable
options.description: Whether to enable receiving systemd journals from the network.

options.title: services.journald.remote.listen
options.description: Which protocol to listen to.

options.title: services.journald.remote.output
options.description:
The location of the output journal.

In case the output file is not specified, journal files will be created
underneath the selected directory. Files will be called
{file}`remote-hostname.journal`, where the `hostname` part is the
escaped hostname of the source endpoint of the connection, or the
numerical address if the hostname cannot be determined.

options.title: services.journald.remote.port
options.type: 16 bit unsigned integer; between 0 and 65535 (both inclusive)
options.description:
The port to listen to.

Note that this option is used only if
{option}`services.journald.upload.listen` is configured to be either
"https" or "http".

options.title: services.journald.remote.settings
options.type: open submodule of attribute set of section of an INI file (attrs of INI atom (null, bool, int, float or string) or a list of them for duplicate keys)
options.description:
Configuration in the journal-remote configuration file. See
{manpage}`journal-remote.conf(5)` for available options.

options.title: services.journald.remote.settings.Remote.Seal
options.description:
Periodically sign the data in the journal using Forward Secure
Sealing.

options.title: services.journald.remote.settings.Remote.ServerCertificateFile
options.description:
A path to a SSL certificate file in PEM format.

This option can be used with `listen = "https"`. If the path
refers to an `AF_UNIX` stream socket in the file system a
connection is made to it and the certificate read from it.

options.title: services.journald.remote.settings.Remote.ServerKeyFile
options.description:
A path to a SSL secret key file in PEM format.

Note that due to security reasons, `systemd-journal-remote` will
refuse files from the world-readable `/nix/store`. This file
should be readable by the "" user.

This option can be used with `listen = "https"`. If the path
refers to an `AF_UNIX` stream socket in the file system a
connection is made to it and the key read from it.

options.title: services.journald.remote.settings.Remote.SplitMode
options.description:
With "host", a separate output file is used, based on the
hostname of the other endpoint of a connection. With "none", only
one output journal file is used.

options.title: services.journald.remote.settings.Remote.TrustedCertificateFile
options.description:
A path to a SSL CA certificate file in PEM format, or `all`.

If `all` is set, then client certificate checking will be
disabled.

This option can be used with `listen = "https"`. If the path
refers to an `AF_UNIX` stream socket in the file system a
connection is made to it and the certificate read from it.

options.title: services.journald.storage
options.description:
Controls where to store journal data. See
{manpage}`journald.conf(5)` for further information.

options.title: services.journald.upload.enable
options.description: Whether to enable uploading the systemd journal to a remote server.

options.title: services.journald.upload.settings
options.type: open submodule of attribute set of section of an INI file (attrs of INI atom (null, bool, int, float or string) or a list of them for duplicate keys)
options.description:
Configuration for journal-upload. See {manpage}`journal-upload.conf(5)`
for available options.

options.title: services.journald.upload.settings.Upload.NetworkTimeoutSec
options.description:
When network connectivity to the server is lost, this option
configures the time to wait for the connectivity to get restored.

If the server is not reachable over the network for the
configured time, `systemd-journal-upload` exits. Takes a value in
seconds (or in other time units if suffixed with "ms", "min",
"h", etc). For details, see {manpage}`systemd.time(5)`.

options.title: services.journald.upload.settings.Upload.ServerCertificateFile
options.description:
SSL CA certificate in PEM format.

In contrary to what the name suggests, this option configures the
client certificate sent to the remote journal server.

options.title: services.journald.upload.settings.Upload.ServerKeyFile
options.description:
SSL key in PEM format.

In contrary to what the name suggests, this option configures the
client private key sent to the remote journal server.

This key should not be world-readable, and must be readably by
the `systemd-journal` group.

options.title: services.journald.upload.settings.Upload.TrustedCertificateFile
options.description:
SSL CA certificate.

This certificate will be used to check the remote journal HTTPS
server certificate.

options.title: services.journald.upload.settings.Upload.URL

The URL to upload the journal entries to.

See the description of `--url=` option in
{manpage}`systemd-journal-upload(8)` for the description of

options.title: services.journaldriver.logStream
options.description:
Configures the name of the Stackdriver Logging log stream into
which to write journald entries.

This option is required on non-GCP machines, but should not be
set on GCP instances.

options.title: services.journalwatch.accuracy
options.description:
The time window around the interval in which the journalwatch run will be scheduled.

The format is described in {manpage}`systemd.time(7)`.

options.title: services.journalwatch.enable
options.description: If enabled, periodically check the journal with journalwatch and report the results by mail.

options.title: services.journalwatch.extraConfig
options.description:
Extra lines to be added verbatim to the journalwatch/config configuration file.
You can add any commandline argument to the config, without the '--'.
See `journalwatch --help` for all arguments and their description.

options.title: services.journalwatch.filterBlocks
options.description:
filterBlocks can be defined to blacklist journal messages which are not errors.
Each block matches on a log entry field, and the filters in that block then are matched
against all messages with a matching log entry field.

All messages whose PRIORITY is at least 6 (INFO) are processed by journalwatch.
If you don't specify any filterBlocks, PRIORITY is reduced to 5 (NOTICE) by default.

All regular expressions are extended Python regular expressions, for details
see: http://doc.pyschools.com/html/regex.html

options.title: services.journalwatch.filterBlocks.*.filters
options.description:
The filters to apply on all messages which satisfy {option}`match`.
Any of those messages that match any specified filter will be removed from journalwatch's output.
Each filter is an extended Python regular expression.
You can specify multiple filters and separate them by newlines.
Lines starting with '#' are comments. Inline-comments are not permitted.

options.title: services.journalwatch.filterBlocks.*.match
options.description:
Syntax: `field = value`
Specifies the log entry `field` this block should apply to.
If the `field` of a message matches this `value`,
this patternBlock's {option}`filters` are applied.
If `value` starts and ends with a slash, it is interpreted as
an extended python regular expression, if not, it's an exact match.
The journal fields are explained in {manpage}`systemd.journal-fields(7)`.

options.title: services.journalwatch.interval
options.description:
How often to run journalwatch.

The format is described in {manpage}`systemd.time(7)`.

options.title: services.journalwatch.mailBinary
options.description: Sendmail-compatible binary to be used to send the messages.

options.title: services.journalwatch.mailFrom
options.description: Mail address to send journalwatch reports from.

options.title: services.journalwatch.mailTo
options.description: Mail address to send journalwatch reports to.

options.title: services.journalwatch.package
options.description: The journalwatch package to use.

options.title: services.journalwatch.priority
options.description:
Lowest priority of message to be considered.
A value between 7 ("debug"), and 0 ("emerg"). Defaults to 6 ("info").
If you don't care about anything with "info" priority, you can reduce
this to e.g. 5 ("notice") to considerably reduce the amount of
messages without needing many {option}`filterBlocks`.

options.title: services.joycond.enable
options.description: Whether to enable support for Nintendo Pro Controllers and Joycons.

options.title: services.joycond.package
options.description: The joycond package to use.

options.title: services.jupyter.command
options.description:
Which command the service runs. Note that not all jupyter packages
have all commands, e.g. `jupyter lab` isn't present in the `notebook` package.

options.title: services.jupyter.enable
options.description: Whether to enable Jupyter development server.

options.title: services.jupyter.extraEnvironmentVariables
options.type: attribute set of (null or (list of (signed integer or string or absolute path)) or signed integer or string or absolute path)
options.description: Extra environment variables to be set in the runtime context of jupyter notebook

options.title: services.jupyter.extraPackages
options.description: Extra packages to be available in the jupyter runtime environment

options.title: services.jupyter.group
options.description:
Name of the group used to run the jupyter service.
Use this if you want to create a group of users that are able to view the notebook directory's content.

options.title: services.jupyter.ip
options.description: IP address Jupyter will be listening on.

options.title: services.jupyter.kernels
options.type: null or (attribute set of (open submodule of (JSON value)))
options.description:
Declarative kernel config.

Kernels can be declared in any language that supports and has the required
dependencies to communicate with a jupyter server.
In python's case, it means that ipykernel package must always be included in
the list of packages of the targeted environment.

options.title: services.jupyter.kernels.<name>.argv
options.description: Command and arguments to start the kernel.

options.title: services.jupyter.kernels.<name>.displayName
options.description: Name that will be shown to the user.

options.title: services.jupyter.kernels.<name>.env
options.description: Environment variables to set for the kernel.

options.title: services.jupyter.kernels.<name>.extraPaths
options.description: Extra paths to link in kernel directory

options.title: services.jupyter.kernels.<name>.language
options.description: Language of the environment. Typically the name of the binary.

options.title: services.jupyter.kernels.<name>.logo32
options.description: Path to 32x32 logo png.

options.title: services.jupyter.kernels.<name>.logo64
options.description: Path to 64x64 logo png.

options.title: services.jupyter.notebookConfig
options.description:
Raw jupyter config.
Please use the password configuration option to set a password instead of passing it in here.

options.title: services.jupyter.notebookDir
options.description: Root directory for notebooks.

options.title: services.jupyter.package
options.description: The jupyter package to use.

options.title: services.jupyter.password
options.description:
Password to use with notebook.
Can be generated following: <https://jupyter-server.readthedocs.io/en/stable/operators/public-server.html#preparing-a-hashed-password>

options.title: services.jupyter.port
options.type: 16 bit unsigned integer; between 0 and 65535 (both inclusive)
options.description: Port number Jupyter will be listening on.

options.title: services.jupyter.user
options.description:
Name of the user used to run the jupyter service.
For security reason, jupyter should really not be run as root.
If not set (jupyter), the service will create a jupyter user with appropriate settings.

options.title: services.jupyterhub.authentication
options.description:
Jupyterhub authentication to use

There are many authenticators available including: oauth, pam,
ldap, kerberos, etc.

options.title: services.jupyterhub.enable
options.description: Whether to enable Jupyterhub development server.

options.title: services.jupyterhub.extraConfig
options.description:
Extra contents appended to the jupyterhub configuration

Jupyterhub configuration is a normal python file using
Traitlets. <https://jupyterhub.readthedocs.io/en/stable/getting-started/config-basics.html>. The
base configuration of this module was designed to have sane
defaults for configuration but you can override anything since
this is a python file.

options.title: services.jupyterhub.host
options.description: Bind IP JupyterHub will be listening on

options.title: services.jupyterhub.jupyterhubEnv
options.description:
Python environment to run jupyterhub

Customizing will affect the packages available in the hub and
proxy. This will allow packages to be available for the
extraConfig that you may need. This will not normally need to
be changed.

options.title: services.jupyterhub.jupyterlabEnv
options.description:
Python environment to run jupyterlab

Customizing will affect the packages available in the
jupyterlab server and the default kernel provided. This is the
way to customize the jupyterlab extensions and jupyter
notebook extensions. This will not normally need to
be changed.

options.title: services.jupyterhub.kernels
options.type: null or (attribute set of (open submodule of (JSON value)))
options.description:
Declarative kernel config

Kernels can be declared in any language that supports and has
the required dependencies to communicate with a jupyter server.
In python's case, it means that ipykernel package must always be
included in the list of packages of the targeted environment.

options.title: services.jupyterhub.kernels.<name>.argv
options.description: Command and arguments to start the kernel.

options.title: services.jupyterhub.kernels.<name>.displayName
options.description: Name that will be shown to the user.

options.title: services.jupyterhub.kernels.<name>.env
options.description: Environment variables to set for the kernel.

options.title: services.jupyterhub.kernels.<name>.extraPaths
options.description: Extra paths to link in kernel directory

options.title: services.jupyterhub.kernels.<name>.language
options.description: Language of the environment. Typically the name of the binary.

options.title: services.jupyterhub.kernels.<name>.logo32
options.description: Path to 32x32 logo png.

options.title: services.jupyterhub.kernels.<name>.logo64
options.description: Path to 64x64 logo png.

options.title: services.jupyterhub.port
options.type: 16 bit unsigned integer; between 0 and 65535 (both inclusive)
options.description: Port number Jupyterhub will be listening on

options.title: services.jupyterhub.spawner
options.description:
Jupyterhub spawner to use

There are many spawners available including: local process,
systemd, docker, kubernetes, yarn, batch, etc.

options.title: services.jupyterhub.stateDirectory
options.description: Directory for jupyterhub state (token + database)

options.title: services.k3s.agentToken
options.description:
The k3s token agents can use to connect to the server.
This option only makes sense on server nodes (`role = server`).

**WARNING**: This option will expose your token unencrypted in the world-readable nix store.
If this is undesired use the tokenFile option instead.

options.title: services.k3s.agentTokenFile
options.description:
File path containing the k3s token agents can use to connect to the server.
This option only makes sense on server nodes (`role = server`).

options.title: services.k3s.autoDeployCharts
options.description:
Auto deploying Helm charts that are installed by the k3s Helm controller. Avoid using
attribute names that are also used in the [](#opt-services.k3s.manifests) and
[](#opt-services.k3s.charts) options. Manifests with the same name will override
auto deploying charts with the same name.
This option only makes sense on server nodes (`role = server`). See the
[k3s Helm documentation](https://docs.k3s.io/helm) for further information.

**WARNING**: If you have multiple server nodes, and set this option on more than one server,
it is your responsibility to ensure that files stay in sync across those nodes. AddOn content is
not synced between nodes, and k3s cannot guarantee correct behavior if different servers attempt
to deploy conflicting manifests.

options.title: services.k3s.autoDeployCharts.<name>.createNamespace
options.description: Whether to create the target namespace if not present.

options.title: services.k3s.autoDeployCharts.<name>.enable
options.description:
Whether to enable the installation of this Helm chart. Note that setting
this option to `false` will not uninstall the chart from the cluster, if
it was previously installed. Please use the the `--disable` flag or `.skip`
files to delete/disable Helm charts, as mentioned in the
[docs](https://docs.k3s.io/installation/packaged-components#disabling-manifests).

options.title: services.k3s.autoDeployCharts.<name>.extraDeploy
options.description: List of extra Kubernetes manifests to deploy with this Helm chart.

options.title: services.k3s.autoDeployCharts.<name>.extraFieldDefinitions
options.description:
Extra HelmChart field definitions that are merged with the rest of the HelmChart
custom resource. This can be used to set advanced fields or to overwrite
generated fields. See <https://docs.k3s.io/helm#helmchart-field-definitions>
for possible fields.

options.title: services.k3s.autoDeployCharts.<name>.hash
options.description:
The hash of the packaged Helm chart. Only has an effect if `package` is not set.
The Helm chart is fetched during build time and placed as a `.tgz` archive on the
filesystem.

options.title: services.k3s.autoDeployCharts.<name>.name
options.description:
The name of the Helm chart. Only has an effect if `package` is not set.
The Helm chart is fetched during build time and placed as a `.tgz` archive on the
filesystem.

options.title: services.k3s.autoDeployCharts.<name>.package
options.description:
The packaged Helm chart. Overwrites the options `repo`, `name`, `version`
and `hash` in case of conflicts.

options.title: services.k3s.autoDeployCharts.<name>.repo
options.description:
The repo of the Helm chart. Only has an effect if `package` is not set.
The Helm chart is fetched during build time and placed as a `.tgz` archive on the
filesystem.

options.title: services.k3s.autoDeployCharts.<name>.targetNamespace
options.description: The namespace in which the Helm chart gets installed.

options.title: services.k3s.autoDeployCharts.<name>.values
options.description:
Override default chart values via Nix expressions. This is equivalent to setting
values in a `values.yaml` file.

**WARNING**: The values (including secrets!) specified here are exposed unencrypted
in the world-readable nix store.

options.title: services.k3s.autoDeployCharts.<name>.version
options.description:
The version of the Helm chart. Only has an effect if `package` is not set.
The Helm chart is fetched during build time and placed as a `.tgz` archive on the
filesystem.

options.title: services.k3s.charts
options.type: attribute set of (absolute path or package)
options.description:
Packaged Helm charts that are linked to {file}`/var/lib/rancher/k3s/server/static/charts` before k3s starts.
The attribute name will be used as the link target (relative to {file}`/var/lib/rancher/k3s/server/static/charts`).
The specified charts will only be placed on the file system and made available via the Kubernetes APIServer from within the cluster. See the [](#opt-services.k3s.autoDeployCharts) option and the
[k3s Helm controller docs](https://docs.k3s.io/helm#using-the-helm-controller)
to deploy Helm charts. This option only makes sense on server nodes (`role = server`).

options.title: services.k3s.clusterInit
options.description:
Initialize HA cluster using an embedded etcd datastore.

If this option is `false` and `role` is `server`

On a server that was using the default embedded sqlite backend,
enabling this option will migrate to an embedded etcd DB.

If an HA cluster using the embedded etcd datastore was already initialized,
this option has no effect.

This option only makes sense in a server that is not connecting to another server.

If you are configuring an HA cluster with an embedded etcd,
the 1st server must have `clusterInit = true`
and other servers must connect to it using `serverAddr`.

options.title: services.k3s.configPath
options.description: File path containing the k3s YAML config. This is useful when the config is generated (for example on boot).

options.title: services.k3s.containerdConfigTemplate
options.description:
Config template for containerd, to be placed at
`/var/lib/rancher/k3s/agent/etc/containerd/config.toml.tmpl`.
See the docs on [configuring containerd](https://docs.k3s.io/advanced#configuring-containerd).
options.example:
# Base config
{{ template "base" . }}

# Add a custom runtime
[plugins."io.containerd.grpc.v1.cri".containerd.runtimes."custom"]
  runtime_type = "io.containerd.runc.v2"
[plugins."io.containerd.grpc.v1.cri".containerd.runtimes."custom".options]
  BinaryName = "/path/to/custom-container-runtime"

options.title: services.k3s.disable
options.description: Disable default components, see the [K3s documentation](https://docs.k3s.io/installation/packaged-components#using-the---disable-flag).

options.title: services.k3s.disableAgent
options.description: Only run the server. This option only makes sense for a server.

options.title: services.k3s.enable
options.description: Whether to enable k3s.

options.title: services.k3s.environmentFile
options.description: File path containing environment variables for configuring the k3s service in the format of an EnvironmentFile. See {manpage}`systemd.exec(5)`.

options.title: services.k3s.extraFlags
options.description: Extra flags to pass to the k3s command.

options.title: services.k3s.extraKubeProxyConfig
options.description:
Extra configuration to add to the kube-proxy's configuration file. The subset of the kube-proxy's
configuration that can be configured via a file is defined by the
[KubeProxyConfiguration](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/config-api/kube-proxy-config.v1alpha1/)
struct. Note that the kubeconfig param will be overriden by `clientConnection.kubeconfig`, so you must
set the `clientConnection.kubeconfig` option if you want to use `extraKubeProxyConfig`.

options.title: services.k3s.extraKubeletConfig
options.description:
Extra configuration to add to the kubelet's configuration file. The subset of the kubelet's
configuration that can be configured via a file is defined by the
[KubeletConfiguration](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/config-api/kubelet-config.v1beta1/)
struct. See the
[documentation](https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/administer-cluster/kubelet-config-file/)
for further information.

options.title: services.k3s.gracefulNodeShutdown.enable
options.description:
Whether to enable graceful node shutdowns where the kubelet attempts to detect
node system shutdown and terminates pods running on the node. See the
[documentation](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/cluster-administration/node-shutdown/#graceful-node-shutdown)
for further information.
.

options.title: services.k3s.gracefulNodeShutdown.shutdownGracePeriod
options.description:
Specifies the total duration that the node should delay the shutdown by. This is the total
grace period for pod termination for both regular and critical pods.

options.title: services.k3s.gracefulNodeShutdown.shutdownGracePeriodCriticalPods
options.description:
Specifies the duration used to terminate critical pods during a node shutdown. This should be
less than `shutdownGracePeriod`.

options.title: services.k3s.images
options.description:
List of derivations that provide container images.
All images are linked to {file}`/var/lib/rancher/k3s/agent/images` before k3s starts and are consequently imported
by the k3s agent. Consider importing the k3s airgap images archive of the k3s package in
use, if you want to pre-provision this node with all k3s container images. This option
only makes sense on nodes with an enabled agent.

options.title: services.k3s.manifests
options.description:
Auto-deploying manifests that are linked to {file}`/var/lib/rancher/k3s/server/manifests` before k3s starts.
Note that deleting manifest files will not remove or otherwise modify the resources
it created. Please use the the `--disable` flag or `.skip` files to delete/disable AddOns,
as mentioned in the [docs](https://docs.k3s.io/installation/packaged-components#disabling-manifests).
This option only makes sense on server nodes (`role = server`).
Read the [auto-deploying manifests docs](https://docs.k3s.io/installation/packaged-components#auto-deploying-manifests-addons)
for further information.

**WARNING**: If you have multiple server nodes, and set this option on more than one server,
it is your responsibility to ensure that files stay in sync across those nodes. AddOn content is
not synced between nodes, and k3s cannot guarantee correct behavior if different servers attempt
to deploy conflicting manifests.

options.title: services.k3s.manifests.<name>.content
options.type: null or (attribute set) or list of (attribute set)
options.description:
Content of the manifest file. A single attribute set will
generate a single document YAML file. A list of attribute sets
will generate multiple documents separated by `---` in a single
YAML file.

options.title: services.k3s.manifests.<name>.enable
options.description: Whether this manifest file should be generated.

options.title: services.k3s.manifests.<name>.source
options.description: Path of the source `.yaml` file.

options.title: services.k3s.manifests.<name>.target
options.description:
Name of the symlink (relative to {file}`/var/lib/rancher/k3s/server/manifests`).
Defaults to the attribute name.

options.title: services.k3s.nodeIP
options.description: IPv4/IPv6 addresses to advertise for node.

options.title: services.k3s.nodeLabel
options.description: Registering and starting kubelet with set of labels.

options.title: services.k3s.nodeName
options.description: Node name.

options.title: services.k3s.nodeTaint
options.description: Registering kubelet with set of taints.

options.title: services.k3s.package
options.description: The k3s package to use.

options.title: services.k3s.role
options.description:
Whether k3s should run as a server or agent.

If it's a server:

- By default it also runs workloads as an agent.
- Starts by default as a standalone server using an embedded sqlite datastore.
- Configure `clusterInit = true` to switch over to embedded etcd datastore and enable HA mode.
- Configure `serverAddr` to join an already-initialized HA cluster.

If it's an agent:

- `serverAddr` is required.

options.title: services.k3s.selinux
options.description: Enable SELinux in containerd.

options.title: services.k3s.serverAddr
options.description:
The k3s server to connect to.

Servers and agents need to communicate each other. Read
[the networking docs](https://rancher.com/docs/k3s/latest/en/installation/installation-requirements/#networking)
to know how to configure the firewall.

options.title: services.k3s.token
options.description:
The k3s token to use when connecting to a server.

**WARNING**: This option will expose your token unencrypted in the world-readable nix store.
If this is undesired use the tokenFile option instead.

options.title: services.k3s.tokenFile
options.description: File path containing the k3s token to use when connecting to a server.

options.title: services.kanata.enable
options.description: Whether to enable kanata, a tool to improve keyboard comfort and usability with advanced customization.

options.title: services.kanata.keyboards
options.description: Keyboard configurations.

options.title: services.kanata.keyboards.<name>.config
options.description:
Configuration other than `defcfg`.

See [the upstream documentation](https://github.com/jtroo/kanata/blob/main/docs/config.adoc) and [example config files](https://github.com/jtroo/kanata/tree/main/cfg_samples) for more information.
options.example:
''
  (defsrc
    caps)
  
  (deflayermap (default-layer)
    ;; tap caps lock as caps lock, hold caps lock as left control
    caps (tap-hold 100 100 caps lctl))
''

options.title: services.kanata.keyboards.<name>.configFile
options.description:
The config file.

By default, it is generated by values from other kanata
module options.

You can also set it to your own full config file which
overrides all other kanata module options.  See [the upstream documentation](https://github.com/jtroo/kanata/blob/main/docs/config.adoc) and [example config files](https://github.com/jtroo/kanata/tree/main/cfg_samples) for more information.
options.default: "A config file generated by values from other kanata module options."

options.title: services.kanata.keyboards.<name>.devices
options.description:
Paths to keyboard devices.

An empty list, the default value, lets kanata detect which
input devices are keyboards and intercept them all.

options.title: services.kanata.keyboards.<name>.extraArgs
options.description: Extra command line arguments passed to kanata.

options.title: services.kanata.keyboards.<name>.extraDefCfg
options.description:
Configuration of `defcfg` other than `linux-dev` (generated
from the devices option) and
`linux-continue-if-no-devs-found` (hardcoded to be yes).

See [the upstream documentation](https://github.com/jtroo/kanata/blob/main/docs/config.adoc) and [example config files](https://github.com/jtroo/kanata/tree/main/cfg_samples) for more information.

options.title: services.kanata.keyboards.<name>.port
options.type: null or 16 bit unsigned integer; between 0 and 65535 (both inclusive)
options.description: Port to run the TCP server on. `null` will not run the server.

options.title: services.kanata.package
options.description:
The kanata package to use. ::: {.note}
If {option}`danger-enable-cmd` is enabled in any of the keyboards, the
`kanata-with-cmd` package should be used.
:::

options.title: services.kanboard.dataDir
options.description: Default data folder for Kanboard.

options.title: services.kanboard.domain
options.description: FQDN for the Kanboard instance.

options.title: services.kanboard.enable
options.description: Whether to enable Kanboard.

options.title: services.kanboard.group
options.description: Group under which Kanboard runs.

options.title: services.kanboard.nginx
options.description:
With this option, you can customize an NGINX virtual host which already
has sensible defaults for Kanboard. Set to `{ }` if you do not need any
customization for the virtual host. If enabled, then by default, the
{option}`serverName` is `${domain}`. If this is set to null (the
default), no NGINX virtual host will be configured.

options.title: services.kanboard.nginx.acmeFallbackHost
options.description:
Host which to proxy requests to if ACME challenge is not found. Useful
if you want multiple hosts to be able to verify the same domain name.

With this option, you could request certificates for the present domain
with an ACME client that is running on another host, which you would
specify here.

options.title: services.kanboard.nginx.acmeRoot
options.description:
Directory for the ACME challenge, which is **public**. Don't put certs or keys in here.
Set to null to inherit from config.security.acme.

options.title: services.kanboard.nginx.addSSL
options.description:
Whether to enable HTTPS in addition to plain HTTP. This will set defaults for
`listen` to listen on all interfaces on the respective default
ports (80, 443).

options.title: services.kanboard.nginx.basicAuth
options.description:
Basic Auth protection for a vhost.

WARNING: This is implemented to store the password in plain text in the
Nix store.

options.title: services.kanboard.nginx.basicAuthFile
options.description:
Basic Auth password file for a vhost.
Can be created by running {command}`nix-shell --packages apacheHttpd --run 'htpasswd -B -c FILENAME USERNAME'`.

options.title: services.kanboard.nginx.default
options.description: Makes this vhost the default.

options.title: services.kanboard.nginx.enableACME
options.description:
Whether to ask Let's Encrypt to sign a certificate for this vhost.
Alternately, you can use an existing certificate through {option}`useACMEHost`.

options.title: services.kanboard.nginx.extraConfig
options.description: These lines go to the end of the vhost verbatim.

options.title: services.kanboard.nginx.forceSSL
options.description:
Whether to add a separate nginx server block that redirects (defaults
to 301, configurable with `redirectCode`) all plain HTTP traffic to
HTTPS. This will set defaults for `listen` to listen on all interfaces
on the respective default ports (80, 443), where the non-SSL listens
are used for the redirect vhosts.

options.title: services.kanboard.nginx.globalRedirect
options.description:
If set, all requests for this host are redirected (defaults to 301,
configurable with `redirectCode`) to the given hostname.

options.title: services.kanboard.nginx.http2
options.description:
Whether to enable the HTTP/2 protocol.
Note that (as of writing) due to nginx's implementation, to disable
HTTP/2 you have to disable it on all vhosts that use a given
IP address / port.
If there is one server block configured to enable http2, then it is
enabled for all server blocks on this IP.
See <https://stackoverflow.com/a/39466948/263061>.

options.title: services.kanboard.nginx.http3
options.description:
Whether to enable the HTTP/3 protocol.
This requires activating the QUIC transport protocol
`services.nginx.virtualHosts.<name>.quic = true;`.
Note that HTTP/3 support is experimental and *not* yet recommended for production.
Read more at <https://quic.nginx.org/>
HTTP/3 availability must be manually advertised, preferably in each location block.

options.title: services.kanboard.nginx.http3_hq
options.description:
Whether to enable the HTTP/0.9 protocol negotiation used in QUIC interoperability tests.
This requires activating the QUIC transport protocol
`services.nginx.virtualHosts.<name>.quic = true;`.
Note that special application protocol support is experimental and *not* yet recommended for production.
Read more at <https://quic.nginx.org/>

options.title: services.kanboard.nginx.kTLS
options.description:
Whether to enable kTLS support.
Implementing TLS in the kernel (kTLS) improves performance by significantly
reducing the need for copying operations between user space and the kernel.
Required Nginx version 1.21.4 or later.

options.title: services.kanboard.nginx.listen
options.description:
Listen addresses and ports for this virtual host.
IPv6 addresses must be enclosed in square brackets.
Note: this option overrides `addSSL`
and `onlySSL`.

If you only want to set the addresses manually and not
the ports, take a look at `listenAddresses`.

options.description: Listen address.

options.title: services.kanboard.nginx.listen.*.extraParameters
options.description: Extra parameters of this listen directive.

options.title: services.kanboard.nginx.listen.*.port
options.type: null or 16 bit unsigned integer; between 0 and 65535 (both inclusive)
options.description:
Port number to listen on.
If unset and the listen address is not a socket then nginx defaults to 80.

options.title: services.kanboard.nginx.listen.*.proxyProtocol
options.description: Enable PROXY protocol.

options.title: services.kanboard.nginx.listen.*.ssl
options.description: Enable SSL.

options.title: services.kanboard.nginx.listenAddresses
options.description:
Listen addresses for this virtual host.
Compared to `listen` this only sets the addresses
and the ports are chosen automatically.

Note: This option overrides `enableIPv6`

options.title: services.keepalived.enable
options.description: Whether to enable Keepalived.

options.description:
Extra lines to be added verbatim to the 'global_defs' block of the
configuration file

options.title: services.keepalived.openFirewall
options.description: Whether to automatically allow VRRP and AH packets in the firewall.

options.title: services.keepalived.package
options.description: The keepalived package to use.

options.title: services.keepalived.secretFile
options.description:
Environment variables from this file will be interpolated into the
final config file using envsubst with this syntax: `$ENVIRONMENT`
or `${VARIABLE}`.
The file should contain lines formatted as `SECRET_VAR=SECRET_VALUE`.
This is useful to avoid putting secrets into the nix store.

options.title: services.keepalived.snmp.enable
options.description: Whether to enable the builtin AgentX subagent.

options.title: services.keepalived.snmp.enableChecker
options.description: Enable SNMP handling of checker element of KEEPALIVED MIB.

options.title: services.keepalived.snmp.enableKeepalived
options.description: Enable SNMP handling of vrrp element of KEEPALIVED MIB.

options.title: services.keepalived.snmp.enableRfc
options.description: Enable SNMP handling of RFC2787 and RFC6527 VRRP MIBs.

options.title: services.keepalived.snmp.enableRfcV2
options.description: Enable SNMP handling of RFC2787 VRRP MIB.

options.title: services.keepalived.snmp.enableRfcV3
options.description: Enable SNMP handling of RFC6527 VRRP MIB.

options.title: services.keepalived.snmp.enableTraps
options.description: Enable SNMP traps.

options.title: services.keepalived.snmp.socket
options.description:
Socket to use for connecting to SNMP master agent. If this value is
set to null, keepalived's default will be used, which is
unix:/var/agentx/master, unless using a network namespace, when the
default is udp:localhost:705.

options.title: services.keepalived.vrrpInstances
options.description: Declarative vhost config

options.title: services.keepalived.vrrpInstances.<name>.extraConfig
options.description: Extra lines to be added verbatim to the vrrp_instance section.

options.title: services.keepalived.vrrpInstances.<name>.interface
options.description: Interface for inside_network, bound by vrrp.

options.title: services.keepalived.vrrpInstances.<name>.noPreempt
options.description:
VRRP will normally preempt a lower priority machine when a higher
priority machine comes online. "nopreempt" allows the lower priority
machine to maintain the master role, even when a higher priority machine
comes back online. NOTE: For this to work, the initial state of this
entry must be BACKUP.

options.title: services.keepalived.vrrpInstances.<name>.priority
options.description:
For electing MASTER, highest priority wins. To be MASTER, make 50 more
than other machines.

options.title: services.keepalived.vrrpInstances.<name>.state
options.description:
Initial state. As soon as the other machine(s) come up, an election will
be held and the machine with the highest "priority" will become MASTER.
So the entry here doesn't matter a whole lot.

options.title: services.keepalived.vrrpInstances.<name>.trackInterfaces
options.description: List of network interfaces to monitor for health tracking.

options.title: services.keepalived.vrrpInstances.<name>.trackScripts
options.description: List of script names to invoke for health tracking.

options.title: services.keepalived.vrrpInstances.<name>.unicastPeers
options.description:
Do not send VRRP adverts over VRRP multicast group. Instead it sends
adverts to the following list of ip addresses using unicast design
fashion. It can be cool to use VRRP FSM and features in a networking
environment where multicast is not supported! IP Addresses specified can
IPv4 as well as IPv6.

options.title: services.keepalived.vrrpInstances.<name>.unicastSrcIp
options.description:
Default IP for binding vrrpd is the primary IP on interface. If you
want to hide location of vrrpd, use this IP as src_addr for unicast
vrrp packets.

options.title: services.keepalived.vrrpInstances.<name>.useVmac
options.description: Use VRRP Virtual MAC.

options.title: services.keepalived.vrrpInstances.<name>.virtualIps
options.description: Declarative vhost config

options.title: services.keepalived.vrrpInstances.<name>.virtualIps.*.addr
options.description: IP address, optionally with a netmask: IPADDR[/MASK]

options.title: services.keepalived.vrrpInstances.<name>.virtualIps.*.brd
options.description: The broadcast address on the interface.

options.title: services.keepalived.vrrpInstances.<name>.virtualIps.*.dev
options.description: The name of the device to add the address to.

options.title: services.keepalived.vrrpInstances.<name>.virtualIps.*.label
options.description:
Each address may be tagged with a label string. In order to preserve
compatibility with Linux-2.0 net aliases, this string must coincide with
the name of the device or must be prefixed with the device name followed
by colon.

options.title: services.keepalived.vrrpInstances.<name>.virtualIps.*.scope
options.description: The scope of the area where this address is valid.

options.title: services.keepalived.vrrpInstances.<name>.virtualRouterId
options.description:
Arbitrary unique number 1..255. Used to differentiate multiple instances
of vrrpd running on the same NIC (and hence same socket).

options.title: services.keepalived.vrrpInstances.<name>.vmacInterface
options.description:
Name of the vmac interface to use. keepalived will come up with a name
if you don't specify one.

options.title: services.keepalived.vrrpInstances.<name>.vmacXmitBase
options.description: Send/Recv VRRP messages from base interface instead of VMAC interface.

options.title: services.keepalived.vrrpScripts
options.description: Declarative vrrp script config

options.title: services.keepalived.vrrpScripts.<name>.extraConfig
options.description: Extra lines to be added verbatim to the vrrp_script section.

options.title: services.keepalived.vrrpScripts.<name>.fall
options.description: Required number of failures for KO transition.

options.title: services.keepalived.vrrpScripts.<name>.group
options.description: Name of group to run the script under. Defaults to user group.

options.title: services.keepalived.vrrpScripts.<name>.interval
options.description: Seconds between script invocations.

options.title: services.keepalived.vrrpScripts.<name>.rise
options.description: Required number of successes for OK transition.

options.title: services.keepalived.vrrpScripts.<name>.script
options.description: (Path of) Script command to execute followed by args, i.e. cmd [args]...

options.title: services.keepalived.vrrpScripts.<name>.timeout
options.description: Seconds after which script is considered to have failed.

options.title: services.keepalived.vrrpScripts.<name>.user
options.description: Name of user to run the script under.

options.title: services.keepalived.vrrpScripts.<name>.weight
options.description: Following a failure, adjust the priority by this weight.

options.title: services.kerberos_server.enable

options.description: Extra arguments to pass to the KDC process. See {manpage}`kdc(8)`.

options.title: services.kerberos_server.settings
options.type: open submodule of attribute set of attribute set of ((list of attribute set of ((list of (signed integer or string or boolean)) or signed integer or string or boolean)) or attribute set of ((list of (signed integer or string or boolean)) or signed integer or string or boolean) or (list of (signed integer or string or boolean)) or signed integer or string or boolean)
options.description:
Settings for the kerberos server of choice.

See the following documentation:
- Heimdal: {manpage}`kdc.conf(5)`
- MIT Kerberos: <https://web.mit.edu/kerberos/krb5-1.21/doc/admin/conf_files/kdc_conf.html>

options.title: services.kerberos_server.settings.include
options.type: (list of absolute path) or absolute path convertible to it
options.description: Files to include in the Kerberos configuration.

options.title: services.kerberos_server.settings.includedir
options.type: (list of absolute path) or absolute path convertible to it
options.description: Directories containing files to include in the Kerberos configuration.

options.title: services.kerberos_server.settings.module
options.type: (list of absolute path) or absolute path convertible to it
options.description: Modules to obtain Kerberos configuration from.

options.title: services.kerberos_server.settings.realms
options.type: attribute set of (open submodule of attribute set of ((list of attribute set of ((list of (signed integer or string or boolean)) or signed integer or string or boolean)) or attribute set of ((list of (signed integer or string or boolean)) or signed integer or string or boolean) or (list of (signed integer or string or boolean)) or signed integer or string or boolean))
options.description: The realm(s) to serve keys for.

options.title: services.kerberos_server.settings.realms.<name>.acl
options.description: The privileges granted to a user.

options.title: services.kerberos_server.settings.realms.<name>.acl.*.access
options.type: (list of (one of "all", "add", "cpw", "delete", "get-keys", "get", "list", "modify")) or string convertible to it
options.description:
The changes the principal is allowed to make.

:::{.important}
The "all" permission does not imply the "get-keys" permission. This
is consistent with the behavior of both MIT Kerberos and Heimdal.
:::

:::{.warning}
Value "all" is allowed as a list member only if it appears alone
or accompanied by "get-keys". Any other combination involving
"all" will raise an exception.
:::

options.title: services.kerberos_server.settings.realms.<name>.acl.*.principal
options.description: Which principal the rule applies to

options.title: services.kerberos_server.settings.realms.<name>.acl.*.target
options.description: The principals that 'access' applies to.

options.title: services.keter.bundle.appName
options.description: The name keter assigns to this bundle

options.title: services.keter.bundle.domain
options.description: The domain keter will bind to

options.title: services.keter.bundle.executable
options.description: The executable to be run

options.title: services.keter.bundle.secretScript
options.description: Allows loading of private environment variables

options.title: services.keter.enable
options.description:
Whether to enable keter, a web app deployment manager.
Note that this module only support loading of webapps:
Keep an old app running and swap the ports when the new one is booted
.

options.title: services.keter.globalKeterConfig
options.description: Global config for keter, see <https://github.com/snoyberg/keter/blob/master/etc/keter-config.yaml> for reference

options.title: services.keter.globalKeterConfig.ip-from-header
options.description: You want that ip-from-header in the nginx setup case. It allows nginx setting the original ip address rather then it being localhost (due to reverse proxying)

options.title: services.keter.globalKeterConfig.listeners
options.description:
You want that ip-from-header in
the nginx setup case.
It allows nginx setting the original ip address rather
then it being localhost (due to reverse proxying).
However if you configure keter to accept connections
directly you may want to set this to false.

options.title: services.keter.globalKeterConfig.listeners.*.host
options.description: host

options.title: services.keter.globalKeterConfig.listeners.*.port
options.type: 16 bit unsigned integer; between 0 and 65535 (both inclusive)
options.description: port

options.title: services.keter.globalKeterConfig.rotate-logs
options.description:
emits keter logs and it's applications to stderr.
which allows journald to capture them.
Set to true to let keter put the logs in files
(useful on non systemd systems, this is the old approach
where keter handled log management)

options.title: services.keter.package
options.description: The keter package to use.

options.title: services.keter.root
options.description: Mutable state folder for keter

options.title: services.keybase.enable
options.description: Whether to start the Keybase service.

options.title: services.keycloak.database.caCert
options.description:
The SSL / TLS CA certificate that verifies the identity of the
database server.

Required when PostgreSQL is used and SSL is turned on.

For MySQL, if left at `null`, the default
Java keystore is used, which should suffice if the server
certificate is issued by an official CA.

options.title: services.keycloak.database.createLocally
options.description:
Whether a database should be automatically created on the
local host. Set this to false if you plan on provisioning a
local database yourself. This has no effect if
services.keycloak.database.host is customized.

options.title: services.keycloak.database.host
options.description:
Hostname of the database to connect to.

For PostgreSQL, this can also be a path to a Unix socket
directory (e.g., `/run/postgresql`) to use peer authentication.
This requires adding `junixsocket-common` and `junixsocket-native-common`
to [](#opt-services.keycloak.plugins).

options.title: services.keycloak.database.name
options.description:
Database name to use when connecting to an external or
manually provisioned database; has no effect when a local
database is automatically provisioned.

To use this with a local database, set [](#opt-services.keycloak.database.createLocally) to
`false` and create the database and user
manually.

options.title: services.keycloak.database.passwordFile
options.description:
The path to a file containing the database password.

Not required when using Unix socket authentication (peer auth)
by setting `host` to a socket path like `/run/postgresql`.

options.title: services.keycloak.database.port
options.type: 16 bit unsigned integer; between 0 and 65535 (both inclusive)
options.description: Port of the database to connect to.

options.title: services.keycloak.database.type
options.description: The type of database Keycloak should connect to.

options.title: services.keycloak.database.useSSL
options.description:
Whether the database connection should be secured by SSL / TLS.

Defaults to `false` for localhost and Unix socket connections.

options.title: services.keycloak.database.username
options.description:
Username to use when connecting to an external or manually
provisioned database; has no effect when a local database is
automatically provisioned.

To use this with a local database, set [](#opt-services.keycloak.database.createLocally) to
`false` and create the database and user
manually.

options.title: services.keycloak.enable
options.description:
Whether to enable the Keycloak identity and access management
server.

options.title: services.keycloak.initialAdminPassword
options.description:
Initial password set for the temporary `admin` user.
The password is not stored safely and should be changed
immediately in the admin panel.

See [Admin bootstrap and recovery](https://www.keycloak.org/server/bootstrap-admin-recovery) for details.

options.title: services.keycloak.package
options.description: The keycloak package to use.

options.title: services.keycloak.plugins
options.description:
Keycloak plugin jar, ear files or derivations containing
them. Packaged plugins are available through
`pkgs.keycloak.plugins`.

options.title: services.keycloak.realmFiles
options.description:
Realm files that the server is going to import during startup.
If a realm already exists in the server, the import operation is
skipped. Importing the master realm is not supported. All files are
expected to be in `json` format. See the
[documentation](https://www.keycloak.org/server/importExport) for
further information.

options.title: services.keycloak.settings
options.type: open submodule of attribute set of (null or string or signed integer or boolean or attribute set of absolute path)
options.description:
Configuration options corresponding to parameters set in
{file}`conf/keycloak.conf`.

Most available options are documented at <https://www.keycloak.org/server/all-config>.

Options containing secret data should be set to an attribute
set containing the attribute `_secret` - a
string pointing to a file containing the value the option
should be set to. See the example to get a better picture of
this: in the resulting
{file}`conf/keycloak.conf` file, the
`https-key-store-password` key will be set
to the contents of the
{file}`/run/keys/store_password` file.

options.title: services.keycloak.settings.hostname
options.description:
The hostname part of the public URL used as base for
all frontend requests.

See <https://www.keycloak.org/server/hostname>
for more information about hostname configuration.

options.title: services.keycloak.settings.hostname-backchannel-dynamic
options.description:
Enables dynamic resolving of backchannel URLs,
including hostname, scheme, port and context path.

See <https://www.keycloak.org/server/hostname>
for more information about hostname configuration.

options.title: services.keycloak.settings.http-host
options.description: On which address Keycloak should accept new connections.

options.title: services.keycloak.settings.http-port
options.type: 16 bit unsigned integer; between 0 and 65535 (both inclusive)
options.description: On which port Keycloak should listen for new HTTP connections.

options.title: services.keycloak.settings.http-relative-path
options.description:
The path relative to `/` for serving
resources.

::: {.note}
In versions of Keycloak using Wildfly (<17),
this defaulted to `/auth`. If
upgrading from the Wildfly version of Keycloak,
i.e. a NixOS version before 22.05, you'll likely
want to set this to `/auth` to
keep compatibility with your clients.

See <https://www.keycloak.org/migration/migrating-to-quarkus>
for more information on migrating from Wildfly to Quarkus.
:::

options.title: services.keycloak.settings.https-port
options.type: 16 bit unsigned integer; between 0 and 65535 (both inclusive)
options.description: On which port Keycloak should listen for new HTTPS connections.

options.title: services.keycloak.sslCertificate
options.description:
The path to a PEM formatted certificate to use for TLS/SSL
connections.

options.title: services.keycloak.sslCertificateKey
options.description:
The path to a PEM formatted private key to use for TLS/SSL
connections.

options.title: services.keycloak.themes
options.description:
Additional theme packages for Keycloak. Each theme is linked into
subdirectory with a corresponding attribute name.

Theme packages consist of several subdirectories which provide
different theme types: for example, `account`,
`login` etc. After adding a theme to this option you
can select it by its name in Keycloak administration console.

options.title: services.keyd.enable
options.description: Whether to enable keyd, a key remapping daemon.

options.title: services.keyd.keyboards

options.title: services.keyd.keyboards.<name>.extraConfig
options.description:
Extra configuration that is appended to the end of the file.
**Do not** write `ids` section here, use a separate option for it.
You can use this option to define compound layers that must always be defined after the layer they are comprised.

options.title: services.keyd.keyboards.<name>.ids

options.title: services.keyd.keyboards.<name>.settings
options.type: attribute set of section of an INI file (attrs of INI atom (null, bool, int, float or string))
options.description:
Configuration, except `ids` section, that is written to {file}`/etc/keyd/<keyboard>.conf`.
Appropriate names can be used to write non-alpha keys, for example "equal" instead of "=" sign (see <https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/issues/236622>).
See <https://github.com/rvaiya/keyd> how to configure.

Structural Kimai's local.yaml configuration.

options.title: services.libeufin.bank.settings.libeufin-bank.SUGGESTED_WITHDRAWAL_EXCHANGE
options.description:
Exchange that is suggested to wallets when withdrawing.

Note that, in order for withdrawals to work, your libeufin-bank
must be able to communicate with and send money etc. to the bank
at which the exchange used for withdrawals has its bank account.

If you also have your own bank and taler exchange network, you
probably want to set one of your exchange's url here instead of
the demo exchange.

This setting must always be set in order for the Android app to
not crash during the withdrawal process but the exchange to be
used can always be changed in the app.

floating point non-negative numbers. This only applies to the custom profile.

options.title: services.libinput.mouse.accelPointsMotion
options.type: null or (list of (signed integer or floating point number))
options.description:
Sets the points of the (pointer) motion acceleration function. The value must be a
list of floating point non-negative numbers. This only applies to the custom profile.

options.title: services.libinput.mouse.accelPointsScroll
options.type: null or (list of (signed integer or floating point number))
options.description:
Sets the points of the scroll acceleration function. The value must be a list of
floating point non-negative numbers. This only applies to the custom profile.

options.title: services.libinput.mouse.accelProfile
options.description:
Sets the pointer acceleration profile to the given profile.
Permitted values are `adaptive`, `flat`, `custom`.
Not all devices support this option or all profiles.
If a profile is unsupported, the default profile for this is used.
`flat`: Pointer motion is accelerated by a constant
(device-specific) factor, depending on the current speed.
`adaptive`: Pointer acceleration depends on the input speed.
This is the default profile for most devices.
`custom`: Allows the user to define a custom acceleration function.
To define custom functions use the accelPoints<Fallback/Motion/Scroll>
and accelStep<Fallback/Motion/Scroll> options.

options.title: services.libinput.mouse.accelSpeed
options.description:
Cursor acceleration (how fast speed increases from minSpeed to maxSpeed).
This only applies to the flat or adaptive profile.

options.title: services.libinput.mouse.accelStepFallback
options.type: null or signed integer or floating point number
options.description:
Sets the step between the points of the fallback acceleration function. When a step of
0.0 is provided, libinput's Fallback acceleration function is used. This only applies
to the custom profile.

options.title: services.libinput.mouse.accelStepMotion
options.type: null or signed integer or floating point number
options.description:
Sets the step between the points of the (pointer) motion acceleration function. When a
step of 0.0 is provided, libinput's Fallback acceleration function is used. This only
applies to the custom profile.

options.title: services.libinput.mouse.accelStepScroll
options.type: null or signed integer or floating point number
options.description:
Sets the step between the points of the scroll acceleration function. When a step of
0.0 is provided, libinput's Fallback acceleration function is used. This only applies
to the custom profile.

options.title: services.libinput.mouse.additionalOptions
services.libinput.mouse.buttonMapping
options.description:
Sets the logical button mapping for this device, see {manpage}`XSetPointerMapping(3)`. The string  must
be  a  space-separated  list  of  button mappings in the order of the logical buttons on the
device, starting with button 1.  The default mapping is "1 2 3 ... 32". A mapping of 0 deac‐
tivates the button. Multiple buttons can have the same mapping.  Invalid mapping strings are
discarded and the default mapping is used for all buttons.  Buttons  not  specified  in  the
user's mapping use the default mapping. See section BUTTON MAPPING for more details.

options.title: services.libinput.mouse.calibrationMatrix
options.description:
A string of 9 space-separated floating point numbers. Sets the calibration matrix to the
3x3 matrix where the first row is (abc), the second row is (def) and the third row is (ghi).

options.title: services.libinput.mouse.clickMethod
options.description:
Enables a click method. Permitted values are `none`,
`buttonareas`, `clickfinger`.
Not all devices support all methods, if an option is unsupported,
the default click method for this device is used.

options.title: services.libinput.mouse.dev
options.description:
Path for mouse device.  Set to `null` to apply to any
auto-detected mouse.

options.title: services.libinput.mouse.disableWhileTyping
options.description: Disable input method while typing.

options.title: services.libinput.mouse.horizontalScrolling
options.description:
Enables or disables horizontal scrolling. When disabled, this driver will discard any
horizontal scroll events from libinput. This does not disable horizontal scroll events
from libinput; it merely discards the horizontal axis from any scroll events.

options.title: services.libinput.mouse.leftHanded
options.description: Enables left-handed button orientation, i.e. swapping left and right buttons.

options.title: services.libinput.mouse.middleEmulation
options.description:
Enables middle button emulation. When enabled, pressing the left and right buttons
simultaneously produces a middle mouse button click.

options.title: services.libinput.mouse.naturalScrolling
options.description: Enables or disables natural scrolling behavior.

options.title: services.libinput.mouse.scrollButton
options.description:
Designates a button as scroll button. If the ScrollMethod is button and the button is logically
held down, x/y axis movement is converted into scroll events.

options.title: services.libinput.mouse.scrollMethod
options.description:
Specify the scrolling method: `twofinger`, `edge`,
`button`, or `none`

options.title: services.libinput.mouse.sendEventsMode
options.description:

or `disabled-on-external-mouse`

options.title: services.libinput.mouse.tapping
options.description: Enables or disables tap-to-click behavior.

options.title: services.libinput.mouse.tappingButtonMap
options.description: Set the button mapping for 1/2/3-finger taps to left/right/middle or left/middle/right, respectively.

options.title: services.libinput.mouse.tappingDragLock
options.description:

and-drag will not immediately release the button. If the finger is set down again within the
timeout, the dragging process continues.

options.title: services.libinput.mouse.transformationMatrix
options.description:

options.title: services.librenms.distributedPoller.distributedBilling
options.description:
Enable distributed billing on this poller.

Note: according to [the docs](https://docs.librenms.org/Extensions/Distributed-Poller/#discovery),
billing should only be calculated on a single node per poller group. You can disable billing on
some nodes with the `services.librenms.enableLocalBilling` option.

options.title: services.librenms.distributedPoller.enable
options.description:
Configure this LibreNMS instance as a [distributed poller](https://docs.librenms.org/Extensions/Distributed-Poller/).
This will disable all web features and just configure the poller features.
Use the `mysql` database of your main LibreNMS instance in the database settings.

options.title: services.librenms.distributedPoller.group
options.description: Group(s) of this poller.

options.title: services.librenms.distributedPoller.memcachedHost
options.description: Hostname or IP of the `memcached` server.

options.title: services.librenms.distributedPoller.memcachedPort
options.type: 16 bit unsigned integer; between 0 and 65535 (both inclusive)
options.description: Port of the `memcached` server.

options.title: services.librenms.distributedPoller.name
options.description: Custom name of this poller.

options.title: services.librenms.distributedPoller.rrdcachedHost
options.description: Hostname or IP of the `rrdcached` server.

options.title: services.librenms.distributedPoller.rrdcachedPort
options.type: 16 bit unsigned integer; between 0 and 65535 (both inclusive)
options.description: Port of the `memcached` server.

options.title: services.librenms.enable
options.description: Whether to enable LibreNMS network monitoring system.

options.title: services.librenms.enableLocalBilling
options.description:
Enable billing Cron-Jobs on the local instance. Enabled by default, but you may disable it
on some nodes within a distributed poller setup. See [the docs](https://docs.librenms.org/Extensions/Distributed-Poller/#discovery)
for more informations about billing with distributed pollers.

options.title: services.librenms.enableOneMinutePolling
options.description:
Enables the [1-Minute Polling](https://docs.librenms.org/Support/1-Minute-Polling/).
Changing this option will automatically convert your existing rrd files.

options.title: services.librenms.environmentFile
options.description:
File containing env-vars to be substituted into the final config. Useful for secrets.
Does not apply to settings defined in `extraConfig`.

options.title: services.librenms.extraConfig
options.description:
Additional config for LibreNMS that will be appended to the `config.php`. See
<https://github.com/librenms/librenms/blob/master/misc/config_definitions.json>
for possible options. Useful if you want to use PHP-Functions in your config.

options.title: services.librenms.finalPackage
options.description: The final package used by the module. This is the package that has all overrides.

options.title: services.librenms.group
options.description: Name of the LibreNMS group.

options.title: services.librenms.hostname
options.description: The hostname to serve LibreNMS on.

options.title: services.librenms.logDir
options.description: Path of the LibreNMS logging directory.

options.title: services.librenms.nginx
options.description: With this option, you can customize the nginx virtualHost settings.

options.title: services.librenms.nginx.acmeFallbackHost
options.description:
Host which to proxy requests to if ACME challenge is not found. Useful
if you want multiple hosts to be able to verify the same domain name.

With this option, you could request certificates for the present domain
with an ACME client that is running on another host, which you would
specify here.

options.title: services.librenms.nginx.acmeRoot
options.description:
Directory for the ACME challenge, which is **public**. Don't put certs or keys in here.
Set to null to inherit from config.security.acme.

options.title: services.librenms.nginx.addSSL
options.description:
Whether to enable HTTPS in addition to plain HTTP. This will set defaults for
`listen` to listen on all interfaces on the respective default
ports (80, 443).

options.title: services.librenms.nginx.basicAuth
options.description:
Basic Auth protection for a vhost.

WARNING: This is implemented to store the password in plain text in the
Nix store.

options.title: services.librenms.nginx.basicAuthFile
options.description:
Basic Auth password file for a vhost.
Can be created by running {command}`nix-shell --packages apacheHttpd --run 'htpasswd -B -c FILENAME USERNAME'`.

options.title: services.librenms.nginx.default
options.description: Makes this vhost the default.

options.title: services.librenms.nginx.enableACME
options.description:
Whether to ask Let's Encrypt to sign a certificate for this vhost.
Alternately, you can use an existing certificate through {option}`useACMEHost`.

options.title: services.librenms.nginx.extraConfig
options.description: These lines go to the end of the vhost verbatim.

options.title: services.librenms.nginx.forceSSL
options.description:
Whether to add a separate nginx server block that redirects (defaults
to 301, configurable with `redirectCode`) all plain HTTP traffic to
HTTPS. This will set defaults for `listen` to listen on all interfaces
on the respective default ports (80, 443), where the non-SSL listens
are used for the redirect vhosts.

options.title: services.librenms.nginx.globalRedirect
options.description:
If set, all requests for this host are redirected (defaults to 301,
configurable with `redirectCode`) to the given hostname.

options.title: services.librenms.nginx.http2
options.description:
Whether to enable the HTTP/2 protocol.
Note that (as of writing) due to nginx's implementation, to disable
HTTP/2 you have to disable it on all vhosts that use a given
IP address / port.
If there is one server block configured to enable http2, then it is
enabled for all server blocks on this IP.
See <https://stackoverflow.com/a/39466948/263061>.

options.title: services.librenms.nginx.http3
options.description:
Whether to enable the HTTP/3 protocol.
This requires activating the QUIC transport protocol
`services.nginx.virtualHosts.<name>.quic = true;`.
Note that HTTP/3 support is experimental and *not* yet recommended for production.
Read more at <https://quic.nginx.org/>
HTTP/3 availability must be manually advertised, preferably in each location block.

options.title: services.librenms.nginx.http3_hq
options.description:
Whether to enable the HTTP/0.9 protocol negotiation used in QUIC interoperability tests.
This requires activating the QUIC transport protocol
`services.nginx.virtualHosts.<name>.quic = true;`.
Note that special application protocol support is experimental and *not* yet recommended for production.
Read more at <https://quic.nginx.org/>

options.title: services.librenms.nginx.kTLS
options.description:
Whether to enable kTLS support.
Implementing TLS in the kernel (kTLS) improves performance by significantly
reducing the need for copying operations between user space and the kernel.
Required Nginx version 1.21.4 or later.

options.title: services.librenms.nginx.listen
options.description:
Listen addresses and ports for this virtual host.
IPv6 addresses must be enclosed in square brackets.
Note: this option overrides `addSSL`
and `onlySSL`.

If you only want to set the addresses manually and not
the ports, take a look at `listenAddresses`.

options.title: services.librenms.nginx.listen.*.addr
options.description: Listen address.

options.title: services.librenms.nginx.listen.*.extraParameters
options.description: Extra parameters of this listen directive.

options.title: services.librenms.nginx.listen.*.port
options.type: null or 16 bit unsigned integer; between 0 and 65535 (both inclusive)
options.description:
Port number to listen on.
If unset and the listen address is not a socket then nginx defaults to 80.

options.title: services.librenms.nginx.listen.*.proxyProtocol
options.description: Enable PROXY protocol.

options.title: services.librenms.nginx.listen.*.ssl
options.description: Enable SSL.

options.title: services.librenms.nginx.listenAddresses
options.description:
Listen addresses for this virtual host.
Compared to `listen` this only sets the addresses
and the ports are chosen automatically.

Note: This option overrides `enableIPv6`

options.description: Declarative location config

Nix store.

options.title: services.librenms.nginx.locations.<name>.fastcgiParams
options.type: attribute set of (string or absolute path)

options.title: services.litestream.environmentFile
options.description:
Environment file as defined in {manpage}`systemd.exec(5)`.

Secrets may be passed to the service without adding them to the
world-readable Nix store, by specifying placeholder variables as
the option value in Nix and setting these variables accordingly in the
environment file.

By default, Litestream will perform environment variable expansion
within the config file before reading it. Any references to $VAR or
${VAR} formatted variables will be replaced with their environment
variable values. If no value is set then it will be replaced with an
empty string.

```
  # Content of the environment file
  LITESTREAM_ACCESS_KEY_ID=AKIAxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx
  LITESTREAM_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx/xxxxxxxxx
```

Note that this file needs to be available on the host on which
this exporter is running.

options.type: attribute set of (null or boolean or signed integer or string)

Environment variables to set.

Livebook is configured through the use of environment variables. The
available configuration options can be found in the [Livebook
documentation](https://hexdocs.pm/livebook/readme.html#environment-variables).

Note that all environment variables set through this configuration
parameter will be readable by anyone with access to the host
machine. Therefore, sensitive information like {env}`LIVEBOOK_PASSWORD`
or {env}`LIVEBOOK_COOKIE` should never be set using this configuration
option, but should instead use
[](#opt-services.livebook.environmentFile). See the documentation for
that option for more information.

Any environment variables specified in the
[](#opt-services.livebook.environmentFile) will supersede environment
variables specified in this option.

options.title: services.livebook.environmentFile
options.description:

Secrets like {env}`LIVEBOOK_PASSWORD` (which is used to specify the
password needed to access the livebook site) or {env}`LIVEBOOK_COOKIE`
(which is used to specify the
[cookie](https://www.erlang.org/doc/reference_manual/distributed.html#security)
used to connect to the running Elixir system) may be passed to the
service without making them readable to everyone with access to
systemctl by using this configuration parameter.

Note that this file needs to be available on the host on which
`livebook` is running.

For security purposes, this file should contain at least
{env}`LIVEBOOK_PASSWORD` or {env}`LIVEBOOK_TOKEN_ENABLED=false`.

See the [Livebook
documentation](https://hexdocs.pm/livebook/readme.html#environment-variables)
and the [](#opt-services.livebook.environment) configuration parameter
for further options.

for example, the test does not know about existing files and system users are
not known.
These limitations mean we must adjust the file for tests (missingok is forced
and users are replaced by dummy users), so tests are complemented by a

{option}`systemd.services.logrotate-checkconf.enable` option.

(e.g. a file path where we don't have access to intermediate directories):

options.title: services.mail.sendmailSetuidWrapper.capabilities
options.description:
A comma-separated list of capability clauses to be given to the
wrapper program. The format for capability clauses is described in the
“TEXTUAL REPRESENTATION” section of the {manpage}`cap_from_text(3)`
manual page. For a list of capabilities supported by the system, check
the {manpage}`capabilities(7)` manual page.

::: {.note}
`cap_setpcap`, which is required for the wrapper
program to be able to raise caps into the Ambient set is NOT raised
to the Ambient set so that the real program cannot modify its own
capabilities!! This may be too restrictive for cases in which the
real program needs cap_setpcap but it at least leans on the side
security paranoid vs. too relaxed.
:::
