options.title: systemd.user.timers.<name>.enable
options.description:
If set to false, this unit will be a symlink to
/dev/null. This is primarily useful to prevent specific
template instances
(e.g. `serial-getty@ttyS0`) from being
started. Note that `enable=true` does not
make a unit start by default at boot; if you want that, see
`wantedBy`.

options.title: systemd.user.timers.<name>.name
options.description:
The name of this systemd unit, including its extension.
This can be used to refer to this unit from other systemd units.

options.title: systemd.user.timers.<name>.onFailure
options.type: list of string matching the pattern [a-zA-Z0-9@%:_.\-]+[.](service|socket|device|mount|automount|swap|target|path|timer|scope|slice)
options.description:
A list of one or more units that are activated when
this unit enters the "failed" state.

options.title: systemd.user.timers.<name>.onSuccess
options.type: list of string matching the pattern [a-zA-Z0-9@%:_.\-]+[.](service|socket|device|mount|automount|swap|target|path|timer|scope|slice)
options.description:
A list of one or more units that are activated when
this unit enters the "inactive" state.

options.title: systemd.user.timers.<name>.overrideStrategy
options.description:
Defines how unit configuration is provided for systemd:

`asDropinIfExists` creates a unit file when no unit file is provided by the package
otherwise it creates a drop-in file named `overrides.conf`.

`asDropin` creates a drop-in file named `overrides.conf`.
Mainly needed to define instances for systemd template units (e.g. `systemd-nspawn@mycontainer.service`).

See also {manpage}`systemd.unit(5)`.

options.title: systemd.user.timers.<name>.partOf
options.type: list of string matching the pattern [a-zA-Z0-9@%:_.\-]+[.](service|socket|device|mount|automount|swap|target|path|timer|scope|slice)
options.description:
If the specified units are stopped or restarted, then this
unit is stopped or restarted as well.

options.title: systemd.user.timers.<name>.reloadTriggers
options.description:
An arbitrary list of items such as derivations.  If any item
in the list changes between reconfigurations, the service will
be reloaded.  If anything but a reload trigger changes in the
unit file, the unit will be restarted instead.

options.title: systemd.user.timers.<name>.requiredBy
options.type: list of string matching the pattern [a-zA-Z0-9@%:_.\-]+[.](service|socket|device|mount|automount|swap|target|path|timer|scope|slice)
options.description:
Units that require (i.e. depend on and need to go down with) this unit.
As discussed in the `wantedBy` option description this also creates
`.requires` symlinks automatically.

options.title: systemd.user.timers.<name>.requires
options.type: list of string matching the pattern [a-zA-Z0-9@%:_.\-]+[.](service|socket|device|mount|automount|swap|target|path|timer|scope|slice)
options.description:
Start the specified units when this unit is started, and stop
this unit when the specified units are stopped or fail.

options.title: systemd.user.timers.<name>.requisite
options.type: list of string matching the pattern [a-zA-Z0-9@%:_.\-]+[.](service|socket|device|mount|automount|swap|target|path|timer|scope|slice)
options.description:
Similar to requires. However if the units listed are not started,
they will not be started and the transaction will fail.

options.title: systemd.user.timers.<name>.restartTriggers
options.description:
An arbitrary list of items such as derivations.  If any item
in the list changes between reconfigurations, the service will
be restarted.

options.title: systemd.user.timers.<name>.startLimitBurst
options.description:
Configure unit start rate limiting. Units which are started
more than startLimitBurst times within an interval time
interval are not permitted to start any more.

options.title: systemd.user.timers.<name>.startLimitIntervalSec
options.description:
Configure unit start rate limiting. Units which are started
more than startLimitBurst times within an interval time
interval are not permitted to start any more.

options.title: systemd.user.timers.<name>.timerConfig
options.description:
Each attribute in this set specifies an option in the
`[Timer]` section of the unit.  See
{manpage}`systemd.timer(5)` and
{manpage}`systemd.time(7)` for details.

options.title: systemd.user.timers.<name>.unitConfig
options.description:
Each attribute in this set specifies an option in the
`[Unit]` section of the unit.  See
{manpage}`systemd.unit(5)` for details.

options.title: systemd.user.timers.<name>.upheldBy
options.type: list of string matching the pattern [a-zA-Z0-9@%:_.\-]+[.](service|socket|device|mount|automount|swap|target|path|timer|scope|slice)
options.description:
Keep this unit running as long as the listed units are running. This is a continuously
enforced version of wantedBy.

options.title: systemd.user.timers.<name>.upholds
options.type: list of string matching the pattern [a-zA-Z0-9@%:_.\-]+[.](service|socket|device|mount|automount|swap|target|path|timer|scope|slice)
options.description: Keeps the specified running while this unit is running. A continuous version of `wants`.

options.title: systemd.user.timers.<name>.wantedBy
options.type: list of string matching the pattern [a-zA-Z0-9@%:_.\-]+[.](service|socket|device|mount|automount|swap|target|path|timer|scope|slice)
options.description:
Units that want (i.e. depend on) this unit. The default method for
starting a unit by default at boot time is to set this option to
`["multi-user.target"]` for system services. Likewise for user units
(`systemd.user.<name>.*`) set it to `["default.target"]` to make a unit
start by default when the user `<name>` logs on.

This option creates a `.wants` symlink in the given target that exists
statelessly without the need for running `systemctl enable`.
The `[Install]` section described in {manpage}`systemd.unit(5)` however is
not supported because it is a stateful process that does not fit well
into the NixOS design.

options.title: systemd.user.timers.<name>.wants
options.type: list of string matching the pattern [a-zA-Z0-9@%:_.\-]+[.](service|socket|device|mount|automount|swap|target|path|timer|scope|slice)
options.description: Start the specified units when this unit is started.

options.title: time.hardwareClockInLocalTime

options.title: users.allowNoPasswordLogin
options.description:

options.title: users.enforceIdUniqueness

options.description:

options.title: users.extraUsers
options.description: Alias of {option}`users.users`.

options.description:
Automatically allocate subordinate user and group ids for this user.

options.title: users.extraUsers.<name>.createHome
options.description:
Whether to create the home directory and ensure ownership as well as

options.title: users.extraUsers.<name>.cryptHomeLuks
options.description:
Path to encrypted luks device that contains

options.type: string, not containing newlines or colons
options.description:

options.title: users.extraUsers.<name>.enable
options.description:
If set to false, the user account will not be created. This is useful for when you wish to conditionally

options.title: users.extraUsers.<name>.expires
options.type: null or string matching the pattern [[:digit:]]{4}-[[:digit:]]{2}-[[:digit:]]{2}

options.title: users.extraUsers.<name>.hashedPassword
options.type: null or (string, not containing newlines or colons)
options.description:
Specifies the hashed password for the user.

The {option}`initialHashedPassword`, {option}`hashedPassword`,
{option}`initialPassword`, {option}`password` and
{option}`hashedPasswordFile` options all control what password is set for
the user.

In a system where [](#opt-systemd.sysusers.enable) is `false`, typically
only one of {option}`hashedPassword`, {option}`password`, or
{option}`hashedPasswordFile` will be set.

In a system where [](#opt-systemd.sysusers.enable) or [](#opt-services.userborn.enable) is `true`,
typically only one of {option}`initialPassword`, {option}`initialHashedPassword`,
or {option}`hashedPasswordFile` will be set.

If the option {option}`users.mutableUsers` is true, the password defined
in one of the above password options will only be set when the user is
created for the first time. After that, you are free to change the
password with the ordinary user management commands. If
{option}`users.mutableUsers` is false, you cannot change user passwords,
they will always be set according to the password options.

If none of the password options are set, then no password is assigned to
the user, and the user will not be able to do password-based logins.

If multiple of these password options are set at the same time then a
specific order of precedence is followed, which can lead to surprising
results. The order of precedence differs depending on whether the
{option}`users.mutableUsers` option is set.


If the option {option}`users.mutableUsers` is
`false`, then the order of precedence is as shown
below, where values on the left are overridden by values on the right:
{option}`initialHashedPassword` -> {option}`hashedPassword` -> {option}`initialPassword` -> {option}`password` -> {option}`hashedPasswordFile`


If the option {option}`users.mutableUsers` is
`true`, then the order of precedence is as shown
below, where values on the left are overridden by values on the right:
{option}`initialHashedPassword` -> {option}`initialPassword` -> {option}`hashedPassword` -> {option}`password` -> {option}`hashedPasswordFile`



To generate a hashed password run `mkpasswd`.

If set to an empty string (`""`), this user will be able to log in without
being asked for a password (but not via remote services such as SSH, or
indirectly via {command}`su` or {command}`sudo`). This should only be used
for e.g. bootable live systems. Note: this is different from setting an
empty password, which can be achieved using
{option}`users.users.<name?>.password`.

If set to `null` (default) this user will not be able to log in using a
password (i.e. via {command}`login` command).

options.title: users.extraUsers.<name>.hashedPasswordFile

password. The password file is read on each system activation. The
file should contain exactly one line, which should be the password in

The {option}`initialHashedPassword`, {option}`hashedPassword`,
{option}`initialPassword`, {option}`password` and
{option}`hashedPasswordFile` options all control what password is set for
the user.

In a system where [](#opt-systemd.sysusers.enable) is `false`, typically

{option}`hashedPasswordFile` will be set.

typically only one of {option}`initialPassword`, {option}`initialHashedPassword`,
or {option}`hashedPasswordFile` will be set.

in one of the above password options will only be set when the user is
created for the first time. After that, you are free to change the

If none of the password options are set, then no password is assigned to

If multiple of these password options are set at the same time then a
specific order of precedence is followed, which can lead to surprising
results. The order of precedence differs depending on whether the
{option}`users.mutableUsers` option is set.


If the option {option}`users.mutableUsers` is
`false`, then the order of precedence is as shown
below, where values on the left are overridden by values on the right:
{option}`initialHashedPassword` -> {option}`hashedPassword` -> {option}`initialPassword` -> {option}`password` -> {option}`hashedPasswordFile`


If the option {option}`users.mutableUsers` is

options.title: users.extraUsers.<name>.isNormalUser
options.description:
Indicates whether this is an account for a “real” user.
This automatically sets {option}`group` to `users`,
{option}`createHome` to `true`,
{option}`home` to {file}`/home/«username»`,
{option}`useDefaultShell` to `true`,
and {option}`isSystemUser` to `false`.
Exactly one of `isNormalUser` and `isSystemUser` must be true.

options.title: users.extraUsers.<name>.isSystemUser
options.description:
Indicates if the user is a system user or not. This option
only has an effect if {option}`uid` is
{option}`null`, in which case it determines whether
the user's UID is allocated in the range for system users
(below 1000) or in the range for normal users (starting at
1000).
Exactly one of `isNormalUser` and
`isSystemUser` must be true.

options.title: users.extraUsers.<name>.linger
options.description:
Whether to enable or disable lingering for this user.  Without
lingering, user units will not be started until the user logs in,
and may be stopped on logout depending on the settings in
`logind.conf`.

By default, NixOS will not manage lingering, new users will default
to not lingering, and lingering can be configured imperatively using
`loginctl enable-linger` or `loginctl disable-linger`. Setting
this option to `true` or `false` is the declarative equivalent of
running `loginctl enable-linger` or `loginctl disable-linger`
respectively.

options.title: users.extraUsers.<name>.name
options.type: string, not containing newlines or colons
options.description:
The name of the user account. If undefined, the name of the
attribute set will be used.

options.title: users.extraUsers.<name>.openssh.authorizedKeys.keyFiles
options.description:
A list of files each containing one OpenSSH public key that should be
added to the user's authorized keys. The contents of the files are
read at build time and added to a file that the SSH daemon reads in
addition to the the user's authorized_keys file. You can combine the
`keyFiles` and `keys` options.

options.title: users.extraUsers.<name>.openssh.authorizedKeys.keys
options.description:
A list of verbatim OpenSSH public keys that should be added to the
user's authorized keys. The keys are added to a file that the SSH
daemon reads in addition to the the user's authorized_keys file.
You can combine the `keys` and
`keyFiles` options.
Warning: If you are using `NixOps` then don't use this
option since it will replace the key required for deployment via ssh.

options.title: users.extraUsers.<name>.openssh.authorizedPrincipals
options.description:
A list of verbatim principal names that should be added to the user's
authorized principals.

options.title: users.extraUsers.<name>.packages
options.description:
The set of packages that should be made available to the user.
This is in contrast to {option}`environment.systemPackages`,
which adds packages to all users.

options.title: users.extraUsers.<name>.pamMount
options.description:
Attributes for user's entry in
{file}`pam_mount.conf.xml`.
Useful attributes might include `path`,
`options`, `fstype`, and `server`.
See <https://pam-mount.sourceforge.net/pam_mount.conf.5.html>
for more information.

options.title: users.extraUsers.<name>.password
options.description:
Specifies the (clear text) password for the user.
Warning: do not set confidential information here
because it is world-readable in the Nix store. This option
should only be used for public accounts.

The {option}`initialHashedPassword`, {option}`hashedPassword`,
{option}`initialPassword`, {option}`password` and
{option}`hashedPasswordFile` options all control what password is set for
the user.

In a system where [](#opt-systemd.sysusers.enable) is `false`, typically
only one of {option}`hashedPassword`, {option}`password`, or
{option}`hashedPasswordFile` will be set.

In a system where [](#opt-systemd.sysusers.enable) or [](#opt-services.userborn.enable) is `true`,
typically only one of {option}`initialPassword`, {option}`initialHashedPassword`,
or {option}`hashedPasswordFile` will be set.

If the option {option}`users.mutableUsers` is true, the password defined
in one of the above password options will only be set when the user is
created for the first time. After that, you are free to change the
password with the ordinary user management commands. If
{option}`users.mutableUsers` is false, you cannot change user passwords,
they will always be set according to the password options.

If none of the password options are set, then no password is assigned to
the user, and the user will not be able to do password-based logins.

If multiple of these password options are set at the same time then a
specific order of precedence is followed, which can lead to surprising
results. The order of precedence differs depending on whether the
{option}`users.mutableUsers` option is set.


If the option {option}`users.mutableUsers` is
`false`, then the order of precedence is as shown
below, where values on the left are overridden by values on the right:
{option}`initialHashedPassword` -> {option}`hashedPassword` -> {option}`initialPassword` -> {option}`password` -> {option}`hashedPasswordFile`


If the option {option}`users.mutableUsers` is
`true`, then the order of precedence is as shown
below, where values on the left are overridden by values on the right:
{option}`initialHashedPassword` -> {option}`initialPassword` -> {option}`hashedPassword` -> {option}`password` -> {option}`hashedPasswordFile`

options.title: users.extraUsers.<name>.shell
options.type: null or package or (absolute path, not containing newlines or colons)
options.description:
The path to the user's shell. Can use shell derivations,
like `pkgs.bashInteractive`. Don’t
forget to enable your shell in
`programs` if necessary,
like `programs.zsh.enable = true;`.

options.title: users.extraUsers.<name>.subGidRanges
options.description:
Subordinate group ids that user is allowed to use.
They are set into {file}`/etc/subgid` and are used
by `newgidmap` for user namespaces.

options.title: users.extraUsers.<name>.subGidRanges.*.count
options.description: Count of subordinate group ids

options.title: users.extraUsers.<name>.subGidRanges.*.startGid
options.description:
Start of the range of subordinate group ids that user is
allowed to use.

options.title: users.extraUsers.<name>.subUidRanges
options.description:
Subordinate user ids that user is allowed to use.
They are set into {file}`/etc/subuid` and are used
by `newuidmap` for user namespaces.

options.title: users.extraUsers.<name>.subUidRanges.*.count
options.description: Count of subordinate user ids

options.title: users.extraUsers.<name>.subUidRanges.*.startUid
options.description:
Start of the range of subordinate user ids that user is
allowed to use.

options.title: users.extraUsers.<name>.uid
options.description:
The account UID. If the UID is null, a free UID is picked on
activation.

options.title: users.extraUsers.<name>.useDefaultShell
options.description:
If true, the user's shell will be set to
{option}`users.defaultUserShell`.

options.title: users.groups
options.description: Additional groups to be created automatically by the system.

options.title: users.groups.<name>.gid
options.description:
The group GID. If the GID is null, a free GID is picked on
activation.

options.title: users.groups.<name>.members
options.type: list of (string, not containing newlines or colons)
options.description:
The user names of the group members, added to the
`/etc/group` file.

options.title: users.groups.<name>.name
options.type: string, not containing newlines or colons
options.description:
The name of the group. If undefined, the name of the attribute set
will be used.

options.title: users.ldap.base
options.description: The distinguished name of the search base.

options.title: users.ldap.bind.distinguishedName
options.description:
The distinguished name to bind to the LDAP server with. If this
is not specified, an anonymous bind will be done.

options.title: users.ldap.bind.passwordFile
options.description:
The path to a file containing the credentials to use when binding
to the LDAP server (if not binding anonymously).

options.title: users.ldap.bind.policy
options.description:
Specifies the policy to use for reconnecting to an unavailable
LDAP server. The default is `hard_open`, which
reconnects if opening the connection to the directory server
failed. By contrast, `hard_init` reconnects if
initializing the connection failed. Initializing may not
actually contact the directory server, and it is possible that
a malformed configuration file will trigger reconnection. If
`soft` is specified, then
`nss_ldap` will return immediately on server
failure. All hard reconnect policies block with exponential
backoff before retrying.

options.title: users.ldap.bind.timeLimit
options.description:
Specifies the time limit (in seconds) to use when connecting
to the directory server. This is distinct from the time limit
specified in {option}`users.ldap.timeLimit` and affects
the initial server connection only.

options.title: users.ldap.daemon.enable
options.description:
Whether to let the nslcd daemon (nss-pam-ldapd) handle the
LDAP lookups for NSS and PAM. This can improve performance,
and if you need to bind to the LDAP server with a password,
it increases security, since only the nslcd user needs to
have access to the bindpw file, not everyone that uses NSS
and/or PAM. If this option is enabled, a local nscd user is
created automatically, and the nslcd service is started
automatically when the network get up.

options.title: users.ldap.daemon.extraConfig
options.description:
Extra configuration options that will be added verbatim at
the end of the nslcd configuration file ({manpage}`nslcd.conf(5)`).

options.title: users.ldap.daemon.rootpwmoddn
options.description:
The distinguished name to use to bind to the LDAP server
when the root user tries to modify a user's password.

options.title: users.ldap.daemon.rootpwmodpwFile
options.description:
The path to a file containing the credentials with which to bind to
the LDAP server if the root user tries to change a user's password.

options.title: users.ldap.enable
options.description: Whether to enable authentication against an LDAP server.

options.title: users.ldap.extraConfig
options.description:
Extra configuration options that will be added verbatim at
the end of the ldap configuration file ({manpage}`ldap.conf(5)`).
If {option}`users.ldap.daemon` is enabled, this
configuration will not be used. In that case, use
{option}`users.ldap.daemon.extraConfig` instead.

options.title: users.ldap.loginPam
options.description: Whether to include authentication against LDAP in login PAM.

options.title: users.ldap.nsswitch
options.description: Whether to include lookup against LDAP in NSS.

options.title: users.ldap.server
options.description: The URL of the LDAP server.

options.title: users.ldap.timeLimit
options.description:
Specifies the time limit (in seconds) to use when performing
searches. A value of zero (0), which is the default, is to
wait indefinitely for searches to be completed.

options.title: users.ldap.useTLS
options.description:
If enabled, use TLS (encryption) over an LDAP (port 389)
connection.  The alternative is to specify an LDAPS server (port
636) in {option}`users.ldap.server` or to forego
security.

options.title: users.manageLingering
options.description: Whether to manage whether users linger or not.

options.title: users.motd
options.description: Message of the day shown to users when they log in.
options.example: "Today is Sweetmorn, the 4th day of The Aftermath in the YOLD 3178."

options.title: users.motdFile
options.description: A file containing the message of the day shown to users when they log in.

options.title: users.mutableUsers
options.description:
If set to `true`, you are free to add new users and groups to the system
with the ordinary `useradd` and
`groupadd` commands. On system activation, the
existing contents of the `/etc/passwd` and
`/etc/group` files will be merged with the
contents generated from the `users.users` and
`users.groups` options.
The initial password for a user will be set
according to `users.users`, but existing passwords
will not be changed.

::: {.warning}
If set to `false`, the contents of the user and
group files will simply be replaced on system activation. This also
holds for the user passwords; all changed
passwords will be reset according to the
`users.users` configuration on activation.
:::

options.title: users.mysql.pam
options.description: Settings for `pam_mysql`

options.title: users.mysql.pam.cryptDefault
options.description: The default encryption method to use for `passwordCrypt = 1`.

options.title: users.mysql.pam.disconnectEveryOperation
options.description:
By default, `pam_mysql` keeps the connection to the MySQL
database until the session is closed. If this option is set to true it
disconnects every time the PAM operation has finished. This option may
be useful in case the session lasts quite long.

options.title: users.mysql.pam.logging.enable
options.description: Enables logging of authentication attempts in the MySQL database.

options.title: users.mysql.pam.logging.hostColumn
options.description:
The name of the column in the log table to which the name of the user
being authenticated is stored.

options.title: users.mysql.pam.logging.msgColumn
options.description:
The name of the column in the log table to which the description
of the performed operation is stored.

options.title: users.mysql.pam.logging.pidColumn
options.description:
The name of the column in the log table to which the pid of the
process utilising the `pam_mysql` authentication
service is stored.

options.title: users.mysql.pam.logging.rHostColumn
options.description:
The name of the column in the log table to which the name of the remote
host that initiates the session is stored. The value is supposed to be
set by the PAM-aware application with `pam_set_item(PAM_RHOST)`.

options.title: users.mysql.pam.logging.table
options.description: The name of the table to which logs are written.

options.title: users.mysql.pam.logging.timeColumn
options.description:
The name of the column in the log table to which the timestamp of the
log entry is stored.

options.title: users.mysql.pam.logging.userColumn
options.description:
The name of the column in the log table to which the name of the
user being authenticated is stored.

options.title: users.mysql.pam.passwordColumn
options.description: The name of the column that contains a (encrypted) password string.

options.title: users.mysql.pam.passwordCrypt
options.description:
The method to encrypt the user's password:

- `0` (or `"plain"`):
  No encryption. Passwords are stored in plaintext. HIGHLY DISCOURAGED.
- `1` (or `"Y"`):
  Use {manpage}`crypt(3)` function.
- `2` (or `"mysql"`):
  Use the MySQL PASSWORD() function. It is possible that the encryption function used
  by `pam_mysql` is different from that of the MySQL server, as
  `pam_mysql` uses the function defined in MySQL's C-client API
  instead of using PASSWORD() SQL function in the query.
- `3` (or `"md5"`):
  Use plain hex MD5.
- `4` (or `"sha1"`):
  Use plain hex SHA1.
- `5` (or `"drupal7"`):
  Use Drupal7 salted passwords.
- `6` (or `"joomla15"`):
  Use Joomla15 salted passwords.
- `7` (or `"ssha"`):
  Use ssha hashed passwords.
- `8` (or `"sha512"`):
  Use sha512 hashed passwords.
- `9` (or `"sha256"`):
  Use sha256 hashed passwords.

options.title: users.mysql.pam.statusColumn
options.description:
The name of the column or an SQL expression that indicates the status of
the user. The status is expressed by the combination of two bitfields
shown below:

- `bit 0 (0x01)`:
   if flagged, `pam_mysql` deems the account to be expired and
   returns `PAM_ACCT_EXPIRED`. That is, the account is supposed
   to no longer be available. Note this doesn't mean that `pam_mysql`
   rejects further authentication operations.
-  `bit 1 (0x02)`:
   if flagged, `pam_mysql` deems the authentication token
   (password) to be expired and returns `PAM_NEW_AUTHTOK_REQD`.
   This ends up requiring that the user enter a new password.

options.title: users.mysql.pam.table
options.description: The name of table that maps unique login names to the passwords.

options.title: users.mysql.pam.updateTable
options.description:
The name of the table used for password alteration. If not defined, the value
of the `table` option will be used instead.

options.title: users.mysql.pam.userColumn
options.description: The name of the column that contains a unix login name.

options.title: users.mysql.pam.verbose
options.description:
If enabled, produces logs with detailed messages that describes what
`pam_mysql` is doing. May be useful for debugging.

options.title: users.mysql.pam.where
options.description: Additional criteria for the query.

options.title: users.mysql.passwordFile
options.description: The path to the file containing the password for the user

options.title: users.mysql.user
options.description: The username to use when connecting to the database

options.title: users.users
options.description:
Additional user accounts to be created automatically by the system.
This can also be used to set options for root.

options.title: users.users.<name>.autoSubUidGidRange
options.description:
Automatically allocate subordinate user and group ids for this user.
Allocated range is currently always of size 65536.

options.title: users.users.<name>.createHome
options.description:
Whether to create the home directory and ensure ownership as well as

options.title: users.users.<name>.cryptHomeLuks
options.description:
Path to encrypted luks device that contains

options.title: users.users.<name>.description
options.type: string, not containing newlines or colons
options.description:
A short description of the user account, typically the
user's full name.  This is actually the “GECOS” or “comment”
field in {file}`/etc/passwd`.

options.title: users.users.<name>.enable
options.description:
If set to false, the user account will not be created. This is useful for when you wish to conditionally
disable user accounts.

options.title: users.users.<name>.expires
options.type: null or string matching the pattern [[:digit:]]{4}-[[:digit:]]{2}-[[:digit:]]{2}
options.description:
Set the date on which the user's account will no longer be
accessible. The date is expressed in the format YYYY-MM-DD, or null

A user whose account is locked must contact the system
administrator before being able to use the system again.

options.title: users.users.<name>.extraGroups

options.title: users.users.<name>.group
options.description: The user's primary group.

options.title: users.users.<name>.hashedPassword
options.type: null or (string, not containing newlines or colons)
options.description:
Specifies the hashed password for the user.

The {option}`initialHashedPassword`, {option}`hashedPassword`,
{option}`initialPassword`, {option}`password` and
{option}`hashedPasswordFile` options all control what password is set for
the user.

In a system where [](#opt-systemd.sysusers.enable) is `false`, typically
only one of {option}`hashedPassword`, {option}`password`, or
{option}`hashedPasswordFile` will be set.

In a system where [](#opt-systemd.sysusers.enable) or [](#opt-services.userborn.enable) is `true`,
typically only one of {option}`initialPassword`, {option}`initialHashedPassword`,
or {option}`hashedPasswordFile` will be set.

If the option {option}`users.mutableUsers` is true, the password defined
in one of the above password options will only be set when the user is
created for the first time. After that, you are free to change the
password with the ordinary user management commands. If
{option}`users.mutableUsers` is false, you cannot change user passwords,
they will always be set according to the password options.

If none of the password options are set, then no password is assigned to
the user, and the user will not be able to do password-based logins.

If multiple of these password options are set at the same time then a
specific order of precedence is followed, which can lead to surprising
results. The order of precedence differs depending on whether the
{option}`users.mutableUsers` option is set.


If the option {option}`users.mutableUsers` is
`false`, then the order of precedence is as shown
below, where values on the left are overridden by values on the right:
{option}`initialHashedPassword` -> {option}`hashedPassword` -> {option}`initialPassword` -> {option}`password` -> {option}`hashedPasswordFile`


If the option {option}`users.mutableUsers` is
`true`, then the order of precedence is as shown
below, where values on the left are overridden by values on the right:
{option}`initialHashedPassword` -> {option}`initialPassword` -> {option}`hashedPassword` -> {option}`password` -> {option}`hashedPasswordFile`



To generate a hashed password run `mkpasswd`.

If set to an empty string (`""`), this user will be able to log in without
being asked for a password (but not via remote services such as SSH, or
indirectly via {command}`su` or {command}`sudo`). This should only be used
for e.g. bootable live systems. Note: this is different from setting an
empty password, which can be achieved using
{option}`users.users.<name?>.password`.

If set to `null` (default) this user will not be able to log in using a
password (i.e. via {command}`login` command).

created for the first time. After that, you are free to change the

If none of the password options are set, then no password is assigned to

If multiple of these password options are set at the same time then a
specific order of precedence is followed, which can lead to surprising
results. The order of precedence differs depending on whether the
{option}`users.mutableUsers` option is set.


If the option {option}`users.mutableUsers` is
`false`, then the order of precedence is as shown
below, where values on the left are overridden by values on the right:
{option}`initialHashedPassword` -> {option}`hashedPassword` -> {option}`initialPassword` -> {option}`password` -> {option}`hashedPasswordFile`


If the option {option}`users.mutableUsers` is

{option}`initialHashedPassword` -> {option}`initialPassword` -> {option}`hashedPassword` -> {option}`password` -> {option}`hashedPasswordFile`

indirectly via {command}`su` or {command}`sudo`). This should only be used
for e.g. bootable live systems. Note: this is different from setting an
empty password, which can be achieved using
{option}`users.users.<name?>.password`.

If set to `null` (default) this user will not be able to log in using a
password (i.e. via {command}`login` command).

options.title: users.users.<name>.initialPassword
options.description:
Specifies the initial password for the user, i.e. the
password assigned if the user does not already exist. If
{option}`users.mutableUsers` is true, the password
can be changed subsequently using the
{command}`passwd` command. Otherwise, it's
equivalent to setting the {option}`password`
option. The same caveat applies: the password specified here
is world-readable in the Nix store, so it should only be
used for guest accounts or passwords that will be changed
promptly.

The {option}`initialHashedPassword`, {option}`hashedPassword`,
{option}`initialPassword`, {option}`password` and
{option}`hashedPasswordFile` options all control what password is set for
the user.

In a system where [](#opt-systemd.sysusers.enable) is `false`, typically
only one of {option}`hashedPassword`, {option}`password`, or
{option}`hashedPasswordFile` will be set.

In a system where [](#opt-systemd.sysusers.enable) or [](#opt-services.userborn.enable) is `true`,
typically only one of {option}`initialPassword`, {option}`initialHashedPassword`,
or {option}`hashedPasswordFile` will be set.

If the option {option}`users.mutableUsers` is true, the password defined
in one of the above password options will only be set when the user is
created for the first time. After that, you are free to change the
password with the ordinary user management commands. If
{option}`users.mutableUsers` is false, you cannot change user passwords,
they will always be set according to the password options.

If none of the password options are set, then no password is assigned to
the user, and the user will not be able to do password-based logins.

If multiple of these password options are set at the same time then a
specific order of precedence is followed, which can lead to surprising
results. The order of precedence differs depending on whether the
{option}`users.mutableUsers` option is set.


If the option {option}`users.mutableUsers` is
`false`, then the order of precedence is as shown
below, where values on the left are overridden by values on the right:
{option}`initialHashedPassword` -> {option}`hashedPassword` -> {option}`initialPassword` -> {option}`password` -> {option}`hashedPasswordFile`


If the option {option}`users.mutableUsers` is
`true`, then the order of precedence is as shown
below, where values on the left are overridden by values on the right:
{option}`initialHashedPassword` -> {option}`initialPassword` -> {option}`hashedPassword` -> {option}`password` -> {option}`hashedPasswordFile`

options.title: users.users.<name>.isNormalUser
options.description:
Indicates whether this is an account for a “real” user.
This automatically sets {option}`group` to `users`,
{option}`createHome` to `true`,
{option}`home` to {file}`/home/«username»`,
{option}`useDefaultShell` to `true`,
and {option}`isSystemUser` to `false`.
Exactly one of `isNormalUser` and `isSystemUser` must be true.

options.title: users.users.<name>.isSystemUser
options.description:
Indicates if the user is a system user or not. This option
only has an effect if {option}`uid` is
{option}`null`, in which case it determines whether
the user's UID is allocated in the range for system users
(below 1000) or in the range for normal users (starting at
1000).
Exactly one of `isNormalUser` and
`isSystemUser` must be true.

options.title: users.users.<name>.linger
options.description:
Whether to enable or disable lingering for this user.  Without
lingering, user units will not be started until the user logs in,
and may be stopped on logout depending on the settings in
`logind.conf`.

By default, NixOS will not manage lingering, new users will default
to not lingering, and lingering can be configured imperatively using
`loginctl enable-linger` or `loginctl disable-linger`. Setting
this option to `true` or `false` is the declarative equivalent of
running `loginctl enable-linger` or `loginctl disable-linger`
respectively.

options.title: users.users.<name>.name
options.type: string, not containing newlines or colons
options.description:
The name of the user account. If undefined, the name of the
attribute set will be used.

options.title: users.users.<name>.openssh.authorizedKeys.keyFiles
options.description:
A list of files each containing one OpenSSH public key that should be
added to the user's authorized keys. The contents of the files are
read at build time and added to a file that the SSH daemon reads in
addition to the the user's authorized_keys file. You can combine the
`keyFiles` and `keys` options.

options.title: users.users.<name>.openssh.authorizedKeys.keys
options.description:
A list of verbatim OpenSSH public keys that should be added to the
user's authorized keys. The keys are added to a file that the SSH
daemon reads in addition to the the user's authorized_keys file.
You can combine the `keys` and
`keyFiles` options.
Warning: If you are using `NixOps` then don't use this
option since it will replace the key required for deployment via ssh.

options.title: users.users.<name>.openssh.authorizedPrincipals
options.description:
A list of verbatim principal names that should be added to the user's
authorized principals.

options.title: users.users.<name>.packages
options.description:
The set of packages that should be made available to the user.
This is in contrast to {option}`environment.systemPackages`,
which adds packages to all users.

options.title: users.users.<name>.pamMount
options.description:
Attributes for user's entry in
{file}`pam_mount.conf.xml`.
Useful attributes might include `path`,
`options`, `fstype`, and `server`.
See <https://pam-mount.sourceforge.net/pam_mount.conf.5.html>
for more information.

options.title: users.users.<name>.password
options.description:
Specifies the (clear text) password for the user.
Warning: do not set confidential information here
because it is world-readable in the Nix store. This option
should only be used for public accounts.

The {option}`initialHashedPassword`, {option}`hashedPassword`,
{option}`initialPassword`, {option}`password` and
{option}`hashedPasswordFile` options all control what password is set for
the user.

In a system where [](#opt-systemd.sysusers.enable) is `false`, typically
only one of {option}`hashedPassword`, {option}`password`, or
{option}`hashedPasswordFile` will be set.

In a system where [](#opt-systemd.sysusers.enable) or [](#opt-services.userborn.enable) is `true`,
typically only one of {option}`initialPassword`, {option}`initialHashedPassword`,
or {option}`hashedPasswordFile` will be set.

If the option {option}`users.mutableUsers` is true, the password defined
in one of the above password options will only be set when the user is
created for the first time. After that, you are free to change the
password with the ordinary user management commands. If
{option}`users.mutableUsers` is false, you cannot change user passwords,
they will always be set according to the password options.

If none of the password options are set, then no password is assigned to
the user, and the user will not be able to do password-based logins.

If multiple of these password options are set at the same time then a
specific order of precedence is followed, which can lead to surprising
results. The order of precedence differs depending on whether the
{option}`users.mutableUsers` option is set.


If the option {option}`users.mutableUsers` is
`false`, then the order of precedence is as shown
below, where values on the left are overridden by values on the right:
{option}`initialHashedPassword` -> {option}`hashedPassword` -> {option}`initialPassword` -> {option}`password` -> {option}`hashedPasswordFile`


If the option {option}`users.mutableUsers` is
`true`, then the order of precedence is as shown
below, where values on the left are overridden by values on the right:
{option}`initialHashedPassword` -> {option}`initialPassword` -> {option}`hashedPassword` -> {option}`password` -> {option}`hashedPasswordFile`

options.title: users.users.<name>.shell
options.type: null or package or (absolute path, not containing newlines or colons)
options.description:
The path to the user's shell. Can use shell derivations,
like `pkgs.bashInteractive`. Don’t
forget to enable your shell in
`programs` if necessary,
like `programs.zsh.enable = true;`.

options.title: users.users.<name>.subGidRanges

options.title: users.users.<name>.subGidRanges.*.count
options.description: Count of subordinate group ids

options.title: users.users.<name>.subGidRanges.*.startGid
options.description:
Start of the range of subordinate group ids that user is

options.title: users.users.<name>.subUidRanges
options.description:
Subordinate user ids that user is allowed to use.
They are set into {file}`/etc/subuid` and are used
by `newuidmap` for user namespaces.

options.title: users.users.<name>.subUidRanges.*.count
options.description: Count of subordinate user ids

options.title: users.users.<name>.subUidRanges.*.startUid
options.description:
Start of the range of subordinate user ids that user is
allowed to use.

options.title: users.users.<name>.uid
options.description:
The account UID. If the UID is null, a free UID is picked on
activation.

options.title: users.users.<name>.useDefaultShell
options.description:
If true, the user's shell will be set to
{option}`users.defaultUserShell`.

options.title: virtualisation.docker.autoPrune.dates
options.description:
Specification (in the format described by
{manpage}`systemd.time(7)`) of the time at
which the prune will occur.

options.title: virtualisation.docker.autoPrune.enable
options.description:
Whether to periodically prune Docker resources. If enabled, a
systemd timer will run `docker system prune -f`
as specified by the `dates` option.

options.title: virtualisation.docker.autoPrune.flags
options.description: Any additional flags passed to {command}`docker system prune`.

options.title: virtualisation.docker.autoPrune.persistent
options.description:
Takes a boolean argument. If true, the time when the service
unit was last triggered is stored on disk. When the timer is
activated, the service unit is triggered immediately if it
would have been triggered at least once during the time when
the timer was inactive. Such triggering is nonetheless
subject to the delay imposed by RandomizedDelaySec=. This is
useful to catch up on missed runs of the service when the
system was powered down.

options.title: virtualisation.docker.autoPrune.randomizedDelaySec
options.description:
Add a randomized delay before each auto prune.
The delay will be chosen between zero and this value.
This value must be a time span in the format specified by
{manpage}`systemd.time(7)`

options.title: virtualisation.docker.daemon.settings
options.description:
Configuration for docker daemon. The attributes are serialized to JSON used as daemon.conf.
See <https://docs.docker.com/engine/reference/commandline/dockerd/#daemon-configuration-file>

options.title: virtualisation.docker.daemon.settings.live-restore
options.description:
Allow dockerd to be restarted without affecting running container.
This option is incompatible with docker swarm.

options.title: virtualisation.docker.enable
options.description:
This option enables docker, a daemon that manages
linux containers. Users in the "docker" group can interact with
the daemon (e.g. to start or stop containers) using the
{command}`docker` command line tool.

options.title: virtualisation.docker.enableNvidia
options.description:
**Deprecated**, please use hardware.nvidia-container-toolkit.enable instead.

Enable Nvidia GPU support inside docker containers.

options.title: virtualisation.docker.enableOnBoot
options.description:
When enabled dockerd is started on boot. This is required for
containers which are created with the
`--restart=always` flag to work. If this option is
disabled, docker might be started on demand by socket activation.

options.title: virtualisation.docker.extraOptions
options.description:
The extra command-line options to pass to
{command}`docker` daemon.

options.title: virtualisation.docker.extraPackages
options.description: Extra packages to add to PATH for the docker daemon process.

options.title: virtualisation.docker.listenOptions
options.description:
A list of unix and tcp docker should listen to. The format follows
ListenStream as described in {manpage}`systemd.socket(5)`.

options.title: virtualisation.docker.liveRestore
options.description: Alias of {option}`virtualisation.docker.daemon.settings.live-restore`.

options.title: virtualisation.docker.logDriver
options.description: This option determines which Docker log driver to use.

options.title: virtualisation.docker.package
options.description: The docker package to use.

options.title: virtualisation.docker.rootless.daemon.settings
options.description:
Configuration for docker daemon. The attributes are serialized to JSON used as daemon.conf.
See <https://docs.docker.com/engine/reference/commandline/dockerd/#daemon-configuration-file>

options.title: virtualisation.docker.rootless.enable
options.description:
This option enables docker in a rootless mode, a daemon that manages
linux containers. To interact with the daemon, one needs to set
{command}`DOCKER_HOST=unix://$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/docker.sock`.

options.title: virtualisation.docker.rootless.extraPackages
options.description: Extra packages to add to PATH for the docker daemon process.

options.title: virtualisation.docker.rootless.package
options.description: The docker package to use.

options.title: virtualisation.docker.rootless.setSocketVariable
options.description:
Point {command}`DOCKER_HOST` to rootless Docker instance for
normal users by default.

options.title: virtualisation.docker.storageDriver
options.description:
This option determines which Docker
[storage driver](https://docs.docker.com/storage/storagedriver/select-storage-driver/)
to use.
By default it lets docker automatically choose the preferred storage
driver.
However, it is recommended to specify a storage driver explicitly, as
docker's default varies over versions.

::: {.warning}
Changing the storage driver will cause any existing containers
and images to become inaccessible.
:::

options.title: virtualisation.hypervGuest.enable
options.description: Whether to enable Hyper-V Guest Support.

options.title: virtualisation.incus.agent.enable
options.description: Whether to enable Incus agent.

options.title: virtualisation.incus.clientPackage
options.description: The incus client package to use. This package is added to PATH.

options.title: virtualisation.incus.enable
options.description:
Whether to enable incusd, a daemon that manages containers and virtual machines.

Users in the "incus-admin" group can interact with
the daemon (e.g. to start or stop containers) using the
{command}`incus` command line tool, among others.
Users in the "incus" group can also interact with
the daemon, but with lower permissions
(i.e. administrative operations are forbidden).
.

options.title: virtualisation.incus.lxcPackage
options.description: The lxc package to use.

options.title: virtualisation.incus.package
options.description: The incus-lts package to use.

options.title: virtualisation.incus.preseed
options.description:
Configuration for Incus preseed, see
<https://linuxcontainers.org/incus/docs/main/howto/initialize/#non-interactive-configuration>
for supported values.

Changes to this will be re-applied to Incus which will overwrite existing entities or create missing ones,
but entities will *not* be removed by preseed.

options.title: virtualisation.incus.socketActivation
options.description:
Whether to enable socket-activation for starting incus.service. Enabling this option
will stop incus.service from starting automatically on boot.
.

options.title: virtualisation.incus.softDaemonRestart
options.description: Allow for incus.service to be stopped without affecting running instances.

options.title: virtualisation.incus.startTimeout
options.description:
Time to wait (in seconds) for incusd to become ready to process requests.
If incusd does not reply within the configured time, `incus.service` will be
considered failed and systemd will attempt to restart it.

options.title: virtualisation.incus.ui.enable
options.description: Whether to enable Incus Web UI.

options.title: virtualisation.incus.ui.package
options.description: The incus-ui-canonical package to use.

options.title: virtualisation.incus.useACMEHost
options.description:
Host of an existing Let's Encrypt certificate to use for TLS.
*Note that this option does not create any certificates and it
doesn't add subdomains to existing ones – you will need to create
them manually using {option}`security.acme.certs`.*

options.title: virtualisation.kvmgt.device
options.description: PCI ID of graphics card. You can figure it with {command}`ls /sys/class/mdev_bus`.

options.title: virtualisation.kvmgt.enable
options.description:
Whether to enable KVMGT (iGVT-g) VGPU support. Allows Qemu/KVM guests to share host's Intel integrated graphics card.
Currently only one graphical device can be shared. To allow users to access the device without root add them
to the kvm group: `users.extraUsers.<yourusername>.extraGroups = [ "kvm" ];`
.

options.title: virtualisation.kvmgt.vgpus
options.description:
Virtual GPUs to be used in Qemu. You can find devices via {command}`ls /sys/bus/pci/devices/*/mdev_supported_types`
and find info about device via {command}`cat /sys/bus/pci/devices/*/mdev_supported_types/i915-GVTg_V5_4/description`

options.title: virtualisation.kvmgt.vgpus.<name>.uuid

options.title: virtualisation.libvirtd.nss
options.description: libvirt NSS module options.

options.title: virtualisation.libvirtd.nss.enable
options.description:
This option enables the older libvirt NSS module. This method uses
DHCP server records, therefore is dependent on the hostname provided
by the guest.
Please see <https://libvirt.org/nss.html> for more information.

options.title: virtualisation.libvirtd.nss.enableGuest
options.description:
This option enables the newer libvirt_guest NSS module. This module
uses the libvirt guest name instead of the hostname of the guest.
Please see <https://libvirt.org/nss.html> for more information.

options.title: virtualisation.libvirtd.onBoot
options.description:
Specifies the action to be done to / on the guests when the host boots.
The "start" option starts all guests that were running prior to shutdown
regardless of their autostart settings. The "ignore" option will not
start the formerly running guest on boot. However, any guest marked as
autostart will still be automatically started by libvirtd.

options.title: virtualisation.libvirtd.onShutdown
options.description:
When shutting down / restarting the host what method should
be used to gracefully halt the guests. Setting to "shutdown"
will cause an ACPI shutdown of each guest. "suspend" will
attempt to save the state of the guests ready to restore on boot.

options.title: virtualisation.libvirtd.package
options.description: The libvirt package to use.

options.title: virtualisation.libvirtd.parallelShutdown
options.description:
Number of guests that will be shutdown concurrently, taking effect when onShutdown
is set to "shutdown". If set to 0, guests will be shutdown one after another.
Number of guests on shutdown at any time will not exceed number set in this
variable.

options.title: virtualisation.libvirtd.qemu

`pkgs.qemu_kvm` saves disk space allowing to emulate only host architectures.

If false, libvirtd runs qemu as unprivileged user qemu-libvirtd.

administration access in LXC. See {manpage}`lxc-usernet(5)`.

options.title: virtualisation.oci-containers.backend
options.description: The underlying Docker implementation to use.

options.title: virtualisation.oci-containers.containers
options.description: OCI (Docker) containers to run as systemd services.

options.title: virtualisation.oci-containers.containers.<name>.autoRemoveOnStop
options.description: Automatically remove the container when it is stopped or killed

options.title: virtualisation.oci-containers.containers.<name>.autoStart

When enabled, the container is automatically started on boot.
If this option is set to false, the container has to be started on-demand via its service.

options.title: virtualisation.oci-containers.containers.<name>.capabilities
options.type: lazy attribute set of (null or boolean)
options.description:
Capabilities to configure for the container.
When set to true, capability is added to the container.
When set to false, capability is dropped from the container.
When null, default runtime settings apply.

options.title: virtualisation.oci-containers.containers.<name>.cmd
options.description: Commandline arguments to pass to the image's entrypoint.

options.title: virtualisation.oci-containers.containers.<name>.dependsOn
options.description:
Define which other containers this one depends on. They will be added to both After and Requires for the unit.

Use the same name as the attribute under `virtualisation.oci-containers.containers`.

options.title: virtualisation.oci-containers.containers.<name>.devices
options.description: List of devices to attach to this container.

options.title: virtualisation.oci-containers.containers.<name>.entrypoint
options.description: Override the default entrypoint of the image.

options.title: virtualisation.oci-containers.containers.<name>.environment
options.description: Environment variables to set for this container.

options.title: virtualisation.oci-containers.containers.<name>.environmentFiles
options.description: Environment files for this container.

options.title: virtualisation.oci-containers.containers.<name>.extraOptions
options.description: Extra options for {command}`podman run`.

options.title: virtualisation.oci-containers.containers.<name>.hostname
options.description: The hostname of the container.

options.title: virtualisation.oci-containers.containers.<name>.image
options.description: OCI image to run.

options.title: virtualisation.oci-containers.containers.<name>.imageFile
options.description:
Path to an image file to load before running the image. This can
be used to bypass pulling the image from the registry.

The `image` attribute must match the name and
tag of the image contained in this file, as they will be used to
run the container with that image. If they do not match, the
image will be pulled from the registry as usual.

options.title: virtualisation.oci-containers.containers.<name>.imageStream
options.description:
Path to a script that streams the desired image on standard output.

This option is mainly intended for use with
`pkgs.dockerTools.streamLayeredImage` so that the intermediate
image archive does not need to be stored in the Nix store.  For
larger images this optimization can significantly reduce Nix store
churn compared to using the `imageFile` option, because you don't
have to store a new copy of the image archive in the Nix store
every time you change the image.  Instead, if you stream the image
then you only need to build and store the layers that differ from
the previous image.

options.title: virtualisation.oci-containers.containers.<name>.labels
options.description: Labels to attach to the container at runtime.

options.title: virtualisation.oci-containers.containers.<name>.log-driver
options.description:
Logging driver for the container.  The default of
`"journald"` means that the container's logs will be
handled as part of the systemd unit.

For more details and a full list of logging drivers, refer to respective backends documentation.

For Docker:
[Docker engine documentation](https://docs.docker.com/engine/logging/configure/)

For Podman:
Refer to the {manpage}`docker-run(1)` man page.

options.title: virtualisation.oci-containers.containers.<name>.login.passwordFile
options.description: Path to file containing password.

options.title: virtualisation.oci-containers.containers.<name>.login.registry
options.description: Registry where to login to.

options.title: virtualisation.oci-containers.containers.<name>.login.username
options.description: Username for login.

options.title: virtualisation.oci-containers.containers.<name>.networks
options.description: Networks to attach the container to

options.title: virtualisation.oci-containers.containers.<name>.podman
options.description:
Podman-specific settings in OCI containers. These must be null when using
the `docker` backend.

options.title: virtualisation.oci-containers.containers.<name>.podman.sdnotify
options.description:
Determines how `podman` should notify systemd that the unit is ready. There are
[three options](https://docs.podman.io/en/latest/markdown/podman-run.1.html#sdnotify-container-conmon-healthy-ignore):

* `conmon`: marks the unit as ready when the container has started.
* `healthy`: marks the unit as ready when the [container's healthcheck](https://docs.podman.io/en/stable/markdown/podman-healthcheck-run.1.html) passes.
* `container`: `NOTIFY_SOCKET` is passed into the container and the process inside the container needs to indicate on its own that it's ready.

options.title: virtualisation.oci-containers.containers.<name>.podman.user
options.description: The user under which the container should run.

options.title: virtualisation.oci-containers.containers.<name>.ports
options.description:
Network ports to publish from the container to the outer host.

Valid formats:
- `<ip>:<hostPort>:<containerPort>`
- `<ip>::<containerPort>`
- `<hostPort>:<containerPort>`
- `<containerPort>`

Both `hostPort` and `containerPort` can be specified as a range of
ports.  When specifying ranges for both, the number of container
ports in the range must match the number of host ports in the
range.  Example: `1234-1236:1234-1236/tcp`

When specifying a range for `hostPort` only, the `containerPort`
must *not* be a range.  In this case, the container port is published
somewhere within the specified `hostPort` range.
Example: `1234-1236:1234/tcp`

Publishing a port bypasses the NixOS firewall. If the port is not
supposed to be shared on the network, make sure to publish the
port to localhost.
Example: `127.0.0.1:1234:1234`

Refer to the
[Docker engine documentation](https://docs.docker.com/engine/network/#published-ports) for full details.

options.title: virtualisation.oci-containers.containers.<name>.preRunExtraOptions
options.description: Extra options for {command}`podman` that go before the `run` argument.

options.title: virtualisation.oci-containers.containers.<name>.privileged
options.description: Give extended privileges to the container

options.title: virtualisation.oci-containers.containers.<name>.pull
options.description: Image pull policy for the container. Must be one of: always, missing, never, newer

options.title: virtualisation.oci-containers.containers.<name>.serviceName
options.description: Systemd service name that manages the container

options.title: virtualisation.oci-containers.containers.<name>.user
options.description:
Override the username or UID (and optionally groupname or GID) used
in the container.

options.title: virtualisation.oci-containers.containers.<name>.volumes
options.description:
List of volumes to attach to this container.

Note that this is a list of `"src:dst"` strings to
allow for `src` to refer to `/nix/store` paths, which
would be difficult with an attribute set.  There are
also a variety of mount options available as a third
field; please refer to the
[docker engine documentation](https://docs.docker.com/engine/storage/volumes/) for details.

options.title: virtualisation.oci-containers.containers.<name>.workdir
options.description: Override the default working directory for the container.

options.title: virtualisation.podman.autoPrune.dates
options.description:
Specification (in the format described by
{manpage}`systemd.time(7)`) of the time at
which the prune will occur.

options.title: virtualisation.podman.autoPrune.enable
options.description:
Whether to periodically prune Podman resources. If enabled, a
systemd timer will run `podman system prune -f`
as specified by the `dates` option.

options.title: virtualisation.podman.autoPrune.flags
options.description: Any additional flags passed to {command}`podman system prune`.

options.title: virtualisation.podman.defaultNetwork.settings
options.description: Settings for podman's default network.

options.title: virtualisation.podman.dockerCompat
options.description: Create an alias mapping {command}`docker` to {command}`podman`.

options.title: virtualisation.podman.dockerSocket.enable
options.description:
Make the Podman socket available in place of the Docker socket, so
Docker tools can find the Podman socket.

Podman implements the Docker API.

Users must be in the `podman` group in order to connect. As
with Docker, members of this group can gain root access.

options.title: virtualisation.podman.enable
options.description:
This option enables Podman, a daemonless container engine for
developing, managing, and running OCI Containers on your Linux System.

It is a drop-in replacement for the {command}`docker` command.

options.title: virtualisation.podman.enableNvidia
options.description:
**Deprecated**, please use hardware.nvidia-container-toolkit.enable instead.

Enable use of Nvidia GPUs from within podman containers.

options.title: virtualisation.podman.extraPackages
options.description: Extra dependencies for podman to be placed on $PATH in the wrapper.

options.title: virtualisation.podman.extraRuntimes
options.description:
Extra runtime packages to be installed in the Podman wrapper.
Those are then placed in libexec/podman, i.e. are seen as podman internal commands.

options.title: virtualisation.podman.networkSocket.enable
options.description:
Make the Podman and Docker compatibility API available over the network
with TLS client certificate authentication.

This allows Docker clients to connect with the equivalents of the Docker
CLI `-H` and `--tls*` family of options.

For certificate setup, see <https://docs.docker.com/engine/security/protect-access/>

This option is independent of [](#opt-virtualisation.podman.dockerSocket.enable).

Path to the private key corresponding to the server certificate.

Use a string for this setting. Otherwise it will be copied to the Nix

options.title: virtualisation.podman.package
options.description: The podman package to use. This package will automatically include extra packages and runtimes.

options.title: virtualisation.rosetta.enable
options.description:
Whether to enable [Rosetta](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/apple-silicon/about-the-rosetta-translation-environment) support.

This feature requires the system to be a virtualised guest on an Apple silicon host.

The default settings are suitable for the [UTM](https://docs.getutm.app/) virtualisation [package](https://search.nixos.org/packages?channel=unstable&show=utm&from=0&size=1&sort=relevance&type=packages&query=utm).
Make sure to select 'Apple Virtualization' as the virtualisation engine and then tick the 'Enable Rosetta' option.

options.title: virtualisation.rosetta.mountTag
options.description:
The VirtioFS mount tag for the Rosetta runtime, exposed by the host's virtualisation software.

If supported, your virtualisation software should provide instructions on how register the Rosetta runtime inside Linux guests.
These instructions should mention the name of the mount tag used for the VirtioFS directory share that contains the Rosetta runtime.

options.title: virtualisation.spiceUSBRedirection.enable
options.description:
Install the SPICE USB redirection helper with setuid
privileges. This allows unprivileged users to pass USB devices
connected to this machine to libvirt VMs, both local and
remote. Note that this allows users arbitrary access to USB
devices.

Whether to enable VirtualBox.

In order to pass USB devices from the host to the guests, the user

options.title: virtualisation.virtualbox.host.enableHardening

Enable hardened VirtualBox, which ensures that only the binaries in the

options.title: virtualisation.virtualbox.host.enableKvm

Enable KVM support for VirtualBox. This increases compatibility with Linux kernel versions, because the VirtualBox kernel modules

options.title: virtualisation.xen.boot.bios.path
options.description:
Path to the Xen `multiboot` binary used for BIOS booting.
Unless you're building your own Xen derivation, you should leave this
option as the default value.

options.title: virtualisation.xen.boot.builderVerbosity
options.description:
The boot entry builder script should be called with exactly one of the following arguments in order to specify its verbosity:

- `quiet` supresses all messages.

- `default` adds a simple "Installing Xen Project Hypervisor boot entries...done." message to the script.

- `info` is the same as `default`, but it also prints a diff with information on which generations were altered.
  - This option adds two extra dependencies to the script: `diffutils` and `bat`.

- `debug` prints information messages for every single step of the script.

This option does not alter the actual functionality of the script, just the number of messages printed when rebuilding the system.

options.title: virtualisation.xen.boot.efi.path
options.description:
Path to xen.efi. `pkgs.xen` is patched to install the xen.efi file
on `$boot/boot/xen.efi`, but an unpatched Xen build may install it
somewhere else, such as `$out/boot/efi/efi/nixos/xen.efi`. Unless
you're building your own Xen derivation, you should leave this
option as the default value.

options.title: virtualisation.xen.boot.params
options.description:
Xen Command Line parameters passed to Domain 0 at boot time.
Note: these are different from `boot.kernelParams`. See
the [Xen documentation](https://xenbits.xenproject.org/docs/unstable/misc/xen-command-line.html) for more information.

options.title: virtualisation.xen.debug
options.description: Whether to enable Xen debug features for Domain 0. This option enables some hidden debugging tests and features, and should not be used in production.

options.title: virtualisation.xen.dom0Resources.maxMemory
options.description:
Maximum amount of memory (in MiB) that Domain 0 can
dynamically allocate to itself. Does nothing if set
to the same amount as virtualisation.xen.memory, or
if that option is set to 0.

options.title: virtualisation.xen.dom0Resources.maxVCPUs
options.description:
Amount of virtual CPU cores allocated to Domain 0 on boot.
If set to 0, all cores are assigned to Domain 0, and
unprivileged domains will compete with Domain 0 for CPU time.

options.title: virtualisation.xen.dom0Resources.memory
options.description:
Amount of memory (in MiB) allocated to Domain 0 on boot.
If set to 0, all memory is assigned to Domain 0, and
unprivileged domains will compete with Domain 0 for free RAM.

options.title: virtualisation.xen.domains.extraConfig
options.description:
Options defined here will override the defaults for xendomains.
The default options can be seen in the file included from
/etc/default/xendomains.

options.title: virtualisation.xen.enable
options.description: Whether to enable the Xen Project Hypervisor, a virtualisation technology defined as a *type-1 hypervisor*, which allows multiple virtual machines, known as *domains*, to run concurrently on the physical machine. NixOS runs as the privileged *Domain 0*. This option requires a reboot into a Xen kernel to take effect.

options.title: virtualisation.xen.package
options.description: The Xen Hypervisor package to use.

options.title: virtualisation.xen.qemu.package
options.description: The QEMU (with Xen Hypervisor support) package to use.

options.title: virtualisation.xen.qemu.pidFile
options.description: Path to the QEMU PID file.

options.title: virtualisation.xen.store.path
options.description:
Path to the Xen Store Daemon. This option is useful to
switch between the legacy C-based Xen Store Daemon, and
the newer OCaml-based Xen Store Daemon, `oxenstored`.

options.title: virtualisation.xen.store.settings
options.description:
The OCaml-based Xen Store Daemon configuration. This
option does nothing with the C-based `xenstored`.

options.title: virtualisation.xen.store.settings.conflict.burstLimit
options.description:
Limits applied to domains whose writes cause other domains' transaction
commits to fail. Must include decimal point.

The burst limit is the number of conflicts a domain can cause to
fail in a short period; this value is used for both the initial and
the maximum value of each domain's conflict-credit, which falls by
one point for each conflict caused, and when it reaches zero the
domain's requests are ignored.

options.title: virtualisation.xen.store.settings.conflict.maxHistorySeconds
options.description:
Limits applied to domains whose writes cause other domains' transaction
commits to fail. Must include decimal point.

The conflict-credit is replenished over time:
one point is issued after each conflict.maxHistorySeconds, so this
is the minimum pause-time during which a domain will be ignored.

options.title: virtualisation.xen.store.settings.conflict.rateLimitIsAggregate
options.description:
If the conflict.rateLimitIsAggregate option is `true`, then after each
tick one point of conflict-credit is given to just one domain: the
one at the front of the queue. If `false`, then after each tick each
domain gets a point of conflict-credit.

In environments where it is known that every transaction will
involve a set of nodes that is writable by at most one other domain,
then it is safe to set this aggregate limit flag to `false` for better
performance. (This can be determined by considering the layout of
the xenstore tree and permissions, together with the content of the
transactions that require protection.)

A transaction which involves a set of nodes which can be modified by
multiple other domains can suffer conflicts caused by any of those
domains, so the flag must be set to `true`.

options.title: virtualisation.xen.store.settings.enableMerge
options.description: Whether to enable transaction merge support.

options.title: virtualisation.xen.store.settings.perms.enable
options.description: Whether to enable the node permission system.

options.title: virtualisation.xen.store.settings.perms.enableWatch
options.description:
Whether to enable the watch permission system.

When this is set to `true`, unprivileged guests can only get watch events
for xenstore entries that they would've been able to read.

When this is set to `false`, unprivileged guests may get watch events
for xenstore entries that they cannot read. The watch event contains
only the entry name, not the value.
This restores behaviour prior to [XSA-115](https://xenbits.xenproject.org/xsa/advisory-115.html).

options.title: virtualisation.xen.store.settings.persistent
options.description: Whether to activate the filed base backend.

options.title: virtualisation.xen.store.settings.pidFile
options.description: Path to the Xen Store Daemon PID file.

options.title: virtualisation.xen.store.settings.quota.enable
options.description: Whether to enable the quota system.

options.title: virtualisation.xen.store.settings.quota.maxEntity

options.title: virtualisation.xen.store.settings.quota.maxOutstanding
options.description: Maximum outstanding requests, i.e. in-flight requests / domain.

options.title: virtualisation.xen.store.settings.quota.maxPath
options.description: Path limit for the quota system.

options.title: virtualisation.xen.store.settings.quota.maxRequests
options.description: Maximum number of requests per transaction.

options.title: virtualisation.xen.store.settings.quota.maxSize
options.description: Size limit for transactions.

options.title: virtualisation.xen.store.settings.quota.maxWatch
options.description: Maximum number of watches by the Xenstore Watchdog.

options.title: virtualisation.xen.store.settings.quota.maxWatchEvents
options.description: Maximum number of outstanding watch events per watch.

options.title: virtualisation.xen.store.settings.quota.transaction

options.title: virtualisation.xen.store.settings.ringScanInterval

Perodic scanning for all the rings as a safenet for lazy clients.
Define the interval in seconds; set to a negative integer to disable.

options.title: virtualisation.xen.store.settings.xenstored.accessLog.file

options.title: virtualisation.xen.store.settings.xenstored.log.file

options.title: virtualisation.xen.store.settings.xenstored.log.level

Whether to install files to support the

Removes associations between mimetypes and applications. See the
